A decomposition according to the two diagonal directions reduces the enumeration to convex polyominoes satisfying a one-bend condition in one diagonal direction. Splitting these polyominoes at the right endpoint of the top row leaves an initial part followed by columns whose vertical intervals decrease by inclusion. Ordered forests describe the initial part and retain the row information needed to determine when column extensions first exceed the prescribed bound. A first-passage calculation, together with a sum over initial parts already above the bound, gives the required generating function. The argument includes the case $k=2$.
Functoriality probes over number fields by mixed zero correlations

We use an automorphic L-function over one number field as a probe for the functorial structure of another automorphic L-function over a possibly different field. No automorphic induction is assumed. We first determine the mixed Euler factors arising from the explicit formula, including the residue-degree multiplicities that occur when local traces are grouped by absolute norm. This local analysis gives four probe constructions. Rational-field probes with known base change detect constituent multiplicities and, in equal rank, exact Satake equalities. Probes over a common Galois field detect conjugacy and stabilizers. Dirichlet-character probes give congruence-weighted combinations of Satake traces even when the leading overlap vanishes. A tensor-product construction realizes general different-field probes whenever the required base changes exist. We then separate the pair calculation from the higher connected calculations and work out the cubic and quartic arithmetic explicitly. In an explicit small Fourier box these expressions yield all finite secondary orders of the centered statistics; the required pair prime number theorems also give raw and distinct-index correlations. The main analytic tools are an independent fixed-data proof of Hypothesis H over number fields, a positive-margin estimate for rationally grouped coefficients, and the theorem of Harcos-Thorner for the realized Rankin-Selberg factors. This expanded version includes the full computations, local examples, and an appendix explaining the character-extension issue avoided by the proof of Hypothesis H. The resulting probes give concrete tests of functorial relationships, while recovery of automorphic induction remains a longer-term goal.
Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models

Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.
Asymptotic behavior of some strongly critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson processes with immigration

We study the asymptotic behavior of a critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson process with immigration whose offspring mean matrix is triangular with diagonal entries 1. Under second-order moment conditions on the offspring and immigration distributions, we establish a functional limit theorem for the sequence of appropriately scaled processes, and describe the limit process as independent squared Bessel processes and some linear combinations of their iterated integral processes. Our work completes and extends some results of Foster and Ney (1978) for some strongly critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson processes with immigration.
The local-to-global minimum problem of Calvert and Vamanamurthy: a quartic counterexample in three variables and the cubic case in all dimensions

In 1980 Calvert and Vamanamurthy asked whether a polynomial whose only critical point is a local minimum must attain its global minimum there. They gave counterexamples of every degree at least five in two or more variables and settled cubics in two and three variables and quartics in two variables, leaving open quartics in three or more variables and cubics in four or more variables. We resolve both remaining cases. First, we give an explicit quartic in three variables whose unique critical point is a nondegenerate strict local minimum, although the polynomial is unbounded below; the example extends to every dimension at least three, and its critical locus is a single point even over the complex numbers. Second, we prove that in every dimension a polynomial of exact degree three with a local minimum has another critical point, so that the cubic case holds vacuously; the proof is elementary and avoids the topological degree arguments used previously in two and three variables. Together with the results of Calvert and Vamanamurthy, this gives the complete classification of the local-to-global property by degree and dimension.
Extremal zero-sum sequences without elements of maximal order

Let $\mathsf D(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of a finite abelian group $G$, the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $G$. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured that every minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)$~\cite[Conjecture~6.1]{GG99} and every zero-sumfree sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)-1$~\cite[Conjecture~4.1]{GG06} contains an element of order $\exp(G)$. We disprove both conjectures by proving a density-one theorem: for every fixed finite abelian group $H$ of exponent $M=2^ap^b$, where $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, and $p$ is an odd prime, the set of integers $r\ge0$ for which $G_r=C_2^r\oplus H$ admits a minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G_r)$ with no term of order $M$ has natural density one.
Generalized Ricci Solitons on Heisenberg and Oscillator Algebras
Vicente Cortés; Shubham Dwivedi; Lorenz Jetter

We prove that on a connected, simply-connected nilpotent Lie group, the notions of left-invariant generalized Ricci soliton, semi-algebraic and algebraic generalized Ricci soliton coincide. Moreover, every such soliton has harmonic torsion. We classify all algebraic solitons with positive definite metric on the five-dimensional Heisenberg algebra, the four-dimensional oscillator algebra and the four-dimensional split-oscillator algebra up to automorphisms and rescalings. We find that there is only a finite number of algebraic solitons, all of which have harmonic torsion.
Tensor Products and the Isomorphic Theory of Daugavet Spaces

We construct two separable Banach spaces with the Daugavet property whose injective and projective tensor squares, respectively, fail the Daugavet property. Both examples arise from one sequence of finite-dimensional extensions. The first space is the completion of the increasing union of the extensions, whereas the second is the closed span of their coordinate functionals. We will also investigate the operator Daugavet properties of these spaces later in the paper, also highlighting natural examples of metric spaces \(M\) for which \(\operatorname{Lip}_0(M)\) has the Daugavet property but fails to have the weak operator Daugavet property. Independently of this, we will also prove that every Banach space admits a linear isometric embedding into a Banach space which is not isomorphic to any Banach space with the Daugavet property.
Adaptive Preference Elicitation in Preference Robust CPT-Based Shortfall
Sainan Zhang; Erick Delage; Huifu Xu

This paper investigates the cumulative prospect theory (CPT)-based shortfall risk measure where the value (utility) function and the distortion (probability weighting) functions are ambiguous. We propose a worst-case CPT-based shortfall risk measure where the capital requirement is based on the worst-case value function and distortion functions from an ambiguity set constructed with user-specific information (e.g., preference between risky and certain lotteries) and well-known general information such as the S-shape of the value functions. When the underlying random loss is discretely distributed and parameters in pairs of lotteries remain undetermined, we demonstrate that the worst-case value function and the distortion functions have a piecewise linear structure. Based on this observation, we develop an adaptive preference elicitation approach extended from the well-known polyhedral method to simultaneously elicit the distortion functions and the positive and negative parts of the value function by solving a sequence of mixed-integer linear programs. Based on the elicited distortions, we design new queries to construct a feasible set of the holistic value functions. The proposed framework iteratively shrinks the ambiguity set through designed queries, yielding a computationally implementable robust CPT-based shortfall risk measure. To examine the in-sample and out-of-sample performance of the elicited CPT-based preference functions and the resulting preference robust shortfall risk measure, we conduct numerical experiments under an S-shaped value function and inverse S-shaped distortion functions and report the corresponding results.
Probing automorphic induction through zero correlations and secondary arithmetic terms

Zero correlations offer a way to test the cuspidal structure of an automorphic L-function, but their leading self statistics retain only coarse degree and multiplicity data. We therefore adjoin a specified cuspidal L-function as a probe and study the resulting raw mixed correlations. Assuming a factorization into cuspidal L-functions over Q, we show that a mixed pair statistic detects the probe's occurrence and recovers its multiplicity. A suitable Gevrey-order-two test eliminates the smooth-density terms and gives a subexponential error. For arbitrary smooth plateau tests, the prime number theorem of Harcos and Thorner gives an error smaller than every fixed inverse power of log T, without a self-contragredience assumption. The stronger prime number theorem of Liu and Ye gives a subexponential remainder under its stated structural assumptions, with the possible norm-twist terms made explicit. To obtain arithmetic information beyond this overlap, we compute the correlation expansion at every fixed level and inverse-logarithmic order within the original strict small-support range. We treat the pair and higher correlations separately, using Jiang's rational-field fixed-data estimates to justify the required prime-power convergence. The pair calculation identifies the mixed arithmetic finite parts and gives detailed error estimates, including the contribution of norm twists. The higher-level calculation retains connected prime-power invariants, whose first cubic contribution appears at order (log T)^{-3}. Explicit third- and fourth-level formulas and examples explain the arithmetic content of these coefficients and the limitations of self-correlations. Varying powers of the probe separates their mixed components. These formulas, together with the distinct-index sieve, provide a collection of arithmetic probe responses toward the further problem of recovering automorphic induction structure.
Rare Event Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Large Deviations

We study finite-horizon reinforcement learning with a safety constraint on the probability of reaching a failure set. In contrast to the well-studied safe reinforcement learning literature, we consider problems where the probability of reaching the failure set is vanishingly small, but the consequences of reaching the failure set are catastrophic. Direct simulation and estimation of the optimal policy is naturally ineffective when the failure probability is extremely small. Moreover, on a real system the controller can only choose actions, and this is not enough to make failures frequent. In contrast to the rare event simulation literature, our goal is not to estimate the probability of the rare event occurrence, but to upper bound it such that the failure constraint is satisfied. Thus, instead of sampling failures, we use the large deviations principle. We define a damage variable that on exceeding a certain threshold indicates failure. We study the cumulant generating function (CGF) as its positive root provides an upper bound on the failure probability via Cramer's theorem. We extend this approach to Markov decision processes with hitting times through state-action CGFs, and give finite-horizon and state-dependent versions of the bound. The state-action CGFs do not depend on the policy and can be estimated from regular transitions, so the bound can be checked for any policy a priori. This gives a policy improvement algorithm in which every policy satisfies the failure constraint with high probability.
A Korselt Characterization of Carmichael Numbers of the Form $(aC_n+1)(aC_{n+1}+1)(aC_{n+2}+1)$

We study products \[ N=(aC_n+1)(aC_{n+1}+1)(aC_{n+2}+1), \] where $(C_n)$ is the Lucas--balancing sequence. Under the assumption that all three factors are prime, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for $N$ to be a Carmichael number: this happens precisely when $n$ is even and $a=kC_{n+1}$ for a positive integer $k$ satisfying \[ 48k\equiv 7\pmod{C_nC_{n+2}}. \] We derive further congruence restrictions, an explicit parametrization of the integer solutions of the resulting congruence, a lower bound for $k$, and a divisibility relation involving the middle prime factor. The characterization is conditional on the primality of the three factors and does not assert that such prime triples exist for infinitely many parameters.

We study the problem of estimating the global treatment effect in randomized experiments under interference, where a unit's outcome may depend on the treatment assignments of other units. We adopt a minimax framework, allowing an adversary to select an outcome function from a class of functions that satisfy bounded outcomes and bounded interference. We derive minimax-optimal static estimators that are robust to a wide range of interference structures, parameterized by a scalar $δ$ controlling the maximum influence of one unit's treatment on another's outcome. Under large interference, we observe two regimes. When the treatment and control groups are equally sized, the minimax-optimal static estimator is the zero estimator. When one of the two groups is larger, the minimax-optimal static estimator is a "half-zero" estimator, in which the outcomes of the smaller group are ignored, and the estimator only considers the outcomes of the larger group.

We study the problem of guarding a set of straight lines in the plane by selecting a minimum-cardinality set of points such that every line contains at least one selected point. This problem is known to be strongly NP-hard \cite{megiddo}. We investigate approximation algorithms for the problem and analyze their performance guarantees under various structural assumptions on the underlying line arrangement. In particular, we present approximation schemes based on set-cover techniques, relaxation methods, and properties of maximal lines. We establish constant-factor bounds on the approximation ratio for several classes of arrangements and derive relationships between the guarding number and the incidence parameters of the arrangement. Connections with Dirac-type incidence results are also explored.
A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems

We prove the Díaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yalç$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
An entropic barrier to equilibration in the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation: Rigorous bounds for the microcanonical Brownian motion

The relaxation of the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation is known to slow down dramatically when the energy density $\varepsilon$ exceeds a critical value $\varepsilon_c$, where the system enters a condensed phase. Replacing the Hamiltonian dynamics by Brownian motion on the microcanonical surface of $N$ sites at fixed mass and energy, we prove rigorous upper and lower bounds on the equilibration time $τ_{\mathrm{eq}}$, which is governed by the first non-zero eigenvalue $λ_1$ of the Laplacian on this surface. In the condensed phase the equilibration time is stretched exponential, not exponential, in the system size. The upper bounds on $λ_1$ come from trial functions: of one occupation for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_c$, where the problem reduces to a Sturm-Liouville equation, and of two occupations for $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_c$, where they cross the bottleneck through which the condensate moves between sites. The lower bounds on $λ_1$ come from a Bochner-Reilly argument, with a vector field that compensates the concavity of the boundary. As a result, $τ_{\mathrm{eq}}=O(1)$ for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_c$, while for $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_c$, asymptotically in $N$, $(\sqrt{2}-1)\sqrt{\varepsilon-\varepsilon_c}\leq\lnτ_{\mathrm{eq}}/\sqrt{N}\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon-\varepsilon_c}$. We conjecture that the left-hand bound is sharp and the right-hand one is not.
Reverse Transportation and Harnack Inequalities for Underdamped Langevin in the Non-convex Setting
The Coxeter-Todd abelian sixfold, Gamma00, and big Schottky

We recall the construction of the Coxeter-Todd principally polarized abelian sixfold, and study its special properties.
 We show that the base locus of the Gamma00 linear system on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold consists of 253 points, disproving the stronger version by Donagi and Beauville--Debarre of the Gamma00 conjecture of van Geemen and van der Geer. This also leads us to construct explicit indecomposable 7-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties that are not Jacobians, but lie in the so-called Big Schottky locus, thus disproving the corresponding conjecture from the Schottky-Jung approach to the Schottky problem.
 We furthermore show that while no even theta constant vanishes for the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, its associated Scorza quartic is identically zero.
 Finally, we show that there exist two different theta level (2,4) structures on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, for which the sets of second order theta constants are projectively equal. This disproves the expected injectivity of the second order theta constant map for all genera starting with 6.
Randomized Adaptive Sequential Allocation and the Limits of Bounded Exposure to Inferior Treatments
Sampurna Kundu; Monitirtha Dey; Atanu Biswas

A clinical trial must learn which treatment is superior while sparing its participants from the inferior one. Kundu et al. 2025 recently showed that a purely deterministic rule, which always assigns the treatment with the larger current sample mean, achieves a strong form of this ethical goal. The smaller allocation count stays almost surely finite and has all moments bounded uniformly in the sample size. Deterministic allocation is, however, predictable, and predictability invites selection bias. We ask whether this bounded-exposure phenomenon survives once the deterministic rule is replaced by a smooth randomized one. We show that it does not. Under any fixed non-degenerate symmetric randomization, both treatments are sampled infinitely often, the adaptive sample means are strongly consistent, and the inferior treatment draws a strictly positive limiting allocation proportion. Consequently, the inferior allocation count grows linearly and its moments are unbounded. We then study annealed randomization, in which the randomization scale cools with the accumulated information, and obtain summability and divergence criteria that separate finite, sublinear, and linear exposure. A forced-exploration variant identifies the superior treatment with probability one while keeping the inferior exposure sublinear, and thereby frees the annealed guarantees from any correct-stabilization event. We also treat normalized multi-treatment rules, ties, indifference zones, unequal variances, general response distributions, and local alternatives. Finally, we develop the post-trial asymptotic inference that each exposure regime permits. The results delineate the trade-off between allocation concealment, persistent exploration, and ethical concentration on the superior treatment.
Volume Doubling and Geometric Inequalities on Graphs with Bakry-Émery Curvature
Yanlong Ding; Shiping Liu; Chiyu Zhou

We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $ε>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\leκm_-$. Under the Bakry--Émery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$
 P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y)
 +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we further prove volume doubling property: let $K_-:=\max\{-K,0\}$ $$
 \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,2R))\le C_0\exp\!\bigl(C_1\sqrt{K_-}\,R\bigr)
 \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R)),\qquad R>0, $$ where $C_0,C_1$ depend only on $ε,κ$. If $d$ is the maximum combinatorial degree of the support graph, we further prove under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ the sharp volume growth bound $\mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R))\le m_-CR^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}$ for all $o$ and $R\geq 1$.
The Carpenter property for subfactors of uniform infinite index

We show that if $N\subset M$ is an inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors of uniform infinite index, for instance an irreducible inclusion of infinite index, then every positive contraction $b\in N$ is of the form $E_N(p)$ for a projection $p\in M$. This gives the exact version of Popa's asymptotic result in the ultrapower, and it is a subfactor analogue of the Carpenter problem for masas. In particular, Popa's relative dimension set of such an inclusion is $[0,1]$, so the set of expectations of projections does not distinguish inclusions without corners of finite index. As applications, the Carpenter property holds for $N\subset N\rtimes G$ whenever an infinite group $G$ acts outerly on a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $N$, and for ICC groups $H\le G$ the inclusion $L(H)\subset L(G)$ has it exactly when $[G:H]=\infty$, confirming a recent conjecture. We also give examples showing that the Carpenter property does not imply uniform infinite index, and that infinite index does not imply the Carpenter property.
A complete characterization of graphs with second largest eigenvalue at most $(\sqrt5-1)/2$
Chaohui Chen; Hangxi Cha; Haiying Shan; Muhuo Liu

In 1993, Cao and Hong posed the problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is greater than $1/3$ and less than $(\sqrt5-1)/2$. Subsequent work extended the question to the non-strict bound. We give a complete structural characterization of connected graphs $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge2$ satisfying $λ_2(G)\le(\sqrt5-1)/2$. Their complements are described by disjoint unions of graphs from an explicit family with least adjacency eigenvalue at least $-(1+\sqrt5)/2$, possibly together with a cone or a thin or thick spider constructed from disjoint unions of members of the same family, subject to explicit numerical inequalities. This provides a positive characterization of the class, going beyond the classical result of Cvetković and Simić that the bound $λ_2\le(\sqrt5-1)/2$ admits only finitely many minimal forbidden induced subgraphs.
Polynomial convexity and non-polynomial convexity of totally real discs in $\mathbb{C}^2$

We study the polynomial convexity of smooth totally real discs contained in the boundaries of strongly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$. Using Wermer's classical example, we construct a bounded domain with smooth strongly pseudoconvex boundary containing a non-polynomially convex totally real disc. We also construct a nonsingular Levi-flat hypersurface in a non-Runge domain containing such a disc. This provides a partial negative answer, to a conjecture proposed in an earlier work. Furthermore, we prove that the Wermer graph over the closed disc of radius $R$ is polynomially convex for every $R\in (0,1)$. Finally, we establish a sufficient condition for the polynomial convexity of totally real discs contained in the smoothly bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$.
A Reider-type theorem for syzygies of cyclic covers of anticanonical rational surfaces

Let $π\colon X\to S$ be a smooth ramified cyclic cover of an anticanonical rational surface, with $κ(X)\geq0$, and let $A$ be a divisor on $S$. We prove a Reider-type theorem for syzygies: for every integer $p\ge 0$, the adjoint divisor $K_X+π^*A$ satisfies Property $\mathrm{N}_p$ provided that $A\cdot C\geq p+3$ for every curve $C\subseteq S$ with $C^2\le 1$. One ingredient is a syzygy criterion for finite covers that reduces the weight-two Koszul vanishing on $X$ to weight-one vanishing for the nontrivial character modules on $S$. The most delicate case, in which $\dim|-K_S|=0$ and $K_S^2<0$, is handled by a separate geometric argument.
Convergence properties of nonlinear RLC electrical networks

Convergence properties of general electrical networks with grounded nonlinear capacitors at the nodes and nonlinear inductors and resistors at the edges are studied. It is shown how, under appropriate conditions, for every initial condition there exists a unique equilibrium to which the system converges asymptotically. Partial extensions to networks with terminals or current sources are also provided. For RC networks this is compared with the use of an alternative storage function based on the co-content functions of the resistors.

We prove Lurie's proposed description of left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories in terms of purely $\infty$-categorical data. More precisely, unfolding gives an equivalence between left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories and complete categorical chain complexes of rigid symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories. More generally, unfolding identifies skeletal sequences with categorical chain complexes without the completeness condition. We extend these equivalences to $(\infty,\infty)$-categories and, stably, obtain an equivalence between complete unbounded categorical chain complexes and left rigid categorical spectra. We also analyze their groupoid completion and express the homotopy groups of the associated spaces and spectra in terms of categorical cycles and boundaries. As examples, we construct the categorical chain complexes associated to geometric and algebraic bordism categories, including their equivariant variants, and to iterated span categories. Their localizations recover classical bordism and $L$-groups, while the span examples are related to algebraic $K$-theory.

In this article we initiate the study of perfect commutative $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras in the non-connective setting. As an application we show that given a finite $C_p$-space $X$ the $\mathbb{F}_p$-cochains on $X^{C_p}$ can be recovered as a base-change of the tilt of the Tate construction on cochains on $X^e$.
Finite-Regularity Counterexamples to Katok's Periodic-Point Conjecture

For any $r>1$ and any nonnegative sequence $ω(n)=o(n)$, we construct a $C^r$ sphere diffeomorphism $f$ with $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)>0$ such that \begin{equation*}
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\#\Fix(f^n)=h,
 \qquad
 \sum_{n\geqslant1}e^{-hn+ω(n)}\#\Fix(f^n)<\infty. \end{equation*} Every ergodic invariant probability measure is hyperbolic, and, apart from finitely many fixed points, all periodic points lie in a single topologically mixing homoclinic class of entropy $h$. This shows that the logarithmic periodic-point lower bound is optimal in finite regularity. In particular, we answer the finite-regularity case of Katok's periodic-point question in the negative.
Covariant Calculus and Hamiltonian Flows for Nonlocal Wasserstein Metrics
Yuanke Chen; Jinqiao Duan; Qiao Huang

In this paper, we study nonlocal metrics on smooth positive probability densities on a closed manifold, induced by symmetric jump kernels and density-dependent mobilities. First, we introduce the density-variation operator to express the density derivatives of the Dirichlet form and kinetic energy. Second, we construct density and velocity-field representations of the tangent space and prove their isometric equivalence. We use the generator's pseudoinverse to derive Levi-Civita connections and covariant differentials in both representations. Third, we establish mechanical Hamiltonian dynamics in both tangent representations; an action principle and Legendre duality identify the Hamilton--Jacobi and covariant Newton equations; smooth negative gradient flows admit a zero-energy Hamiltonian lift. Entropy diffusion, nonlocal mean-field equations, Keller--Segel dynamics, and a nonlocal Vlasov equation illustrate the resulting calculus. For geometric-mean mobility, the Hopf--Cole transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger bridge system and the Madelung transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger equation yield hyperbolic and trigonometric phase energies, respectively. At zero momentum, both recover the metric kinetic energy to second order.
Generic point processes are intermittently hyperuniform and maximally rigid

We study the prevalence of hyperuniformity and spatial rigidity among translation- invariant ergodic simple point processes of fixed intensity, in a topology controlling local second moments. Hyperuniform processes are dense but meagre. We prove that intermittent hyperuniformity is residual: the number variance exhibits hyperuniform behavior along some sequences of radii and hyperfluctuating behavior along others. Maximal rigidity is also residual. Thus generic processes are maximally rigid but not hyperuniform. A local-to-global principle reduces the proofs to cross-section constructions for an arbitrary fixed essentially free ergodic $\mathbb{R}^d$-action. We also prove that processes admitting revival sequences form a residual set and exhibit near-quadratic variance along suitable van Hove sequences.

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. The Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constant $\mathsf{s}(G)$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ contains a zero-sum subsequence of length $\exp(G)$. The short zero-sum constant $η(G)$ is defined similarly, with the requirement that the zero-sum subsequence is nonempty and has length at most $\exp(G)$. It is known that $\mathsf{s}(G)\ge η(G)+\exp(G)-1.$ A conjecture proposed by W. Gao in 2003, which has been widely studied in zero-sum theory, predicts that $$ \mathsf{s}(G)=η(G)+\exp(G)-1 $$ for every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$. In this paper, we prove that this conjecture fails for the group $C_2^7\oplus C_6$.
On Bykov Cycles in Filippov Systems
Matheus G. C. Cunha; Paulo R. da Silva

We introduce two types of Bykov cycles for Filippov systems: crossing Bykov cycles, which retain the main dynamical features of their smooth counterparts, and sliding Bykov cycles, whose dynamics intrinsically involves the switching manifold. We construct explicit piecewise linear examples of both configurations. For crossing Bykov cycles, we prove the existence of hyperbolic invariant sets carrying symbolic dynamics, as in the classical smooth setting. For sliding Bykov cycles, under suitable open conditions, we obtain a countable symbolic dynamics on an invariant set; we prove that this invariant set has several interesting properties: the Hausdorff dimension of it and of its closure are equal, and it lies strictly between zero and one, and so both sets have zero Lebesgue measure; its closure is a Cantor set; and we also obtain conformal and invariant ergodic measures for the associated return dynamics. Finally, we show that convolution regularization of a suitable piecewise constant vector field produces a spatial cusp whose versal unfolding contains classical Bykov cycles. Thus, Bykov-type dynamics arises in the non-smooth setting both intrinsically, through crossing and sliding mechanisms, and through smooth regularization.
Finite tests and low-rank excluded minors for matroid path-width two

The path-width of a matroid is the minimum, over all orderings of its ground set, of the maximum value of its connectivity function on an initial segment. For any two connected rooted matroids whose roots are neither loops nor coloops, we form the 2-sum of each with a third such rooted matroid by identifying their roots and deleting the common element. The two original rooted matroids are equivalent when these sums agree on whether their path-width is at most two for every choice of the third rooted matroid. We prove that the two rooted matroids are equivalent if and only if this agreement holds for thirteen fixed graphic or cographic rooted matroids. They distinguish exactly twenty equivalence classes, and, moreover, there exists no family of twelve fixed connected rooted matroids that can guarantee this. Using these classes, we show that the tree in the canonical tree decomposition of an excluded minor for path-width at most two has diameter at most ten edges. For a connected matroid given by a tree decomposition using 2-sums, we give an exact recurrence to decide whether its path-width is at most two and to construct an ordering of width at most two when possible. Moreover, we derive a formula for the path-width of parallel extensions that gives complete binary excluded-minor lists in ranks three, four and five, containing two, four and eleven isomorphism classes, respectively.
Calabi flow on polarized Kähler surfaces
Haozhao Li; Bing Wang; Kai Zheng

We study global smooth Calabi flows on polarized Kähler surfaces $(M,L)$, assuming uniformly bounded Sobolev constants and the algebraic conditions $χ(\mathcal O_M)=1$ and $c_1(M)\cdot c_1(L)>0$. Using the orbifold compactness theorem, we prove a uniform Bergman estimate, construct a normal test configuration for each geometric limit, and establish uniqueness of the extremal orbifold limit up to polarized holomorphic isometry. K-polystability then identifies the limit with the original surface and gives a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric. We also prove finite-group equivariant versions of these results. Independently of the flow, we obtain a uniform Bergman lower bound for polarized cscK surfaces with bounded volume and Sobolev constants and $|S|\leq1$. We illustrate the hypotheses with nonstationary flows near a product cscK metric on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ and near Calabi's non-cscK extremal metric on the first Hirzebruch surface. Their controlled-cone energy inequalities follow from elementary calculations and continuity.
OC-OPD: Observation-coordinated Supervision for On-Policy Distillation
Ruoran Xu; Yilun Zhao; Ziyu Chen; Arman Cohan

Reverse and forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences provide complementary supervision in on-policy distillation: reverse KL refines the student's active token rankings, and forward KL allocates mass to teacher-supported candidates. At student-generated prefixes, we form a four-observation matrix by treating the student and teacher as both candidate sources and evaluators. The diagonal self-observations measure uncertainty, while source-centered cross-observations recover the two KL objectives. We establish an exact identity equating the Fisher inverse-metric coupling of their logit gradients with the sum of these contrasts, yielding a common local descent direction for distinct positive distributions. Observation-coordinated on-policy distillation (OC-OPD) uses observations to set preferences, closed-form bargaining to coordinate gradients, and distributional discrepancy to scale the update. Across three heterogeneous student settings (non-thinking generation, thinking generation, and base-model initialization), OC-OPD achieves strong gains in mathematical reasoning and transfers effectively to out-of-distribution scientific question answering and code generation. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/RuoranXu/OC-OPD.
Chain Conditions for Abelian Normal Subgroups
Falih A. M. Aldosray; Ian Stewart

We investigate various chain conditions for abelian normal subgroups of groups, following Robinson (1968). We focus on the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups, an exceptional case excluded from his results except for some counterexamples. In particular we show that a hypercentral group satisfies the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups if and only if it is is finitely generated nilpotent.
Shenwei Huang; Yidong Zhou; Yuwen Zhou

The well-known Erdős-Hajnal conjecture states that for any graph $H$, there is a constant $c=c(H)>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with no induced copies of $H$ contains a clique or an independent set of size at least $n^{c}$.
 In this paper, we prove that the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture holds for every path.
Moduli spaces of rank 2 sheaves on $\mathbb P^3$ via Quot schemes
Charles Almeida; Nicolò Bignami; Marcos Jardim; Andrea T. Ricolfi

We study the Gieseker--Maruyama moduli space $M_{c_3}$ of stable rank 2 torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^3$ with Chern classes $c_1=-1$, $c_2=1$, and odd $c_3 \le 1$. Every such sheaf $E$ has reflexive hull $E^{\ast\ast}$ parametrised by $M_1$, and the quotient $E^{\ast\ast}/E$ is a 0-dimensional sheaf of length $n = (1-c_3)/2$. We prove that $M_{c_3}$ is isomorphic to the relative Quot scheme $\mathsf{Quot}_{\mathbb{P}^3 \times M_1/M_1}(\mathscr{R},n)$, where $\mathscr{R}$ is the universal reflexive sheaf over $M_1$. Our technique combines (i) Bridgeland-type wall-crossing in Donaldson--Thomas theory, (ii) the theory of good moduli spaces, (iii) deformation theory in dgla and Ext-quiver language. We deduce that $M_{c_3}$ is connected, and we analyse its \emph{smoothable component} $M_{c_3}^{\mathsf{main}}$, proving it is rational and generically smooth of dimension $4n+3$. We further prove that $\dim \mathrm{Sing} M_{c_3} \geq 4n-2$ for all $n \geq 2$. Finally, we provide a geometric characterisation for the cases $n\leq 2$. We show that $M_{-1}$ is a smooth rational projective variety of dimension 7 and compute its motive in the Grothendieck ring of varieties, while $M_{-3}$ is shown to be an integral, normal variety of dimension 11 that is regular in codimension 4.
Carleson Measures and Integral Operators on Fock--Sobolev Spaces

For integers $n\ge1$ and $N\ge0$, let $\mathbf g=(g_0,\ldots,g_N)$ be a vector of entire functions. We consider the generalized integral operator \ [T_{\mathbf g}^{(n,N)}f
 =I^n\!\left(\sum_{j=0}^N g_jf^{(j)}\right),
 \qquad (Ih)(z)=\int_0^z h(w)\dd w. \] We characterize its boundedness and compactness between Fock--Sobolev spaces $\F_m^p$ and $\F_\ell^q$, where $0<p,q<\infty$ and $m,\ell\ge0$ are integers. The coefficients of critical total degree determine the operator modulo compact operators and yield essential-norm estimates. In the Hilbert case, a Laurent Toeplitz representation gives the exact essential norm, a Fredholm criterion and an index formula. As an application, we obtain conditions for solutions of linear differential equations to belong to Fock--Sobolev spaces, including a necessary and sufficient polynomial zero condition in the Hilbert case. For entire functions $u_0,\ldots,u_N$ and $\varphi$, we also characterize boundedness, compactness and essential norms of the operators \[
 L_{\mathbf u,\varphi}^{(N)}f
 =\sum_{j=0}^N u_j\,f^{(j)}\circ\varphi. \] The proofs use Carleson measure characterizations for finite sums of weighted differentiation operators on Fock--Sobolev spaces.
Theoretical relations between basic centrality measures in real-world networks

We establish new relationships among several fundamental measures of real-world networks, including the average clustering coefficient, the global clustering coefficient, the average shortest-path length and degree centrality, closeness centrality, betweenness centrality and ksi-centrality. We further develop the theory of $j$-neighborhood centrality, which encompasses degree centrality and ksi-centrality as special cases.
Time-Decay Rates toward Rarefaction Waves for the One-Dimensional Isentropic Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations
Mutong He; Feimin Huang; Lingjun Liu; Lingda Xu

While the asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations has been well established since the pioneering works of Matsumura--Nishihara \cite{MatsumuraNishihara1986} and Liu--Xin \cite{LiuXin1988}, the classical $L^2$ energy method yields only qualitative convergence in $L^\infty(\R)$ as $t\to\infty$ without any explicit decay rate. In this paper, we establish for the first time a standalone \(L^4\) energy estimate for perturbations of a weak rarefaction wave in the one-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes system, thereby obtaining the first explicit algebraic time-decay rates for this model. Specifically, for small initial perturbations in $H^2(\R)$ and small wave strength $δ$, we prove that $(v-V,u-U)$ decays in $L^4(\R)$ at the rate \[ \|(v-V,u-U)(t)\|_{L^4}\le C\bigl(\|(v_0-V(0),u_0-U(0))\|_{H^2}+\sqrtδ\bigr)(1+t)^{-1/8}, \] where \((V,U)\) denotes the smooth rarefaction wave, while the relative Riemann invariants \(z_\pm\) of the perturbed system decay in \(L^\infty(\R)\) at the rate \((1+t)^{-1/6}\). The proof relies on a new local quartic energy estimate for \(z_\pm\) and \(z_\pm-Q\), where \(Q=μ(v)v_x-μ(V)V_x\), as well as a nonlocal half-space wave-interaction functional for corrected characteristic modes and a weighted higher-order derivative energy estimate coupled at the scale of the one-dimensional Nash inequality.
The signed error-sum function of tent-map expansions

In this paper, we study the signed error-sum function of tent map base series introduced by Dai and Tang in 2011. We show that the function is discontinuous at every dyadic rational in the open unit interval, although it was asserted to be continuous. We determine its values at these points and analyze its range, differentiability, and variation. We also obtain sharp covering estimates for its graph and calculate the Hausdorff, box-counting, and covering dimensions of the graph, which are $1$, $1$, and $0$, respectively. Moreover, we show that the signed error sum agrees with Lévy's function away from dyadic rationals and that the unsigned error sum is the Takagi function.
Multi-Period Donation Allocation for Food Banks under Stochastic Capacity and Supply
Irem Sengul Orgut; Julie S. Ivy; Reha Uzsoy; James Wilson

Each food bank within the national Feeding America network faces the challenge of distributing donated food equitably across the food-insecure population it serves while minimizing food storage and waste over a multi-period planning horizon. Donated food supply is highly stochastic, and distribution to beneficiaries is done by autonomous local agencies whose capacities are uncertain and vary over time. Based on our long-standing partnership with a regional food bank in the southeastern United States, we address the equitable and effective distribution of food donations to charitable agencies over a finite planning horizon under uncertain capacity and supply. We derive structural properties of this problem and use them to develop efficient heuristics. An extensive numerical study evaluates the performance of the heuristics relative to a stochastic dynamic programming benchmark, which suffers from the curse of dimensionality. One heuristic consistently provides near-optimal solutions and can be easily implemented by food banks. Our results also apply to other problems involving the equitable and effective distribution of scarce resources under stochastic capacity and supply.
Asymptotic delta-like behavior of the weighted taper in Thomson's multitaper F-test

We study the weighted taper arising in Thomson's multitaper F test, which is constructed from pre-plunge discrete prolate spheroidal wave functions (DPSWF). Numerical evidence suggests that, in the asymptotic regime, the Fourier transform of this taper converges to a delta measure supported at the origin. We provide a rigorous theoretical justification for this behavior.
Convergence Guarantees for the Broximal Point Method under Perturbations
Alina Abdikarimova; Ammar Mahran; Peter Richtárik

The Broximal Point Method (BPM) of Gruntkowska et al. (2025) comes with strong guarantees for convex optimization: under convexity alone, it terminates after finitely many steps and converges linearly in function value, with bounds that do not depend on the condition number or on any other regularity property of the objective. Each iteration, however, requires the exact minimization of the objective over a ball, which is generally intractable. As a first step toward implementable variants, we study the method when these subproblems are solved only approximately. We introduce and analyze Inexact BPM, which replaces the exact broximal point by an approximation and makes no assumption on how this approximation is obtained. Under summable or sufficiently small errors, we bound the number of iterations needed to reach a neighborhood of the set of minimizers, and these bounds remain independent of the regularity of the objective. Under the weaker requirement that the errors stay below the ball radius, we prove sublinear convergence in function value for the exact broximal points underlying the perturbed iterates, valid until the target neighborhood is reached, and we recover linear rates under bounded sublevel sets or strong convexity.
Entire solutions of Fermat-Type Partial Differential-Difference equations in higher dimensions
Sujoy Majumder; Jhilik Banerjee; Abhijit Banerjee; Elias Saleeby

The purpose of this paper is to investigate the finite-order entire solutions of the following Fermat-type partial differential-difference equations: \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z+c))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z+c)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \left(\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_1}+\left(P_1(z)f(z+c)+P_2(z)f(z)\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} in $\mathbb{C}^m$, where $m_1,m_2\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $m_1+m_2>2$, $c=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_m)\in\mathbb{C}^m$, $P(\not\equiv 0)$, $P_1$, $P_2$ and $Q_i\;(i=1,2,\ldots,m)$ are polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^m$ such that $P(z)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{C}^m$.
 The results established in this paper generalize those of Xu et al. \cite{Xu-Luo-Cao-2025} from $\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathbb{C}^m$.
Boundary fibers of the holonomy map for complex projective structures

We study the Morgan--Shalen boundary of holonomy representations of complex projective structures on a compact Riemann surface of genus at least two. We prove that every direction defined by a holomorphic quadratic differential with a multiple zero admits distinct projective marked length limits. Together with Dumas's uniqueness theorem for simple zeros, this gives a complete characterization of directions with unique limits. We also establish that no nonzero abelian length function can occur in the holonomy boundary of any such fixed surface, regardless of the limiting quadratic differential. Finally, we characterize all directional boundary fibers by a necessary-and-sufficient analytic condition involving valued representations and the holomorphic jet bundle underlying an oper.
Global existence and decay estimates of solutions for the compressible Prandtl type equations in Sobolev spaces

This paper addresses the global existence and large-time decay of solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces. We study small perturbations around a monotone shear flow and establish global weighted Sobolev estimates together with precise time-decay rates for the solutions. The main difficulties are that the normal velocity causes a loss of one tangential derivative, the variable density gives rise to nonstandard boundary and shear-flow coupling terms, and the global-in-time argument requires sufficiently strong decay to close the time-weighted energy estimates. To overcome these difficulties, we combine the cancellation method introduced by Masmoudi and Wong~\cite{MW2015} with the good-quantity approach developed by Paicu and Zhang~\cite{PZ2021}, together with weighted shear-flow estimates and a careful treatment of the natural boundary structure. Under suitable assumptions on the density perturbation, the shear flow, and the function $f(t)$ describing the outer tangential flow, we prove the global-in-time well-posedness of solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces. In this sense, the present result may be viewed as a Sobolev-space counterpart of the recent analytic-framework result obtained by Chen, Huang and Li (J. Funct. Anal. 286 (2024), 110322)~\cite{CHL2024} for the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl-type equations, while requiring a weaker time-decay assumption on the density perturbation.
Parameter-robust preconditioners for a stabilized control-volume discretization of Biot's equations

We develop and analyze parameter-robust block preconditioners for a stabilized control-volume discretization of the quasi-static Biot equations. Beginning with a five-field formulation, we eliminate the poroelastic stress and time-scaled Darcy velocity through independent vertex-local solves, obtaining a symmetric cell-centered displacement--rotation--pressure system. A macrocell rotation-jump term stabilizes the weak-symmetry constraint. We prove the well-posedness of the fully discrete scheme and show that the condensed, coupled displacement--rotation mechanics block is uniformly spectrally equivalent to its block-diagonal counterpart. For uncoupled preconditioners, we derive an exact discrete pressure-control criterion and a sufficient parameter condition that accommodates the scaling \(c_0\asymp K_{\rm dr}^{-1}\), thereby allowing the storage coefficient to vanish in the nearly incompressible limit. We then construct a Schur-consistent pressure block that approximates the mechanics-induced pressure correction and prove its uniform equivalence to the exact pressure Schur complement. These results yield parameter-independent spectral bounds for block-diagonal preconditioning and weighted field-of-values estimates for lower-triangular preconditioning. Practical realizations employ a macrocell mass-matrix approximation for the stabilized rotation block and tailored two-grid solvers for the displacement and pressure blocks. Numerical experiments verify the expected convergence behavior in two dimensions and demonstrate robust performance under mesh refinement and broad variations of the physical parameters in both two and three dimensions.

Motivated by the recent asymptotic formula for the moment of the alternating sum of parts in partitions by Craig and Li, we study the moment of the alternating sum of parts in compositions. Tensor networks are a diagrammatic representation of complicated relations between tensors, and tensor contraction is the evaluation of a tensor network analogous to matrix multiplication. Tensor networks and tensor contraction are ubiquitous in computer science, physics, and applied mathematics.

It is equivalent to another possibly more straightforward but still NP-hard problem of finding the treewidth of the line graph of the tensor network.

This observation leads to the core innovation of this thesis, which is a new tensor contraction paradigm that uses graph theoretic operations to produce an equivalent tensor network whose line graph has lower treewidth than the original tensor network, before applying the bond-by-bond contraction algorithm. For every positive discount rate, we show that its characteristic polynomial has one negative root and two distinct positive roots. abla^{p-1}f$ and $

abla^{p-2}f$. Since the two reconstructions have different point-query costs, we use a block length $m$ for the order-$p$ approximation and a subblock length $\ell\leq m$ for the order-$(p-1)$ approximation. The latter is transported between consecutive reconstruction points using the stored order-$p$ approximation. This leads to an adaptive regularization method that does not require prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant. We prove finite termination at an $ε$-approximate first-order stationary point and derive an explicit bound on the number of bundled order-$(p-2)$ oracle queries. For $m=(p-2)n^2$ and $\ell=(p-2)n$, the accuracy-dependent term has dimension--accuracy scaling $n^{3/p}ε^{-(p+1)/p}$. Thus the method retains the $ε^{-(p+1)/p}$ dependence of full order-$p$ regularization while using derivatives only through order $p-2$. Within the dense reconstruction framework considered here, using separate block and subblock lengths gives dimension dependence of order $n^{3/p}$, compared with $n^{4/p}$ when a common length is imposed.
On Separately Continuous Functions of the First Baire Class on Squares and Mixed Products

We consider Mykhaylyuk's problem asking whether the Baire-one property for every separately continuous real-valued function on each of the squares $X^2$ and $Y^2$ implies the same property on $X\times Y$. Assuming $\mathfrak b>ω_1$, the article obtains a negative answer using the compact cube $K=[-1,1]^{ω_1}$ and the space $E=(c_{00}(ω_1),σ(c_{00}(ω_1),\ell_\infty(ω_1)))$. It presents a finite-coordinate characterization of Baire-one functions on $E$ under this hypothesis.
On Variational Inequalities for Averages over Hypersurfaces

This paper establishes sharp variational estimates for families of averaging operators over smooth hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$. For a hypersurface with $k$ non-zero principal curvatures at a given point, we prove that the $r$-variation operator $V_r(A_t f : t>0)$ is bounded on $L^p$ for all exponents satisfying $(k+1)/k < p < r(k+1)$, with operator norm depending explicitly on a translation parameter $D$. In the special case $k=n$ (i.e., non-vanishing Gaussian curvature), we show that the range $p<r(n+1)$ is optimal, thereby recovering and extending classical results for the sphere. Furthermore, for convex hypersurfaces of finite type (in the sense of Iosevich-Sawyer), we obtain variational bounds in the range $p_0 < p < 2r$, where $p_0$ is the contact index of the associated hypersurface. The proofs combine long-short variational decompositions, stationary phase analysis, vector-valued singular integrals, and local smoothing estimates for Fourier integral operators. These results unify and generalize earlier work on maximal functions and variational inequalities for averages over hypersurfaces.
An infinite family of graphs with Šoltés fraction uniformly above one half

The Wiener index $W(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is the sum of the distances between all unordered pairs of vertices. A vertex $x$ is a Šoltés vertex if $G-x$ is connected and $W(G-x)=W(G)$. We construct an infinite family of graphs in which the proportion of Šoltés vertices is strictly greater than $(\sqrt{21}-3)/3=0.5275\ldots>1/2$ and decreases to this value from $2/3$. The family is also described by a generalized Pell equation and starts from a $12$-vertex example of Akhmejanova et al. (Discrete Appl. Math. 325 (2023) 37-42). We also show that the construction remains valid after adding edges among certain vertices.
Perfect 1-factorisations of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group
Andrei V. Ivanov; Leonid M. Tertitski

A perfect 1-factorisation (P1F) of $K_{2n}$ is a partition of its edges into $2n-1$ perfect matchings, any two of which form a Hamiltonian cycle. Exhaustive classification is known only up to $K_{16}$. We present a method for the exhaustive generation, up to isomorphism, of perfect 1-factorisations with a non-trivial automorphism group, which reduces the search tree far enough to make $K_{18}$ and beyond feasible. It combines two ideas. For automorphism groups of order greater than 2, classical results of Ihrig on the automorphisms of P1Fs are used as tools that reject almost all prescribed cycle types without search. For the order-2 case, which dominates, candidates are recalculated from inherited compatibility lists, in the spirit of Gill and Wanless, with an outer loop over two further rows that keeps those lists small, and Ihrig's results restrict the first factor. As the numerical proof of the method we compute all 10,710 P1Fs of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group; before, only six were known.
RaFH and CRaFH superalgebras: Frobenius forms, representation theory and respectability

We introduce \emph{RaFH superalgebras}, which are Rees affine Frobenius Hecke superalgebras. These algebras are defined by generators and relations, using \emph{Frobenius-tensor superalgebras} to axiomatise tensor powers of Frobenius superalgebras together with their copairing elements. The RaFH superalgebras include, as special cases, the affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebras of type $A$, the affine Sergeev superalgebras, the affine wreath product algebras and quantum affine wreath algebras, as well as the recently introduced quantum wreath product algebras in the special case of the superflip braiding. We study the RaFH superalgebras from both structural and representation theoretic points of view. We prove a basis theorem for the RaFH superalgebras, construct universal Jucys--Murphy elements, and classify their simple modules over an algebraically closed field via atomic superalgebras, which are smaller RaFH superalgebras of Hecke, Clifford or wreath type.
 We then study \emph{CRaFH superalgebras}, which are the cyclotomic quotients of the RaFH superalgebras. We construct bases for these superalgebras, and compute the Gram determinants of natural trace forms, and use these to determine when these superalgebras are symmetric or Frobenius. To study the representation theory of the CRaFH superalgebras, we introduce the \emph{respectable algebras}, which is a vast generalisation of cellular algebras, standardly based algebras and finite dimensional affine cellular algebras, and give many examples illustrating their variety and ubiquity. We then show that CRaFH superalgebras are respectable algebras with weight poset given by multipartitions that are coloured by the representations of the underlying Frobenius algebra. This result can be viewed as a far-reaching generalisation of Murphy's bases into the setting of CRaFH algebras.
Uniform retractions onto a probability measure algebra and an application to topological groups
Dekui Peng; Li-Hong Xie; Jiang Yang

We prove that the indicator functions form a uniformly continuous retract of the set of $[0,1]$-valued functions in $L^2([0,1])$. Consequently, the Lebesgue probability measure algebra, equipped with the symmetric-difference metric, is an injective uniform space. The construction uses dyadic conditional expectations and a common exponential coupling to obtain Lipschitz maps into the indicator functions that approximate the identity uniformly on that set. As an application, we construct a Polish topological group whose left uniform space is injective but which admits a bounded left uniformly continuous real-valued function that is not right uniformly continuous. This answers the injective part of a question of Bouziad and Troallic in the negative. The group is a semidirect product of two copies of the measure algebra and is also bounded, locally finite, and of exponent at most four.
Finite Cotangent Power Sums Weighted by Additive Characters With Application to Mean Values of Additive-and-Multiplicatively Twisted $L$-Functions

We derive explicit formulas for finite sums of powers of cotangents, both at rational and arbitrary arguments, together with their alternating counterparts, weighted by additive characters. Our method relies on Apostol--Bernoulli polynomials and on the partial fraction expansion of trigonometric functions. As applications, we solve the problem posed by Berndt, Kim and Zaharescu \cite{BKZ:2023} on evaluating $\sum\csc^{2m}$ and $\sum\sec^{2m}$ at rational arguments, recover as a special case the classical Berndt--Yeap formula, and relate our identities to spectral zeta functions of circulant graphs.
 Furthermore, to systematically evaluate higher-order derivatives arising from the Lipschitz summation formula, we introduce a novel sequence of polynomial coefficients $c_{m,j}(β)$, termed \emph{deformed cotangent coefficients}, and establish their recursive and algebraic properties. Using these coefficients, we establish a general additive-and-multiplicatively twisted character mean value theorem for Lerch zeta functions, significantly extending the framework of Bayad and Raouj to incorporate additive character twists.
Dimension bounds for finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes

We prove that a finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytope has dimension at most $81$, substantially improving Prokhorov's bound of $995$. A refinement of Prokhorov's method gives the intermediate bound $162$, while an extension of Vinberg's planar-angle comparison to the finite-volume setting yields the sharper bound. Both arguments combine improved weighting functions with estimates using cusp geometry to control weight contributions of angles at ideal vertices or edges incident to them.
Critical characteristic-polynomial chaos for complex iid matrices
Yin Cai; Xiang Fang; Feng Guo

We prove convergence to critical Gaussian multiplicative chaos for characteristic-polynomial measures of complex iid matrices. Let $A_N=N^{-1/2}(ξ_{ij})$, with a fixed law satisfying $\mathbb Eξ=\mathbb Eξ^2=0$, $\mathbb E|ξ|^2=1$, and finite moments of every order; no density is assumed. On each fixed disk $\{|z|\le r\}$, $0<r<1$, expectation-normalized determinant measures at power $2\sqrt2$, multiplied by $\sqrt{\tfrac12\log N}$, converge to critical chaos with a fourth-cumulant covariance correction. The normalized height-deficit marked measure converges to the product of this spatial limit and the standard Rayleigh law. Convergence holds jointly with centered averages of the $\sqrt2$-scaled original logarithmic field against finitely many smooth compactly supported bulk tests, and with the two-sided near-critical curve at powers $q=2\sqrt2-2λ/\sqrt{\log N}$. On fixed compact parameter intervals, the curve converges in law in the uniform weak topology; all limiting coordinates use the same Gaussian field. The limiting curve is an explicit deterministic profile times the same critical measure.

We study groups of units modulo $n$ whose nonidentity elements are all primes in $\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$. We prove that there are only nine groups of prime units which are the full group of units modulo $n$, and there are fewer than $10^{22}$ groups of prime units containing all prime units in the possible range $(\sqrt n,n-\sqrt n)\cup\{n-1\}$. We prove under Dickson's conjecture that there are infinitely many groups of prime units of arbitrary order $d \ge 2$ modulo composite integers. We prove under Schinzel's Hypothesis H that there are infinitely many groups of prime units of order 3 modulo a prime $r$. We prove that the number of such prime moduli $r$ smaller than $X$ is $\ll X/(\log X)^3$.
Global weak solutions with vacuum for isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the unit disk under Dirichlet boundary conditions

We construct global weak solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson systems in the unit disk under no-slip boundary conditions, allowing vacuum and unbounded densities for sufficiently small initial energy. Such solutions particularly possess uniform $L^{q_0}$ density bounds for some $q_0>4γ$, beyond the natural energy class. Our analysis combines Green function representations with the mean-value property of harmonic functions to isolate a pressure-generated harmonic component of the effective viscous flux and obtain a purely interior potential representation valid for both systems. These results complement Perepelitsa's half-space theory (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 212 (2014), pp. 709-726) and our recent half-plane work (arXiv:2601.11852, 2026), treating bounded-domain geometry and Poisson coupling with nonnegative initial density.
IncVNM: An Interactive Recommender System with Incremental von Neumann-Morgenstern Utility Learning

In modern recommender systems, users are often presented with products whose outcomes are random. The values of such products depend on their entire outcome distributions and on users' attitudes toward risk, making them difficult to evaluate using traditional product-level recommendation methods. We propose \textsc{IncVNM}, an interactive recommender system that incrementally learns a user-specific von Neumann--Morgenstern (VNM) utility function from ordinal click feedback generated during ordinary webpage browsing. At each interaction, \textsc{IncVNM} converts the click order within a displayed product list into pairwise comparisons between outcome distributions and updates the nominal utility by minimizing its deviation from the previous estimate while incorporating the newly observed pairwise comparisons. To close the interaction loop, an entropy-regularized sampling policy balances exploitation of the learned utility against exploration for additional preference information. We evaluate \textsc{IncVNM} in a rolling-window experiment with different response-error probabilities and show that it substantially outperforms the expected-return, mean--variance, discounted-UCB, and distribution-aware BPR baselines.

Lehto-type growth conditions and a Picard theorem for the gradient of entire solutions to the Euler -- Lagrange equations of variational integrals with linear growth in the plane including a small extension of Moser's Bernstein result

We mainly consider entire solutions $u: \mathbb{R}^2 ightarrow \mathbb{R}$ of the Euler -- Lagrange equation for a variational integral with density $g(|
abla u|)$ of linear growth. Assuming a Lehto-type condition at infinity, we show that either $
abla u$ is a constant vector or the image of $
abla u$ is the whole plane with the possible exception of at most one point. This result is extended to certain energy densities of nearly linear growth. Moreover, we slightly generalize the Bernstein result of Moser.
Inhomogeneous Fiber Refinement of Gallagher's Theorem
Qian Li; Bo Tan; Qing-Long Zhou
Uniqueness results for the exterior Dirichlet and Neumann problem in two dimensions for the Euler-Lagrange equations of variational integrals with linear growth

We consider solutions $u, v:Ω\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{N}$ of the Euler-Lagrange equations associated to the variational integral $\int_Ωf(\nabla u)dx$, where $Ω$ is an exterior domain in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ e.g., the complement of a disk or a half plane, and the density $f$ is of linear growth. Among other things we show that $u|_{\partialΩ}=v|_{\partialΩ}$ together with the boundedness of $u-v$ yields that $u=v$ on the entire domain.

In this paper, we prove that for every topological MV-algebra the topology is induced by a uniformity. As a application, we obtain that every topological MV-algebra is completely regular and every \(T_0\) first countable topological MV-algebra is metrizable.
Romain Bourneuf; Johannes Carmesin; Jan Kurkofka; Tim Planken

The classical cactus theorem of Dinitz, Karzanov and Lomonosov from 1976 states that the minimum edge-cuts of a connected graph are displayed by a cactus. For vertex-separations, Tutte's theorem gives an exact cactus-decomposition for connectivity $2$, but exact cactus-decompositions fail for higher connectivity. Extending earlier approximate cactus-decomposition results for connectivities $3$ and $4$ by Carmesin and Kurkofka [FOCS 2023] and Kurkofka and Planken [SODA 2026] to all connectivities, we prove that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there is a constant $d=d(k)$ such that every $k$-connected graph $G$ admits a cactus-decomposition displaying $k$-separations such that every $k$-separation of $G$ has edit-distance at most $d$ to a displayed separation.
 Our proof develops tools that may be useful beyond this result. The first is a three-dimensional version of the classical corner-diagram method, which we use to show that triples of crossing $k$-separations have a controlled two-dimensional behaviour. The second is a covering-space approach for studying local crossing patterns from a global perspective. Third, we advance the theory of flowers, which originated in matroid theory.
The Maximum Diagonal Product of a Stochastic Matrix of Bounded Rank

Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be a nonnegative row-stochastic or column-stochastic $n\times n$ matrix of rank at most $k$, where $1\le k\le n$. Write $n=qk+s$, where $0\le s<k$. The author conjectured in 2018 that, for every permutation $σ$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $\prod_{i=1}^n a_{i,σ(i)}\le q^{-q(k-s)}(q+1)^{-(q+1)s}$. We prove this bound and classify all equality cases.
Siegel-Weil type identities for general linear groups related to parabolic induction from two Speh representations

We prove identities of Siegel-Weil type for Eisenstein series on general linear groups, attached to parabolic induction from two Speh representations corresponding to the same irreducible, cuspidal representation. Such an identity relates a residue, at a (simple) pole of an Eisenstein series, as above, to a value of a similarly structured Eisenstein series at a point of holomorphy.
Double Fibration Transforms: Geometry and Microlocal Analysis

Double fibration transforms integrate functions over families of submanifolds. We survey the recovery of singularities by both classical normal operator methods and direct analytic methods. We also discuss support theorems, injectivity and applications to geodesic ray transforms, seismic inversion and minimal surface data.
Stochastic Orders of the Exit Pair and the Monotone Response to Resetting
Tony Newton; Juan Antonio Vega Coso

Resetting a process, that is, restarting it from its initial position at random times, changes the probability that it leaves an interval through one end rather than the other. We show that the direction of this change is governed by how the exit time depends on the exit side, and we express this through classical stochastic orders. For random walks and birth-death chains we determine when resetting more intensively always moves the exit probability in the same direction, and we show that this can fail: we give an explicit chain in which the direction reverses twice over time, and bound the number of such reversals spectrally. We also show how the direction depends on the starting point. In the continuum limit we obtain the corresponding results for diffusions with drift.
Optimization Frameworks & Learning Algorithms for Discrete-Time Mean Field Games

This monograph introduces discrete-time mean field games with finite state and action spaces, emphasizing optimization formulations and learning algorithms. Starting from Markov decision processes and finite-player stochastic games, it develops the notion of mean field Nash equilibrium, establishes existence and uniqueness results under suitable assumptions, and explains how mean field equilibria yield approximate equilibria in large finite-player games. Building on the linear programming formulation of Markov decision processes, occupation measures and primal-dual formulations connect equilibrium computation with mathematical optimization. The monograph presents fixed-point iterations, fictitious play, online mirror descent, and optimization-based methods, discussing their convergence properties and limitations. Numerical examples illustrate crowd motion, traffic routing, epidemic management, and the computation of multiple equilibria. It combines examples, theoretical results, and implementable algorithms, with bibliographic notes providing connections to the broader literature.
The maximum concentration of results in incomplete round-robin tournaments

The Herfindahl--Hirschman Index (HHI), a standard measure of market concentration, is widely used to quantify competitive balance in sports tournaments. To enable comparisons over time or across leagues, both its minimum and maximum should be known. The minimum is usually trivial. Our paper provides results on the maximum HHI in incomplete round-robin tournaments, where the set of matches is represented by a regular but not complete undirected graph. We prove that the lower bound of maximum HHI is reached when the tournament consists of independent round-robin groups, while the upper bound of maximum HHI is reached when the set of matches is represented by a bipartite graph. Maximising HHI is computationally difficult even for highly structured graph types corresponding to real-world tournaments, where the teams are partitioned into pots and play the same number of matches against opponents from every pot. The complexity of the problem does not depend on the scoring system or the number of opponents from a pot.
An Observable-Algebra Approach to Quantum Coherence in Anyonic Systems

Physical restrictions on operations can make quantum coherence inaccessible. Quantifying off-diagonal density matrix elements in a chosen basis alone does not reveal which information is hidden by each restriction. To distinguish their effects, we describe physical restrictions through subalgebras of accessible observables. The associated trace-preserving conditional expectations unify two reconstruction principles: each gives both the maximum-entropy state compatible with the accessible data and the closest state in the corresponding subalgebra in relative entropy. We apply this framework to anyonic systems to separate the contributions from local-charge superselection and non-Abelian fusion rules. We prove that the charge-line severing map is the conditional expectation onto the local-product subalgebra. It is completely positive and quantum-trace-preserving, and uniquely reconstructs a state in this space from all local-product expectation values. The hierarchy of measurement restrictions then separates total bipartite coherence into three nonnegative contributions: coherence between local charges, inaccessible fusion information, and conventional coherence. The first two decompose the anyonic charge entanglement and distinguish the effects of local-charge superselection from the remaining fusion information. Finally, we relate basis-independent measures of anyonic coherence to entanglement. For pure anyonic states with vacuum total charge, the optimized total and correlated coherence equal the total and conventional relative-entropy entanglement, respectively.
A remark on the AI proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture

We give a geometric interpretation of the projection and reconstruction underlying the Open AI's characteristic-two proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture. Using the double covering and filling a puncture, we construct a morphism on normalized level-two associators with an explicit inverse on its image. We compute the restricted tangent reconstruction in the pro-2 realization and identify the leading coefficient maps with those of the OpenAI proof, making its implicit reconstruction explicit.
Convex Regression at Scale: Geometry-Preserving Constraint Sparsification

Convex regression provides a flexible nonparametric estimation framework while incorporating appropriate shape information. However, its standard least-squares formulation has $O(n^2)$ supporting-hyperplane constraints creating a computational bottleneck as the sample size $n$ increases. We study a $K$-nearest-neighbor (KNN) localized relaxation for convex regression where we for each sample, we only maintain the $K$ nearest hyperplane constraints. Under mild regularity conditions, we establish statistical guarantees for our modified estimator in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. In particular, for $d>4$, the population risk of our modified problem can be shown to have equivalent convergence rates as the original least square convex regression estimator of $\widetilde O(n^{-2/d})$ using neighborhoods sizes (i.e. $K=K_n$) of order $\widetilde O(n^{2(d-1)/(2d-1)})$ for general convex functions and $\widetilde O(n^{(d+1)/(d+2)})$ for strongly convex functions. To corroborate our theory, we implement iterative optimization methods to compare the prediction accuracy of the KNN relaxation with those of the full estimator across synthetic convex benchmarks. Our experiments demonstrate that KNN prediction risk approaches the full-estimator prediction risk at neighborhood sizes matching the theoretical scale.
Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration

Let $0<λ_1\leqλ_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ λ_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^kλ_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω) \frac{n}{n+2}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{ω_{n-1}}{ω_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.
Expected Minimax Regret Rates for Adaptive LQG Control on Fixed Parameter Sets

We study how a fixed model family determines expected minimax regret in adaptive LQG control. The family is compact and affine, with partial observation and unknown noise covariances.
