We organize methods by how they split cost between offline preparation and online inference, and compare their assumptions, advantages and limitations, with emphasis on computational speedups. Some ongoing directions and open questions are gathered at the end.
Similarity cancellation and primitive operator roots

Kaplansky's second test problem for similarity asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$ for bounded operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We answer this question in the negative, even for compact operators whose singular values satisfy any prescribed positive upper bounds tending to zero. We also show that cancellation can fail under the stronger hypothesis $J_2(T)\sim J_2(S)$ considered by Marcoux, Radjavi, Troscheit, and Zhang \cite{MRTZ}. For these operators, finite amplifications and primitive roots are similar exactly at even multiplicities and even orders, respectively. In contrast, cancellation in fixed matrix size admits a uniform bound on the condition number. This extends the finite type~$I$ results of Jiang, Ma, Shi, and Zhang \cite{JMSZ}. The bound also holds for simultaneous similarity of arbitrary families of matrices and can be chosen to tend to one as the amplified bound tends to one. We conclude that, in a finite type~$I$ von Neumann algebra, cancellation of doubles and cancellation of primitive square roots are each equivalent to boundedness of the orders of its nonzero homogeneous summands.
Exponential suppression of bit-flip errors in dissipative cat qubits

We study the infinite-dimensional Lindblad generator $L_ε=D[a^2-α^2]+εD[a]$, describing a dissipative cat qubit subject to single-photon loss. For sufficiently large $α$ and sufficiently small $ε>0$, we identify a two-dimensional spectral subspace near zero and establish an upper bound on the slow decay rate that decreases exponentially with $α^2$, uniformly in $ε$. This proves exponential suppression of bit-flip errors.
Counterexamples to uniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform under quadratic decay

We show nonuniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform on $\mathbb Z^2$ under quadratic decay. We construct an explicit nonzero function in $\ell^1(\mathbb Z^2)$ with pointwise decay $O(|z|^{-2})$ whose sums over integer lines vanish. We also obtain an infinite-dimensional null space with the same decay assumption. Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.
Contact multiplicity and a sharp six-map bound for collinear self-similar dendrites

Let $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the attractor of $n\ge2$ similarities $z\mapstoλz+b_k$, $0<|λ|<1$, whose fixed points are evenly spaced on a line, and suppose that $K$ does not lie in a line. We prove that $K$ can be a dendrite only if $n\le6$, and that such dendrites exist for every $2\le n\le6$; no separation or finite-intersection hypothesis is imposed. Hence, for $n\ge7$, every connected $K$ of this kind has interior points or separates the plane. Neighboring pieces of $K$ meet in similar copies of a single contact set. In a dendrite exactly one first-level piece meets this set, whereas for $n\ge7$ at least $n-\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil\ge2$ do, a bound attained by explicit quadratic parameters. The proof combines a planar translation obstruction for replicated contact arcs with an estimate based on Jensen's formula. After normalizing to $z\mapsto t+z/c$, $t\in\{-n+1,-n+3,\ldots,n-1\}$, the connectedness locus is the closure, outside the unit disk, of the roots of monic integer polynomials of height at most $n-1$. The same estimate shows that, for $n\ge7$, every such polynomial with a non-real root $c$ satisfying $|c|^2\ge\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil+1$ has subleading coefficient of absolute value at most $\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$, and that this bound is sharp. Accordingly, for $n\ge7$, at every non-real boundary point $c$ of the locus with $|c|>1$, each expansion $c=\sum_{j\ge0}d_jc^{-j}$ with integer digits $|d_j|\le n-1$ has $|d_0|\le\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$.
Minimax estimation of linear functionals in the Darcy inverse problem
Yi Liu; Xiaotian Chang; Qirui Hu

We study estimation of linear functionals $\int fψ$ of the conductivity $f$ in the Darcy problem $\nabla\cdot(f\nabla u)=g$ from observations of $u$ in Gaussian white noise of level $N^{-1/2}$. When the potential has a single nondegenerate minimum, we determine the minimax rates over Sobolev balls in the linearised experiment. Unless a compatibility condition along the gradient flow holds, the rate is governed by an effective dimension $T$ of the Hessian at the minimum, not by the ambient dimension: it is $N^{-(2s+T)/(4s+8)}$ for $T<4$, has an elbow at $T=4$ with an extra logarithmic factor, and is parametric for $T>4$. In the nonlinear experiment we show that these lower bounds persist when compatibility fails at the reference and $T\le4$, and we prove the minimax rate on classes with isotropic critical Hessians, and the parametric rate near references with $T>4$. In dimension at most four, no nonzero linear functional is uniformly $\sqrt N$-estimable on a Sobolev neighbourhood of the constant conductivity, even when it is regular there.
Sharp Critical Rates for Locally Private Distribution Estimation
Yi Liu; Xiaotian Chang; Qirui Hu

We determine sharp minimax rates for distribution estimation under pure local differential privacy at critical query smoothness. For the integral probability metric generated by the unit ball of $B^d_{2,q}$, $1\le q\le\infty$, over fixed periodic Sobolev density balls with positive smoothness and interior slack at the uniform density, the expected risk is of order $N^{-1/2}(\log N)^{3/2-1/q}$, where $N=n\varepsilon^2$; expected squared risk has the squared order. The fine index governs aggregation across resolutions that share one private information budget. A single noninteractive release with a measurable proper density output attains these rates, and matching lower bounds allow finite public blackboard interaction and repeated participation under each user's total privacy budget. A known $L^2$ radius permits the same rates without using density smoothness, with output in the $L^2$ density ball. Separately, for positive smooth densities on $[0,1]$, integrated squared CDF risk has minimax order $(\log N)^2/N$, with sharp quantile, Wasserstein, and transport map consequences. The rates hold uniformly for $0<\varepsilon\le1$ as $N\to\infty$, with class parameters fixed.
Small-LCM Distinct Covering Systems via Segmented Local Search

We construct distinct covering systems with minimum moduli 8, 9, 10, 11 and least common multiples 20160, 75600, 302400, 3326400, respectively, and conjecture that these values are minimal. For minimum modulus 8, the exclusion computations leave only 10080 and 15120 unresolved below our construction. The constructions use segmented local search: moduli are introduced in increasing blocks, followed by joint reoptimization of selected blocks. We give complete residue lists and an independent integer-arithmetic verifier. Two computational studies, comprising 180 initial runs and 130 follow-up runs, compare initialization orders, revisit rules and seed-bank capacities under fixed scan limits.
The Prodigal Elephant Returns: Last-Return Laws in the Superdiffusive Regime

Let $(S_n)$ be the one-dimensional elephant random walk with memory parameter $p\in(3/4,1)$ and first-step probability $q=\mathbb{P}(S_1=1)\in[0,1]$. Set $a=2p-1$, and let $f_{q,a}$ denote the density of the almost-sure limit of $S_n/n^a$. We prove that the last return time $T_0=\sup\{m\geq0:S_m=0\}$ satisfies:
 $\mathbb{P}(T_0\geq n)\sim f_{q,a}(0)\sqrt{\frac{8}{π(2a-1)}}n^{-(a-1/2)}$.
 Reflection gives $f_{q,a}(0)=f_{1,a}(0)$, so the constant is independent of $q$. For future walks started from admissible states $(n,x_n)$ with $x_n/\sqrt n\to z$, we establish functional convergence of the centered martingale-normalized paths to a time-changed Brownian motion. Uniform control of late hitting times then gives the eventual-return kernel $2Φ(-\sqrt{2a-1}|z|)$, uniformly on bounded scaled windows, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The same last-visit asymptotic holds uniformly for nonempty deterministic targets $F_n\subseteq[-r_n,r_n]\cap\mathbb{Z}$, $r_n=o(\sqrt n)$, held fixed during each trajectory. Conditionally on $T_0\geq n$, we identify the joint limit of $S_n/\sqrt n$, the next return divided by $n$, and the last return divided by the next return. The last ratio converges to $A^{-1/(2a-1)}$, independently of the other two limiting coordinates, where $A$ has the arcsine distribution on $(0,1)$.
Artinian reduction applied to the Largest Intersection Problem

Suppose we have $r$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^m$ of degree $d$, whose defining polynomials are linearly independent and whose intersection is zero-dimensional. What is the maximum number of points in their intersection? This problem is motivated by computing the generalized Hamming weights of projective Reed-Muller codes, and a conjectured formula for this maximum was given in [21]. We prove the conjectured formula for arbitrary $m$ when $\binom{m+d}{d}-\binom{d+2}{2}<r\leq\binom{m+d}{d}$. We use the notion of Artinian reduction to reformulate the problem in terms of graded Artinian algebras and then apply combinatorial tools to bound their Hilbert functions.
Mixed-Integer Programming for Causal Discovery with Unknown Hard-Intervention Targets
Tong Xu; Armeen Taeb; Simge Küçükyavuz; Ali Shojaie

When intervention targets are uncertain, learning causal relationships and identifying directly perturbed variables become a joint task. We develop an exact mixed-integer program based on optimized parent-set scores (PS-MIP) for joint graph and intervention-target estimation in linear Gaussian structural equation models under stochastic hard interventions. The method can incorporate candidate-edge restrictions and partial target knowledge when available. For each random variable, PS-MIP evaluates candidate sets of direct causes, or parent sets, by optimizing the likelihood parameters and compatible target patterns, retaining both the score and a minimizing target pattern. A global mixed-integer program then selects parent sets subject to acyclicity. Under stated conditions, this reduction preserves the joint objective and reconstructs the graph, targets, and likelihood parameters. Because the local scores are precomputed, PS-MIP replaces a direct large bilinear mixed-integer program with a linear selection problem; empirically it certifies global optimality on far more instances than the direct formulation (126 of 180 versus 34) and is often orders of magnitude faster. On synthetic data, PS-MIP achieves favorable false-discovery--true-discovery trade-offs relative to several benchmark algorithms for causal discovery with unknown intervention targets, along with strong intervention-target recovery in denser settings. An exploratory study on real data from a controlled physical system further demonstrates recovery beyond simulation.
Singular Perturbations for Control Systems Safety
Stefano Di Gregorio; Guido Carnevale; Giuseppe Notarstefano

Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) offer a powerful theory for enforcing safety in dynamical systems. Yet, applying this framework to complex systems is challenging when subsystems are feedback-interconnected and operate at different timescales. Such structures arise naturally in multiphysics systems and in control architectures where physical plants interact with optimization, estimation, and control algorithms. In many of these settings, safety involves only part of the system, motivating the design of reduced-order certificates. Inspired by singular perturbation theory, we establish sufficient conditions, involving separation between slow and fast dynamics, under which a reduced-order safety certificate can be lifted to the full interconnected system. Specifically, we construct a composite CBF ensuring forward invariance of a lifted subset of the original safe set. We also show that the certified safe set expands monotonically as the tuning parameter accelerating the fast dynamics is reduced. Numerical results validate the approach on two robotic systems: a planar 2-DoF manipulator with motor dynamics and a 6-DoF UR10e manipulator controlled by a suboptimal optimization algorithm.
Sub Terahertz LEO Satellite Communication: Is Doppler Shift a Major Challenge?
Seongjoon Kang; Parisa Ramezani; Ki Won Sung; Vitaly Petrov

In this work, we investigate the impact of Doppler frequency shift on sub-terahertz low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications using OFDM transmission. To comprehensively evaluate the severity of the Doppler shift impact on sub-terahertz satellite-to-ground links, we first put together an evaluation framework that jointly accounts for major Doppler-induced and non-Doppler-induced signal impairments in such systems. We then compare and contrast three possible engineering approaches to deal with Doppler shift in such a communication system. Our study concludes that (i)~while just ignoring the Doppler effect in such high-frequency and high-mobility systems substantially compromises the performance and reliability, (ii)~most of the negative effects can be eliminated by implementing only a small set of low-complexity measures. We particularly show that even a single Doppler shift estimation over a 5-min-long satellite pass over the ground user location may be sufficient to ensure high performance throughout the entire connectivity period. Hence, while Doppler shift is an important effect to account for in sub-terahertz LEO satellite communications, it should not constitute a critical design challenge for these emerging systems.
Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop

We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman reconstruction. In the second, we obtain a closed-form evaluation of the generating series from which the conjecture follows. For $n=3$, the resulting closed formula establishes a special case of a Gopakumar-Vafa-type conjecture for Calabi-Yau fivefolds.
Clique counts under degree and matching constraints

We study the maximum number of $t$-cliques in graphs with maximum degree at most $D$ and matching number at most $M$, with no restriction on the number of vertices. For $t\ge 3$, we determine this maximum whenever $D\ge 2M-1$ and characterize all extremal graphs when the maximum is positive. Up to isolated vertices, these are complete or complete split graphs for $D\ge 2M$, while $K_{2M}$ is uniquely extremal when $D=2M-1$. We also derive a general upper bound from the Chvátal-Hanson edge theorem and refine it for even $D$. For fixed even $D$ and $3\le t\le D+1$, every extremal graph consists, apart from isolated vertices, of copies of $K_{D+1}$ together with a remainder whose order is bounded independently of $M$. When $D/2$ divides $M$, this remainder is empty and the extremal graph is unique. This structure yields an eventual recurrence, reducing the determination of all extremal values and graphs to finitely many matching bounds.
$a$-contraction applied to the time-asymptotic stability of weak shocks for a general 1-D viscous system
Young-Sam Kwon; Jiayun Meng; Alexis Vasseur

The method of $a$-contraction with shifts builds on the relative entropy method of Dafermos and DiPerna and allows both viscous shocks and rarefaction waves to be studied directly at the level of the solution. This unified framework led to the resolution of Matsumura's long-standing conjecture on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous shock in composition with a rarefaction. Kang, Vasseur, and Wang established this stability for the one-dimensional compressible barotropic Navier-Stokes system. Their result was subsequently extended to composite planar waves for general $n\times n$ viscous systems in arbitrary spatial dimensions.
 The present paper is a companion to that work. Here we prove the estimates on viscous shock profiles needed to apply $a$-contraction with shifts, including derivative estimates that go beyond the standard bounds. We also give a streamlined account of the main ideas of the method by focusing on a single viscous shock for a general one-dimensional system.
Entropic Column Generation and Lehmer Branch-and-Price for Bin Packing Problem

We introduce Lehmer branch-and-price, an exact algorithm for bin packing and cutting stock problems built on the Lehmer transform, the ratio of Mellin transforms of item weights at consecutive orders. The transform maps each bin, a finite multiset of item weights, to a smooth increasing curve, and so gives the discrete problem a continuous representation on which the tools of analysis, such as convexity, exponential families and smoothing, can act. Read along this curve, the problem yields an explicit dual solution, a monotone representation of the dominance order, a family of constructive heuristics with first fit decreasing as its limit, and an integer identity that tells when the linear relaxation can decide an instance and when only a perfect packing can improve the best solution known. Lifted from items to patterns, the transform gives entropic column generation, a new form of column generation that bounds the relaxation from both sides at every iteration without solving the pricing problem exactly, maximizes a smoothed dual at an explicit rate, and measures by an entropy how much the relaxation leaves undecided. We show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the standard benchmark in both the number of instances solved and the computational time.
Modular proof analysis and cut elimination for the Reflection Calculi $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$
Joost J. Joosten; Cosimo Perini Brogi

The reflection calculus with one modality is denoted by $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and its quantified generalization is known as $\mathsf{QRC}_1$. These decidable calculi are of interest since they generate the strictly positive fragments of the (quantified) provability logic for theories like Peano Arithmetic and Heyting Arithmetic.
 We introduce analytic cut-free calculi ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ for $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The new calculi derive sequents of the form $A\Longrightarrow B$ with $A,B$ strictly positive formulas. In particular, the new calculi do not use (multi)sets nor nested sequents.
 For both ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ it is shown that the cut-rule is admissible. As a consequence, it is proven that the calculi are deductively equivalent to $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The cutfree systems are used to prove uniform interpolation for the two reflection calculi.
 In addition, ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ is used to give a syntactic proof of Dashkov's Theorem to the extent that $\mathsf{RC}_1$ is the strictly positive fragment of the provability logic ${\mathsf{GL}}$.
 The paper also introduces non-analytic calculi that are conceptually easier but proof-theoretically behave badly. It is shown that even those systems allow direct cut-elimination: the benefits of the strict positivity outweigh the draw-backs of a non-analytic calculus in these cases.
When Pedal Shapes Come Back: a Complex Story

Under the usual nondegeneracy assumptions, repeatedly projecting a fixed point onto the side lines of an $n$-gon returns its shape after $n$ steps. We explain this classical theorem through a short complex-number identity: the multipliers of one step move cyclically around the polygon. The same calculation allows a different common angle of projection at each step. A sharp angle-dependent contraction bound identifies the incircle centre as the maximiser for tangential polygons. In space, even a regular tetrahedron can fail to recover its shape after four steps. We give an exact example, then show how concentric inscribed and circumscribed spheres restore a two-step return. Rectangular boxes provide a further four-step family.

We compute the resonance varieties of the Orlik--Solomon algebras of Schubert matroids. Previously known results have been largely confined to matroids of rank $3$, and the Schubert matroids give a family of nontrivial examples of arbitrary rank. We give an expression for the cohomology of the Orlik--Solomon algebra that we show holds for Schubert matroids as well as for simple, complex-realizable rank-$3$ matroids that do not support multinets. Our proof introduces a family of matroids for which the Orlik--Solomon algebra is isomorphic to an exterior Stanley--Reisner algebra.
Varieties of associative algebras with slow central codimension growth
Antonio Ioppolo; Wesley Quaresma Cota; Ana Cristina Vieira

Central codimensions measure the dimensions of spaces of multilinear polynomials modulo those taking values in the center of an algebra. We classify associative algebras over a field of characteristic zero whose central codimensions grow at most linearly. The classification is given up to equality of polynomial identities, in terms of explicit generating algebras and an equivalent finite exclusion criterion. We also give a direct structural characterization of the bounded case. As a consequence, we determine the five varieties of quadratic central codimension growth whose proper subvarieties all have at most linear central growth. As an application of the bounded-growth classification, we characterize algebras graded by an arbitrary finite group whose graded central codimensions are bounded. Up to graded PI-equivalence, these are direct sums of commutative and nilpotent graded algebras, possibly together with the Grassmann algebra on two generators endowed with the trivial grading.

Starting from a positive integer, repeatedly halve the current value, rounding up or down. Which resulting sequences have terms that add to the starting integer? A simple balance identity turns the rounding choices into hyperbinary expansions, in which each power of two occurs at most twice. This correspondence gives exact counts by length and an injection into the expansions counted by Stern's diatomic sequence. We characterize equality in the resulting bound by the binary digits of the odd part of the integer. We also determine the unique longest partition and give a short recursive counting algorithm. When the required total is allowed to vary, the chain counts eventually equal Stern's number, and we determine the exact threshold. A direct proof shows that the counts of hyperbinary expansions in the three length classes modulo three differ by at most one. For sufficiently long halving partitions, the counts by length first weakly increase and then weakly decrease, although the full sequence need not do so.
Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. III

This paper is the third in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices of size $n\times k$ with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough.
 In this part we study the remaining case where $k = 3$ and $n \ge k + 2 = 5$ and prove that every linear map preserving the Cullis' determinant admits the same description as for the case where $k \ge 4$ and $n \ge k + 2$ obtained previously.

Chow associated with every finite multigraph $G$ a symplectic matroid $\GraphS{G}$ on the signed edge set $E\sqcup E^{*}$, whose restrictions to transversals are frame matroids of signed graphs, and Sarvepalli asked which of these matroids are representable. For a connected graph containing a cycle, we show that every isotropic representation of $S(G)$ admits an incidence-flow normal form. The remaining representation conditions are expressed through its admissible minors. Consequently, if $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable, then the bridgeless part of $G$ has a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow. In characteristic other than two, $\GraphS{G}$ is representable if and only if every non-loop edge on a cycle has a parallel mate. In characteristic two, we characterize the loopless graphs without two vertex-disjoint cycles by the existence of a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow, and we show that rigidly linked short cycles, and hence subdivisions of the prism, are obstructions. For $3$-connected simple graphs this gives a complete answer: $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable if and only if $\F$ has characteristic two, $G$ has no two vertex-disjoint cycles, and either $|\F|>2$ or $G\cong K_5$. In particular, the matroid of the Petersen graph is representable over no field. Finally, the admissible corank--nullity polynomial of an arbitrary symplectic matroid is intrinsic and satisfies a three-term contraction identity. For graphical symplectic matroids, this becomes a deletion-contraction recursion that closes up once marked vertices are allowed, and polynomials built from enveloping matroids agree with it exactly for sheltering envelopes.
How Much Can Approximate Equilibria Change the Social Cost of Selfish Routing?

We study approximate Nash equilibria in nonatomic congestion games, with the goal of understanding how much the social cost can change when the equilibrium condition is relaxed. We consider $ε$-approximate Nash equilibria ($ε$-NE), in which each player uses a strategy whose cost is at most $1 + ε$ times the minimum available cost. We compare the social costs of $ε$-NE and exact Nash equilibria. This lets us quantify, for example, how much a navigation app can reduce total travel time when drivers tolerate routes slightly slower than the fastest available route.
 For degree-$d$ polynomial latencies in both general nonatomic congestion games and single-commodity routing games on series-parallel networks, we give tight lower and upper bounds on the relative change in social cost from an exact Nash equilibrium to any $ε$-NE, with matching instances for every $ε$. For small $ε$, the largest possible relative reduction and increase in general congestion games are both $Θ(\sqrt{dε})$, independently of the number of resources and populations. In contrast, on series-parallel networks of depth $h$, the largest possible relative reduction is $Θ(hε)$, while the largest possible relative increase is known to be $ε$. For the classes of games we study, these results give a tight and quantitative characterization of the possible changes in social cost and establish a separation between general and series-parallel networks.
The Lorentz Threshold in Fourier Restriction

Classical Stein--Tomas restriction controls a Fourier transform on a curved surface, but the estimate changes when its values lie in a Banach space. We determine the sharp Lorentz threshold at the critical exponent $4/3$: for coefficients in $\ell_D^{4/3,q}$, the optimal Gaussian restriction constant grows like $(1+\log D)^{|3/4-1/q|}$. A multiscale wave-packet construction proves sharpness, including the delicate index $q=2$. The same threshold holds for fractional Gaussian noise, while Gaussian type and cotype alone do not distinguish the positive and negative cases. As a dispersive consequence, we establish a sharp Lorentz-channel spacetime estimate for linear capillary waves.
Partial coactions of Hopf algebras on nonunital algebras and categories
Marcelo Muniz Alves; Tiago Luiz Ferrazza

In this paper, we introduce and investigate partial coactions of a Hopf algebra on an associative, possibly nonunital algebra and on $\Bbbk$-linear categories. We prove that every partial coaction has a globalization in a broad sense. We study in detail the case of a partial coaction on an algebra with local units; we prove that such a coaction is always induced from a global coaction, and we show that there exists a naturally associated $\Bbbk$-linear category endowed with a partial coaction.
Enriched Surface Thermodynamics for Sharp-Interface Fluid Models

A sharp interface can retain material and structural information about an unresolved fluid transition zone. We formulate a local thermodynamic framework for isotropic surfaces carrying constituent surface mass densities and a thickness descriptor. The distinction between densities of additive contents and internal descriptors determines the area conjugate, reversible surface stress, and Gibbs-Duhem relation. A volume-per-area thickness has a pressure-like conjugate, a mechanical work contribution, and a separate evolution equation. Independent, constrained, and rapidly equilibrating thicknesses require different kinematics and reductions. Material storage can be retained without retaining surface inertia.
 The balances and entropy production specify admissible exchange and structural relaxation. For a moving surface patch, an available-free-energy identity accounts for mechanical power and for the contributions of material and structural fluxes across its boundary. Equilibrium reduction retains the production and transport needed to follow the reduced state. An explicit mass-thickness free energy has a positive-definite material Hessian and gives coupled adsorption, expansion, compression, and dissipative relaxation. Pressure response yields conditional restrictions on reduced states and demonstrates that distinct independent and constrained states can share an entire pressure-tension curve. Geometric thickness realizations and finite-rate transfer are treated with their associated mechanical and balance requirements. The framework separates state selection, constitutive closure, reduction, and identification from observations.
Paolo Mantero; Matthew Mastroeni; Jason McCullough

We give a complete classification of all Koszul licci ideals, including a complete description of the defining equations and graded Betti tables for these ideals, showing that they exactly correspond to quadratic licci ideals that are at most two links away from a complete intersection. More generally, we show how to uniquely associate the Hilbert function of a quadratic licci ideal to a partition of its codimension, and use it to prove that the Hilbert function of a quadratic ideal determines whether or not it is licci. This provides a strong affirmative answer in the quadratic case to a question of Huneke, Polini, and Ulrich asking whether graded Betti tables determine the licci property of graded ideals.
Himani Sharma; Adam Sikora; Sundaram Thangavelu

We investigate the $L^p$ norm convergence of Bochner-Riesz means $S_R^δf$, $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^+,dμ_β)$ associated to Laguerre expansions of type $β\geq -1/2$. For any given $1 < p < \infty$ and $β> -1/2$, we provide a complete characterisation of the order $δ$ for which these means are uniformly bounded on $L^p$ spaces. A particularly noteworthy phenomenon arises for $-1/3 <β<0$, where the admissible $(p, δ)$ region differs substantially from those for $ -1/2 \leq β\leq -1/3$ or $β\geq 0$. Interestingly, the convergence for $-1/3 < β<0$ is an interaction between the ranges $ -1/2 \leq β\leq -1/3$ and $β\geq 0$.
Optimal Conversion from Zero-Concentrated to Gaussian Differential Privacy
Yu-Wei Chen; Aaradhya Pandey; Jordan Awan

Gaussian differential privacy (GDP) and zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP) are two competing privacy accounting frameworks, but they share similar minimax lower bounds in various estimation problems. Moreover, it is known that a mechanism satisfying $μ$-GDP satisfies $(μ^2/2)$-zCDP, whereas the converse fails to hold at the same calibration. In this paper, we establish the optimal reverse conversion, showing that every $ρ$-zCDP mechanism satisfies $μ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)$-GDP, where $μ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)=2Φ^{-1}((1+e^{-t_ρ})^{-1})$ and $t_ρ$ uniquely solves the equation $ρ=t_ρ\tanh(t_ρ/2)$. We also obtain simplified bounds $\sqrt{πρ}\leqμ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)\leq\sqrt{8ρ}$, with sharp constants, which imply equivalence of the two frameworks up to constants. This explains why their minimax risks agree up to a constant rescaling of the privacy budget. We show that the squared conversion is strictly convex, which implies that converting zCDP to GDP before applying composition or group privacy yields a tighter GDP guarantee than converting afterward. We also derive the sharp conversion from bounded-range and logistic DP mechanisms (e.g., exponential mechanism) to GDP, where converting before composition but after group privacy gives the tighter guarantee.
Adaptive Optimizers Can Get a Policy Ranking Wrong: Momentum, Dependent Data, and a Two-Run Remedy

Operators choosing among decision rules, such as when a battery charges or where an idle taxi goes, rank them by estimated long-run value. A standard estimator, linear temporal-difference (TD) learning, fits values from one stream of correlated observations. Large fits often use an adaptive optimizer, such as adaptive moment estimation (Adam), with fixed averaging rates. We show that these rates can change what is estimated, not just how fast: the same observations drive the updates and the optimizer's step-size scaling, moving the fit away from the intended TD value. The shift differs across rules, so it need not cancel in a comparison, and more data only makes a wrong ranking look more certain. Our remedy refits the same data at a second averaging rate that halves the effective gain, the number to which the leading shift is proportional. Twice the new fit minus the original removes that shift. In New York taxi and battery models calibrated to real data, common optimizer settings leave the selected rule unchanged but order close rules wrongly and misstate its value. Our remedy corrects nearly every wrong ordering, with one extra fit when the shift is moderate and two when it is larger.
Hodge theory and topology of Bogomolov--Guan manifolds
Nikon Kurnosov; Ángel David Ríos Ortiz

Bogomolov--Guan manifolds are simply connected, irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds that are not Kähler, yet they echo hyperkähler geometry in striking ways. We show that their Frölicher spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ and that their Hodge numbers are stable under small deformations. The general fibers of their natural Lagrangian fibration are rationally null-homologous, and the Beauville--Bogomolov--Fujiki form is degenerate. Despite this, in every dimension, the Euler characteristics agree with those of generalized Kummer manifolds. In dimensions four and six, we compute the full Hodge diamonds and all Chern and Pontryagin numbers. Surprisingly, these characteristic numbers are the same as the generalized Kummer ones, even though the Betti numbers differ and the Hodge diamonds are asymmetric.
Density functionals for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
Mihály A. Csirik; Andre Laestadius; Markus Penz; Erik I. Tellgren

We develop a density-functional theory for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian of nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics in the spirit of the convex-analytic formulation of Lieb. We consider finitely many electrons, subject to external scalar and vector potentials, coupled to the full continuum of massless transverse photons with an ultraviolet cutoff. The natural basic variables are the standard electron density and a combined current density, the sum of the paramagnetic current density and a field-induced current density generated by the quantized vector potential. We prove representability results for these density-current pairs and show that the mixed-state constrained-search functional attains its infimum and coincides with the Lieb functional obtained by convex conjugation. Since arbitrarily soft photons purify mixed states at a negligible energy cost without changing their density and combined current density, the pure-state Levy-Lieb functional equals the Lieb functional and is therefore convex, even though its infimum need not be attained. In addition, we establish the zero-coupling limit, which recovers the mixed-state Vignale-Rasolt functional of current-density-functional theory. Finally, we consider the long-wavelength (dipole) limit and show that the limiting functional can be written as a constrained search for the well-known length-gauge dipole Hamiltonian.
Entanglement for elliptic curve group orders
Francesco Campagna; Nathan Jones; Francesco Pappalardi; Peter Stevenhagen

For an elliptic curve $E$ defined over a number field $K$ and $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime of good reduction of $E/K$, we let $n_\mathfrak{p}=\#E(k_\mathfrak{p})$ be the order of the group of points over the residue class field $k_\mathfrak{p}$. Divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by a prime $\ell$ depends on the splitting behavior of $\mathfrak{p}$ in the $\ell$-division field $K(E[\ell](\bar{K}))$ of $E$ and, generically, divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by different primes $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ are `independent events' on the set of primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of good reduction. However, there do exist elliptic curves with `entangled division fields' for which infinitely many $n_\mathfrak{p}$ are coprime to $\ell_1$ and infinitely many $n_\mathfrak{p}$ are coprime to $\ell_2$, but no $n_\mathfrak{p}$ is coprime to to $\ell_1 \ell_2$. For $\ell_1=2$, we classify in group theoretical terms the entanglement giving rise to this behavior, and count up to isomorphism the number of `special $2\ell$-division groups' exhibiting the phenomenon. A final section shows how such groups may be realized as the Galois group of $2\ell$ division fields for elliptic curves $E/\mathbf{Q}$.
On the growth of weak regular partitions in k-uniform hypergraphs

This paper classifies hereditary properties of k-uniform hypergraphs according to bounds in the weak hypergraph regularity lemma first developed by Chung. Specifically, we prove the bounds must grow at a constant, polynomial, exponential, or tower rate. This generalizes work in the 3-uniform case by the second author.
Fermat curves and explicit class field theory for real quadratic number fields

We use Fermat curves with real multiplication and classical CM theory to construct an explicit class field theory for arbitrary real quadratic number fields. The underlying strategy is well-established in computational class field theory, our main contribution is a geometric model to realize this strategy explicitly. This approach complements the recent breakthrough works solving conjectures by Brumer, Stark and Shintani and gives an alternative constructive solution to Hilbert's 12th problem for real quadratic fields.
Online Autotuning of Algebraic Multigrid via Contextual Bandits and Reinforcement Learning
Xudong He; Ruiyu Wang; Yilang Ding; Rui Peng Li; Yuanzhe Xi

Algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are widely used for solving large sparse linear systems, but their efficiency depends strongly on interacting setup and solve parameters. Effective parameter choices typically depend on the problem. We develop a phase-aware online autotuning method for hypre's BoomerAMG to reduce cumulative time-to-solution over sequences of related linear systems. A LinUCB-based contextual bandit selects mixed-type parameters for AMG hierarchy construction using a shared cost model over PDE descriptors and configuration encodings. A recursive LSTDQ controller uses residual and timing observations to estimate the AMG solve time within each attempt and adapt relaxation weights between multigrid cycles. Both learners update from ongoing solves without offline pretraining. Across grids of sizes $40^3$, $60^3$, and $80^3$, the joint autotuning method reduces total runtime, including recurring learner computation, by 36.1-43.3% for diffusion problems and 19.8-31.0% for diffusion-advection problems over sequences of 5000 linear systems, relative to the reference BoomerAMG default configuration. On a variable-flow diffusion-advection benchmark comprising 30,000 systems on a $60^3$ grid, 2 systems fail to converge with joint autotuning, compared with 1677 for the reference configuration, under their respective attempt budgets.
Casson invariant of knots defined by random braids

We investigate the expectation $E(v_2)$ of the Casson invariant $v_2$ for knots represented by two similar types of braids, the rosette $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $\prod_{1\leq 2i\leq s}σ_{2i}^{\pm 1}\prod_{1\leq 2i+\leq s}σ_{2i+1}^{\pm 1}$ and the quasitoric $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $σ_{1}^{\pm 1}σ_{2}^{\pm 1}...σ_{s-1}^{\pm 1}$. If $k$ is of the form $ns+1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{s+1}{24}$ where $c$ is the number of crossing points of braid; if $k$ is of the form $ns-1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{5-s}{24}$.\\ If we go through all $3$-braids, regardless of the shape of their diagram, we get $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{8}$. \\ For knots with a checkerboard diagram, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{16}$.
Lyapunov functions for the Langevin equation with dissipative damping

We study the well-posedness and the large time stability of the Langevin equation in the presence of potentials and dissipative damping together with additive white noise. While the confining potential is assumed to be smooth, the nonlinear damping is allowed to have either polynomial growth or singular behaviors. We construct novel Lyapunov functions and determine the corresponding parameter regimes that lead to global well-posedness or finite-time explosion. These Lyapunov functions also allow for deriving quantitative mixing rates toward equilibrium. Our results extend existing ergodic theory established for the instance of nonlinear damping satisfying suitable integrability conditions.
Cartesian closedness of lax comma categories
Maria Manuel Clementino; Fernando Lucatelli Nunes

For a finitely complete category X, we prove that the lax comma category Cat//X is cartesian closed if and only if its free coproduct completion Fam(X) is cartesian closed. The proof uses a change-of-base theorem: postcomposition with a functor induces a left adjoint between lax comma categories precisely when that functor is a left multiadjoint. We describe the exponentials and derive examples from known results on family categories.
Fluid Limits and Upper Bounds for Randomized Greedy Matching

The Modified Randomized Greedy (MRG) algorithm [Tinhofer (1984), Aronson-Dyer-Frieze-Suen (1995)] is a classical greedy algorithm for finding approximate maximum matchings. MRG repeatedly picks a uniformly random unmatched vertex and matches it to a uniformly random unmatched neighbor, if one exists. Since 1991, the best upper bound on its approximation ratio has been $2/3$, given by the Bomb graphs of [Dyer and Frieze (1991)]. We improve this bound to $0.6569$ on general graphs and $0.6607$ on bipartite graphs.
 Our constructions consist of copies of small gadgets, with specified vertex classes joined completely. We track each algorithm by counting gadget copies with each possible configuration of remaining vertices. Wormald's differential equation method [Wormald (1995)] shows that these counts, scaled by the size parameter of the construction, converge to a deterministic trajectory known as the \textit{fluid limit}, which is described by ordinary differential equations. This fluid limit approximation holds while the relevant vertex classes have positive density, and so we devise a separate counting argument determines the contribution from the end of the run.
 Furthermore, we apply our framework to Random Decision Order (RDO), in which vertices are processed in uniformly random order and choose unmatched neighbors according to fixed adversarial preferences. On bipartite graphs, we determine the exact limiting ratio on the Double-Bomb family of [Tang-Wu-Zhang (2020)]. Its minimum is $31/48$, confirming their numerical estimate of about $0.646$.On general graphs, we improve their upper bound of $5/8$, given by the paw graph, to $0.5946$ on a new family. Finally, we give one possible explanation for why $2/3$ seemed to be optimal for MRG in the concluding remarks.
An Incidence-Based Edge-Averaged Method for Convection-Diffusion Problems on Polytopal Meshes
James H. Adler; Xiaozhe Hu; Seulip Lee; Eoghan O'Keefe

We develop an incidence-based edge-averaged method for scalar convection-diffusion problems on convex polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimensions. The proposed method extends the classical edge-averaged finite-element scheme through a graph-theoretic formulation based on vertex-edge incidence matrices. We first establish this formulation on simplices in arbitrary dimensions and then extend it to convex polytopes by introducing complementary edges and generalized barycentric coordinates. A key ingredient is a matrix identity that relates the generalized Whitney edge mass matrix to a diagonal representation of the Poisson stiffness matrix, enabling an exponentially-fitted discretization expressed entirely in terms of nodal values and edge weights. We prove that the resulting stiffness matrix is a nonsingular $M$-matrix under suitable positivity and connectivity conditions, ensuring monotonicity and the discrete maximum principle. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional simplicial and nonsimplicial meshes demonstrate first-order convergence in the $H^1$ semi-norm and stable, nonoscillatory solutions in convection-dominated regimes.
Coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity from a universal cumulant lifting

Using probabilistic methods, we establish universal cumulant lifting criteria for Stieltjes and Hamburger moment sequences. In the Stieltjes case, we characterize coefficientwise Hankel total positivity after convolution with every initial moment sequence by requiring each once-shifted cumulant sequence to be Stieltjes. We also prove equivalence with the numerical moment property at every nonnegative intensity. In the Hamburger case, we use twice-shifted cumulants to obtain coefficientwise-positive leading Hankel determinants, a degree bound, an explicit highest-degree component, and drift invariance. We work with formal series and require neither exponential moments nor moment determinacy. We establish composition, binomial-convolution, and substitution results, and apply them to implicit equations and autonomous differential equations, tree and forest families, and lognormal compound-Poisson moments in a unified approach. From known moment sequences, we obtain general coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive families containing the classical Bessel, Lah, and Laguerre polynomials. We not only give new proofs of coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity of many combinatorial polynomials, but also prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity for the component polynomials of functional digraphs confirming a conjecture of Sokal and establish fixed-shape Schläfli--Gessel--Seo polynomials positivity supporting another conjecture of Sokal.
On Wagstaff primes in the $k$-Pell number sequence

A Wagstaff prime is a prime number of the form $(2^{\mathfrak{p}}+1)/3$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is an odd prime. For an integer $k\ge 2$, the sequence of $k$-generalized Pell numbers $\bigl(P_n^{(k)}\bigr)_{n\ge 2-k}$ is the linear recurrence of order $k$ given by $P_n^{(k)}=2P_{n-1}^{(k)}+P_{n-2}^{(k)}+\cdots+P_{n-k}^{(k)}$ for $n\ge 2$, with initial values $P_{2-k}^{(k)}=\cdots=P_{0}^{(k)}=0$ and $P_1^{(k)}=1$. For $k=2$ this is the classical Pell sequence. Motivated by the recent determination of the Wagstaff primes in the $k$-Fibonacci and $k$-Lucas sequences, we study the exponential Diophantine equation $P_n^{(k)}=(2^{\mathfrak{p}}+1)/3$ in positive integers $n,k$ and an odd prime $\mathfrak{p}\geq 3$, with $k\ge 2$. We show that this equation has no solutions, that is no $k$-Pell number is a Wagstaff prime. The proof combines linear forms in logarithms of algebraic numbers with reduction based on the theory of continued fractions, together with a computational verification in the remaining finite range.
Optimal AB-program for Poincaré--Sobolev and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on hyperbolic spaces
Anh Do; Debdip Ganguly; Nguyen Lam; Guozhen Lu

In this paper, we prove that we can subtract the full spectral gap $\left(\frac{N-1}{p}\right)^{p}$ of the $p$-Laplacian and keep the sharp Sobolev constant $S(N,p)$ of $\mathbb{R}^N$ at the same time in a large family of $p$. For $p=2$, this was proved by Benguria, Frank and Loss in dimension three, and it was shown by Hebey to be false in dimensions $N\geq4$. For $p\neq2$, it was proved by Nguyen for $N\geq4$ and $\frac{2N}{N-1}\leq p<N$. By employing, among other tools, a suitable conjugation that maps the radial $p$-Dirichlet integral on $\mathbb{H}^N$ onto its Euclidean counterpart on $\mathbb{R}^N$ while preserving the $L^p$ norm, together with a one-dimensional tangent line inequality, we establish such sharp Poincaré--Sobolev inequalities for $N=3$ and $2\leq p<3$, for $N=4$ and $\frac{1+\sqrt{13}}{2}\leq p<4$, and for $N\geq5$ and $\min\{3,\frac{1+\sqrt{4N-3}}{2}\}\leq p<N$. In particular, in all cases we also obtain an explicit remainder term. Moreover, since the change of function keeps the $L^p$ norm, we prove the sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with the full spectral gap and the sharp Euclidean constant for $N=3$ and $2\leq p\leq3$, and for $N\geq4$ on an explicit interval of $p$. For $p\geq3$, we also use the change of variable $t=\sinhρ$ and the Hardy inequality, which give a second remainder term. At the endpoint $p=N$, this remainder gives a Hardy--Trudinger--Moser inequality on $\mathbb{H}^N$ under a weaker constraint than the one of Liang, Lu, Wang and Yang, in every dimension $N\geq3$. Finally, we show that for $1<p<\frac{1+\sqrt{4N-3}}{2}$, which includes all $1<p<2$, the full spectral gap can still be subtracted with some positive constant in front of the Sobolev term, and that this constant is smaller than $S(N,p)^{p}$ when $p<\min\{2,\sqrt N\}$. Together with our other results, this shows that the full spectral gap can be subtracted for every $1<p<N$.
Nonlinear Dynamics in Periodically Distributed Fibre Amplification Systems
Sunday O. Atuba; Boris A. Malomed

We investigate effects of longitudinally varying nonlinearity on periodically distributed amplification systems in optical fibres. Emphasis is made on configurations in which the nonlinear coefficient exponentially grows or decays along the propagation distance, while the group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) coefficient is held constant. Such systems are of practical relevance to the design of highly efficient nonlinear devices, including broadband light sources and advanced amplification schemes, where precise management of the interplay between the GVD, nonlinearity, and gain is essential. Adopting the known generic integrability condition, we derive exact analytical expressions for the evolution of the optical field in the presence of the tailored nonlinearity profiles and periodically distributed gain. The resulting periodic wavetrain solutions and their long-wave limit in the form of bright and dark solitons provide insight into the controlled enhancement or suppression of nonlinear effects under realistic amplification conditions. The robustness of these solutions is examined by introducing finite perturbations and directly evaluating their effects on the corresponding intensity profiles. The structural stability of solutions against deviations from the integrability condition is demonstrated too. Outcomes of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the nonlinear pulse dynamics in engineered gain-managed fibres and offer guidance for the development of novel optical systems, where the spatial distribution of the nonlinearity is exploited to optimise the performance.
A study on v-numbers of $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(L,M/I^nN)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(L,M/I^nN)$
Sayed Sadiqul Islam; Lisa Mandal; Samarendra Sahoo

Let $R$ be a Noetherian $\mathbb{N}$-graded ring. Assume that $L$ and $M$ are finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}$-graded $R$-module, and $I$ a homogeneous ideal of $R$. Let $N$ be a graded submodule of $M$. Fix $k\in \mathbb{N}$. Denote $H:=\operatorname{Ext}^k_R(L,M)$ (or $\operatorname{Tor}_k^R(L,M)$) and $H_n:=\operatorname{Ext}^k_R(L, M/I^nN)$ (or $\operatorname{Tor}_k^R(L,M/I^nN)$). When $I$ is generated by elements of positive degree, we show that the local $v$-number of $H_n$ either coincides with that of colon submodule $(0:_H I)$ or is a polynomial in $n$ of degree one whose leading coefficient is one of the degrees of the generators of $I$. This extends the main result of Ghosh-Pramanik [J. Algebra 671 (2025), 61-74], where asymptotic linearity was shown under the assumption that $(0:_H I)=0$.
Lower Bounds on Inference Complexity for Polyak-Ruppert Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent
Denis Belomestny; Alexey Naumov; Sergey Samsonov

In this paper, we establish sharp lower bounds for Gaussian approximation of Polyak-Ruppert averaged stochastic gradient descent with polynomially decreasing step sizes. For every fixed exponent $γ\in(1/2,1)$, a single one-dimensional smooth, strongly convex example has approximation error with the limiting variance of order $n^{1/2-γ}+n^{γ-1}$ in Kolmogorov and convex distances. This matches the existing upper bound throughout the range of $γ$. The nonlinear bias contributes $n^{1/2-γ}$ even when the Gaussian reference uses the finite linearized variance. We also derive a lower bound of order $n^{-(1-γ)/2}$ for the relative mean error of estimating the limiting variance from one SGD trajectory, uniformly over a scalar quadratic family. With the limiting variance known, achieving approximation error $\varepsilon$ on this example takes order $\varepsilon^{-4}$ iterations for the best choice $γ=3/4$. Achieving both Gaussian approximation and relative mean variance-estimation errors at most $\varepsilon$ uniformly over the model class requires at least order $\varepsilon^{-6}$ iterations for every fixed $γ$.

A player's impatient valuation of an infinite stream of stage payoffs is a weighted average with nonincreasing weights. Such valuations generalize geometric discounting and allow imprecise or heterogeneous time preferences. For a stochastic game \(Γ\) and a profile \(u\) of impatient valuations, let \(Γ_u\) be the induced game. We ask when approximately optimal or equilibrium behavior can be chosen to vary continuously and stably with \(u\).
 We show that this robustness is governed by the corresponding uniform long-run payoff property: the uniform value in the adversary case, and uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs in the equilibrium case. In finite state spaces, the latter is equivalent to the usual existence of a uniform equilibrium payoff.
 In the two-player zero-sum case, if \(Γ\) has a uniform value, then the value of \(Γ_u\) varies uniformly continuously with \(u\), and for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a uniformly continuous mapping assigning to each \(u\) an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal strategy in \(Γ_u\). Hence this holds for every finite two-player zero-sum stochastic game.
 In the non-zero-sum case, uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs imply a finite cover of the valuation-profile space by neighborhoods on each of which a single strategy profile is a robust \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium.
 For sunspot, correlated, and extensive-form correlated equilibria, uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs are equivalent to the existence, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), of a uniformly continuous mapping assigning to each valuation profile a robust \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium on a neighborhood of that profile. Consequently, every finite stochastic game admits uniformly continuous robust extensive-form correlated \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium selections.
Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
A. B. Aleksandrov; V. V. Peller

In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.
Enumeration of plane hypermaps with a mixed boundary II

A plane hypermap with a boundary is a connected graph embedded in the plane with a distinguished face, and whose inner faces are properly face-bicolored. We say that such hypermaps are k-alternating if the colors of the faces adjacent to the distinguished face alternate at most 2k times when going counterclockwise. Eynard and Orantin, in [EO2005], have found a universal expression for the generating functions of k-alternating hypermaps as a surprisingly simple function of the generating function of 1-alternating hypermaps. In this article, we will provide combinatorial formulas for k-alternating hypermaps using specific subclasses of hypermaps in which each vertex can either be connected to a previously marked vertex, called accessible, or connected to all other vertices in what we call a blob. In particular, this method will allow us to derive the results from [EO2005] from a combinatorial perspective, and we anticipate that it will lead to the computation of asymptotics for hypermaps in future work. This article is naturally a sequel to, and most importantly a generalization of, the results in [BEL26], which deals essentially with the case of 1- and 2-alternating hypermaps.

These notes cover the material of two courses given at SISSA, Trieste, in the academic years 2023-2024 and 2025-2026, together with some material from courses taught in other recent years. The original idea behind these courses emerged from conversations with Andrea Causin and Margherita Solci about the somewhat elusive notion of `multiscale behaviour', which arises in the study of variational problems involving one or more small parameters. Two main mechanisms govern their asymptotic behaviour: concentration and oscillations. Their description is often associated with the emergence of a characteristic `scale', quantifying either the speed of concentration or the period of an optimal oscillation. These mechanisms may originate from different variational principles and may occur separately, coexist, compete, or interact, thus providing a natural interpretation of the term `multiscale'. This perspective inspired the informal title of the courses, which also became the title of these notes.
 The natural framework for these analyses is $Γ$-convergence. However, these notes are not intended as a general introduction to this now well-established theory. We provide only a brief account of the techniques relevant to our purposes, referring the reader to the author's book chapter {\em A Handbook of $Γ$-convergence}. For a broader introduction to $Γ$-convergence, and in particular to its topological properties, the standard reference is Dal Maso's monograph {\em An Introduction to $Γ$-convergence}.

We study the Seshadri function on the ample cone of a smooth complex projective surface at a fixed point. At a submaximal class, we show that the function is differentiable if and only if there is a unique Seshadri curve. At a maximal class $L$, differentiability is equivalent to every curve $C$ computing the Seshadri constant satisfying $\frac{[C]}{{\rm mult}_x C}=\frac{[L]}{\sqrt{L^{2}}}$. We also prove that the non-differentiability locus is nowhere dense.
 For the blow-up of $\mathbb P^{2}$ at $r\ge 9$ very general points, assuming the $(-1)$-curves conjecture for the blow-up at $r+1$ very general points, we construct a non-empty open subset of the ample cone on which the Seshadri function at a very general point equals $\sqrt{L^{2}}$. Consequently, this function is not piecewise linear. Under the assumption of the Strong SHGH conjecture, we obtain a common non-empty open subset on which maximality holds at every point when $r\ge36$.
Local superderivations of Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$

We prove that every even or odd local superderivation of the Block Lie superalgebra $S(q)$ is a superderivation for every $q\in\mathbb{C}$, with both basis indices ranging over $\mathbb{Z}$. The superderivations used in the local condition have the same parity as the map. The proofs use the known description of homogeneous superderivations, bracket computations, and coefficient comparisons.
Local and global conservation laws of partial differential equations on moving domains in three dimensions
Alexey F. Shevyakov; Stephen C. Anco

For PDE systems in three spatial dimensions, firstly, a review of the various types of global conservation laws --- volumetric, surface-flux, circulatory --- is given using vector calculus, and their corresponding local forms --- divergence, curl, gradient --- are explained. Secondly, an extension of each type of conservation law to moving domains is presented, where the domain --- volume, surface, curve --- is transported by a prescribed velocity field. This provides a generalization of Reynolds' transport theorem known for material domains in which the velocity field is the fluid velocity. The main results are illustrated by numerous physical examples taken from gas dynamics, fluid flow, nonlinear acoustics, chemotaxis, plasma dynamics, and also Maxwell's equations, which do not involve any physically specified velocity field. As an additional main result, an extension of the multiplier method for finding local conservation laws of divergence-type is presented for local curl-type and gradient-type conservation laws on both static and moving domains.
Some Characterisations of the Strichartz Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group

Recently, Thangavelu introduced a scalar-valued Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group, built from the joint spectral theory of the sublaplacian and the central vector field. Around the same time, Krukowski characterised the classical Fourier transform on various groups from a small number of structural properties, paired with a normalisation hypothesis. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the Strichartz Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Here, the spectral property is formulated jointly for the sublaplacian and the central vector field, and the translation property is based on a twisted form of left translation. The joint spectral property, paired with the twisted translation property and a normalisation at a single explicit test function, characterises the Strichartz Fourier transform on each ray of the underlying spectral set, the Heisenberg fan. The twisted translation property alone, paired with a Dirac delta property, already suffices. We also characterise the radial kernel of the transform on each ray by a Laguerre-type differential equation.
Magnetic norm inflation below the velocity regularity threshold for viscous non-resistive MHD

We study viscous, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamics on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. For every fixed magnetic exponent $s>d/2$ and every velocity exponent $q<s-1$, we prove norm inflation at the origin in $H^q\times H^s$. Arbitrarily small divergence-free Schwartz data generate classical solutions whose magnetic $H^s$ norm becomes arbitrarily large at arbitrarily small positive times, while the velocity remains arbitrarily small in $H^q$ throughout the observation interval. Together with endpoint local well-posedness, this identifies $q=s-1$ as the sharp lower velocity threshold for fixed $s>d/2$. The construction uses a symmetric pair of high-frequency velocity packets and a fixed low-frequency magnetic profile. A Fourier component of their stretching interaction has a fixed sign and gains the power $K^{s-1-q}$ on a short diffusive time scale. Subtracting an exact reference flow and using endpoint Besov estimates controls the full nonlinear remainder. Quantitative higher-order estimates ensure existence through the observation time and yield the uniform smallness of the velocity in the target norm.

We extend the non-backtracking Laplacian for graphs, introduced by Jost, Mulas and Torres, to hypergraphs. The operator is defined on the permutations of the edges and is normalized by the number of edges through which a non-backtracking walk can continue. We show that it satisfies a symmetry that generalizes the graph case, and that it can be obtained from the random walk Laplacian of a directed graph by rescaling if and only if all edges have the same cardinality. Moreover, we show that, up to copies of the eigenvalue $1$, its spectrum can be computed from a much smaller matrix indexed by the incidences of the hypergraph, and we use this reduction to bound the remaining eigenvalues away from $1$.
Semiclassical Wave Packet Dynamics For Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations with Harmonic Potentials

We propose an approximate Hamiltonian dynamics for the Gross--Pitaevskii equation $i\hbarψ_t = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}Δψ+ V(x)ψ+ \hbar^2 λ|ψ|^2ψ$ with harmonic potential $V(x)$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. We do this by extending the Gaussian ansatz of Perez-Garcia et al.~(Phys.~Rev.~A 56, 1424 (1997)) to the semiclassical wave packets of Hagedorn. We derive the evolution equations for the wave packets from the Hamiltonian/symplectic perspective, rather than the Lagrangian/variational one taken by Perez-Garcia et al. We first show that these two perspectives yield identical evolution equations in the Gaussian case. We then derive the evolution equations for an arbitrary element of the semiclassical wave packets. Finally, we demonstrate the efficacy of the approximate dynamics with numerical experiments.
Digital Twin-Assisted Fast Beam Alignment for mmWave MIMO Networks

Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication relies on directional beam sweeping for initial access, which incurs substantial latency and signaling overhead as antenna arrays grow large and deployments become denser. Machine-learning-based beam prediction can reduce this overhead, but its effectiveness depends on training data that accurately reflects the deployment environment, a requirement that is difficult to meet in practice. This paper presents a latency-aware beam management architecture that integrates digital-twin-assisted prediction, regionbased localization, weighted ensemble learning, and explainability-driven beam pruning into a unified framework. A digital twin (DT) generates site-specific ray-traced channel knowledge offline, enabling environment-aware beam prediction without exhaustive real-world measurements and supporting both initial access and beam tracking. The proposed ensemble learning scheme combines a base classifier and a specialist classifier through reliability-weighted fusion to improve prediction accuracy and robustness, while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based attribution pruning reduces the beam codebook to a small subset of the most informative beams for beam allocation. To capture the distributional mismatch between the DT and real-world environments: the network was trained on imperfect digital-twin data but evaluated on real-world surrobase data. Results show that the proposed method achieves 96.80% top-1 and 98.36% top-3 beam prediction accuracy, while reducing over-the-air sounding overhead by nearly an order of magnitude relative to exhaustive sweeping, outperforming convolutional and deep neural network baselines from prior work.
The Value of Steiner Hubs in Two-Hop Distance Labeling

Two-hop distance labelings were introduced in 2002 by Cohen, Halperin, Kaplan, and Zwick with hubs of two kinds: vertices of the graph, or, in their Steiner variant, arbitrary objects carrying arbitrary real values. On no family is the value of that freedom known. We determine it on $\ell_1$ products of betweenness-free metrics, those with no point between two others, a class containing every Hamming graph. The freedom is worth nothing when the factors have at most three letters, while from four letters on the largest saving is polynomial in the size of the product, attained on products of positively weighted stars. The $d$-dimensional hypercube is the two-letter case, and labeling it takes $(5/2+o(1))^d$ entries even with arbitrary hubs, matching the vertex-hub optimum of Goldberg, Razenshteyn, and Savchenko. Every lower bound here comes from one semidefinite program on a single factor, whose value $Λ$ never exceeds the rate that vertex hubs already achieve on the Hamming graph; where $Λ$ meets that ceiling, the freedom is worth nothing, and the ceiling is met exactly up to three letters.
Minimum-Norm Interpolation in Weighted Variation Spaces: Direct and Inverse Problems
Weizhao Li; Lei Shi; Hanfei Zhou

We study minimum-norm interpolation in weighted variation spaces generated by ReLU$^s$ ridge functions on the unit ball, where $s$ is a positive integer. For a target $f$ in the weighted variation space and a node set with sufficiently small fill distance $h$, every minimum-norm interpolant satisfies the direct bound $\|f-\mathscr{I}_{X_h}f\|_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}h^{(2s+1)/4}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$. Under a boundary separation condition on the nodes, we construct a matching lower bound for the worst-case interpolation error. For the inverse problem, we introduce dual certificates and derive an estimate analogous to a Bernstein inequality. Under suitable upper bounds on dictionary size and spectral lower bounds for the atomic Gram matrices, sufficiently fast $L_2$ convergence of minimum-norm interpolants along geometrically decreasing fill distances implies that the target belongs to $\mathcal{V}_s$. As a byproduct, the best $L_2$ approximation error $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}$ for shallow ReLU$^s$ networks of width at most $n$ satisfies $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}n^{-1/2-(2s+1)/(2d)}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, with the weighted atomic cost of an approximating network bounded by a constant multiple of $\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, independently of $n$.
Secant dimensions and bilinear decomposition widths for finite Heisenberg groups
Nguyen Bich Van; Nguyen Trung Kien

Let $G=UT_3(\F_q)$ be the finite Heisenberg group. We study the image closures and secant varieties of a family of equivariant bilinear maps between representations induced from central characters. Evaluation at a basepoint identifies the ambient space with $M_{q^2}(\C)$. A single channel is represented by $A^T\operatorname{diag}(d)B$, with $A$ and $B$ in prescribed twisted-convolution algebras. We prove that its affine image closure has dimension $3q^2-2$ for every central-character pair and that its affine second-secant closure has the expected dimension for every prime power $q$. For $q\ge3$, the proof constructs two differential images with zero intersection. We also prove a subgroup-lifting theorem for channel parameterizations on finite abelian groups with bicharacter coefficients: a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|H|-2)$ on a subgroup $H$ extends by zero to a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|K|-2)$ on the ambient group $K$, provided that every parameter vector is nonzero. Exact Jacobian certificates determine all secant dimensions for $q=2,3,4,5$, with generic widths $2,4,6,9$. The lifting theorem yields specified higher-secant dimensions on infinite families of extension fields. Attainment of the dimension lower bound for arbitrary $q$ remains a conjecture.
A matroid characterization of the combinatorially symmetric maximum nullity of a graph
Louis Deaett; Veronika Furst; John Hutchens; Lon Mitchell

The graph parameter ${\mathrm N}(G)$ is the maximum nullity among all combinatorially symmetric matrices associated to a graph $G$. The zero forcing number ${\mathrm Z}(G)$ is a well-known upper bound for ${\mathrm N}(G)$, and a zero forcing set of $G$ is exactly a set that intersects each fort of the graph. So the zero forcing number can be defined as the size of a minimum set that intersects every fort of $G$. This paper provides a similar characterization of ${\mathrm N}(G)$ that is purely combinatorial, using a connection to matroid theory and collections of forts that are compatible in a certain sense. We provide several examples highlighting subtle differences among compatible collections of forts and how they relate to full spark matrices and matroids associated to $G$.
A localized packing lemma for sets of bounded $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension

In the setting of abelian groups, Haussler's packing lemma implies that any subset of bounded $\operatorname{VC}$-dimension can be approximated by one of a small number of representative translates. While this exact statement is provably false under the weaker hypothesis that $A$ has bounded $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension, we show that in $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ a similar statement does hold after localization to cosets of subspaces depending on the individual translates.
 More precisely, given $ε>0$ and $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p^n$ with $\operatorname{VC}_2(A)<k$, we show that there exist $r\leq ε^{-O_{k,p}(1)}$ and $g_1,\ldots, g_r\in \mathbb{F}_p^n$ with the property that for every $x\in \mathbb{F}_p^n$, there is a partition $\mathcal{C}_x$ of $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ into cosets of (possibly distinct) subgroups, each of index at most $\exp(ε^{-O_{k,p}(1)})$, and a subcollection $Ω_x\subseteq \mathcal{C}_x$ whose union has size at least $(1-ε)|\mathbb{F}_p^n|$, such that on each $C\in Ω_x$, the translate $A-x$ looks like one of $A-g_1,\ldots, A-g_r$, in the sense that $|((A-x)Δ(A-g_{i_{x,C}}))\cap C|<ε|C|$ for some $1\leq i_{x,C}\leq r$. We also prove a second version of this result in which each partition $\mathcal{C}_x$ is the set of cosets of a single subgroup $H_x$ of quasipolynomial index but where the bound on $r$ is a quadruple exponential.
From Gaussian to stable and back: Non-Pareto points in growing dimension
Chinmoy Bhattacharjee; Andrii Ilienko; Bochen Jin; Ilya Molchanov

We study the number of non-Pareto points in two high-dimensional models: a homogeneous Poisson point process and a fixed-size sample of independent uniform points in the unit cube. A point is non-Pareto if some other sample point is coordinatewise less than or equal to it. As the dimension grows on the logarithmic scale of the intensity or sample size, the asymptotic behavior exhibits a surprising sequence of transitions: from Gaussian to stable fluctuations, back to Gaussian, then to a Poisson limit at the sparsity threshold, followed by the eventual disappearance of non-Pareto points.
 We identify the critical thresholds, normalizations, and limiting laws in both models. Notably, the return to Gaussianity occurs while the stability index remains strictly below $2$ and is driven by a change in the dominant fluctuation mechanism. Moreover, in part of the returning Gaussian regime, the natural normalization is the square root of the expected count rather than its standard deviation. At the stable--Gaussian transition, the two mechanisms can coexist, giving rise to a sum of independent stable and Gaussian random variables.
Profile decomposition, strict binding and global compactness for a critical Grushin embedding
Understanding Work/Life Balance Through Mathematical Model

Work/life balance (WLB) remains a central yet elusive concept in social and organizational sciences, often described qualitatively without a unified quantitative framework. To address this gap, a novel compartmental mathematical model is proposed that formalizes WLB as a dynamic population-level phenomenon. The individuals are categorized into 4 compartments, namely, regularly employed, temporarily employed, imbalanced (infected), and balanced (recovered), representing balanced and imbalanced states. Role-based complaints govern the transitions between states, the conflict conversion rates of these complaints, and the recovery rate. The model, structured as a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations, is analyzed for the existence of the equilibrium and its stability. In the analysis, the stable disease-free equilibrium is found to exist, representing complete societal balance. The other endemic equilibrium is shown to be infeasible through simulations and thus requires certain parameter constraints, which represent a specific scenario that may occur in the population. However, it is found that the endemic equilibrium always remains unstable. The model's ability to quantify how micro-level stressors spread into macro-level imbalance is demonstrated by numerical simulations, which also validate the analytical results. This work establishes a rigorous mathematical foundation for WLB, enabling future empirical and mathematical calibrations.
We review the eleven open questions in Appendix H of Farina's manuscript on entire solutions of the Allen-Cahn equation (dated March 9, 2016).
A relative version of Weinstein's morphism

We introduce a relative version of Weinstein's morphism associated to a
 Lagrangian submanifold \(L\) of a closed symplectic manifold
 \((M,ω)\). We construct a homomorphism
 \[
 \mathcal{A}^{(L,α)}\colon
 π_{1}\bigl(\operatorname{Ham}_0(M,L)\bigr)
 \longrightarrow
 \mathbb{R}/\mathcal{P}_{2}(M,ω),
 \]
 and establish its basic properties. We compute the invariant
 in several examples, including latitude circles in \(S^2\), and more generally, Lagrangian fibers in toric manifolds. These computations provide
 obstructions to Ha\-mil\-to\-nian isotopy of Lagrangian submanifolds and detect
 nontrivial, and in some cases infinite-order, elements in the homotopy
 groups of their Hamiltonian stabilizers.
Massively parallel Schwarz methods for the high-frequency Helmholtz equation with O(k) convergence
Yan Xie; Yue Yu; Shihua Gong; Ivan G. Graham; Chen-song Zhang

We develop a one-level restricted additive Schwarz solver with perfectly matched layer transmission conditions (RAS--PML) for high-frequency Helmholtz systems. For problems with ${O}(k^d)$ unknowns, $d=2,3$, the solver uses Cartesian decompositions and ${O}(k^d)$ concurrent local solves for a single right-hand side, where $k$ is the wavenumber. Starting from the convergence theory for fixed decompositions established in~\texttt{arXiv:2404.02156}, we address the growing cost {as $k$ increases} of local solves through a nested RAS--PML construction. Under suitable stability and contraction assumptions, we prove that sufficiently accurate recursive local solves preserve convergence of the outer iteration. We also prove that a single inner iteration at each non-terminal level yields a correction algebraically equivalent to one-level RAS--PML, provided that the hierarchy-induced finest local problems and composite restriction and weighted extension operators are retained. This equivalence provides a hierarchical interpretation and permits a direct implementation without recursive transfers. We assess the one-level solver using PML and overlap widths of order ${O}(k^{-1}\log k)$. Constant-coefficient experiments cover $300\leq k\leq19200$ in two dimensions and $60\leq k\leq780$ in three dimensions, reaching $1.47\times10^9$ and $4.75\times10^8$ complex unknowns, respectively. Richardson iteration counts grow approximately linearly with $k$ over these ranges, while total parallel runtime, including setup and solution, exhibits near-linear growth at the larger tested wavenumbers. Further experiments assess the effects of mesh refinement and heterogeneous media.
