In this paper, we establish Morse theory for the Neumann mean field equation on a compact Riemann surface at $ρ=4πm$, $m\in\mathbb N$. To address the loss of compactness associated with bubbling, we use Bahri's theory of critical points at infinity. Assume that the reduced functionals are Morse and that the leading scale coefficient does not vanish at their critical points. We classify the critical points at infinity arising from interior, boundary, and mixed concentration, compute their Morse indices and local relative homology, and establish deformation lemmas at resonance. We prove that, for $m\geq 2$, every sufficiently negative sublevel is homotopy equivalent to the boundary-weighted barycenter space of order $m-1$. The Euler--Poincaré identity gives the Leray--Schauder degree at resonance without assuming nondegeneracy of the solutions. If all solutions are nondegenerate, we further obtain strong Morse inequalities with explicit Betti numbers over $\mathbb Z_2$. As a consequence, we obtain existence and multiplicity results, as well as criteria for solutions with prescribed Morse index.

We prove that a finite-dimensional connected monomial algebra over an algebraically closed field is derived tame if and only if every finite connected convex subcategory of its universal cover has non-negative Euler form. Derived tameness is also equivalent to tameness of its repetitive category and trivial extension. For one-cycle algebras, this condition is equivalent to the non-negativity on $\mathbb R$ of $|Q_0|$ explicitly computable polynomials in $\mathbb Q[t]$. This gives a finite algorithm for deciding derived tameness. We also construct an infinite family of derived-tame one-cycle string algebras with minimal cubic relations, no two of which are derived equivalent.
Gang Cai; Qingjin Cheng; Longfa Sun; Yinghua Sun

In this paper, we prove that if a Banach space $X$ has the hereditary approximation property, then $X\oplus_2 H$ has the hereditary approximation property for every Hilbert space $H$. This answers a question of Johnson and Szankowski. In addition, if $X$ is also reflexive, then every closed subspace of $X\oplus_2H$ has the metric approximation property. The proof uses Grothendieck's characterization of the approximation property, a factorization of nuclear operators through quotients of $X$, and a nuclear perturbation of the coordinate projection on a closed graph.
$W^{1,p}$ error estimates of an IPDG and a class of HDG methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains

This paper analyzes a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method, a hybrid mixed DG method, and two representative hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains. For any fixed $ε\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, we first derive optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates for $2\leq p<\frac{1}ε$ by combining the interface Green's functions developed in \cite{lq2026} with the Fubini-type weighted estimates established in this paper. These error estimates lead to discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability for $2\leq q<\frac{1}ε$, where $q$ is the conjugate number of $p$ such that $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. Using this stability result and a suitably constructed dual problem, we extend the optimal error estimates to $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<2$ and subsequently establish the corresponding inf-sup stability for $\frac{1}{1-ε}< q<2$. Thus, both optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates and discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability hold throughout the range $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<\frac{1}ε$, with $q=p/(p-1)$. Note that all of the aforementioned results are free of logarithmic factors and also hold on polyhedral meshes (except for the hybrid mixed DG method). Compared with the conforming finite element method (FEM), establishing such error estimates and inf-sup stability results for DG methods on convex polyhedral domains is more delicate because their analysis involves mesh-dependent norms. Consequently, the operator interpolation theory employed for conforming FEMs cannot be directly applied to DG methods. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the theoretical results.
A solution to Haagerup's Problem on decomposable maps
We prove that a von Neumann algebra $N$ is injective if and only if $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for every linear map $T:\ell^\infty_3to N$, answering a problem of Haagerup (1985).
Feasibility of Common-Stream-Only Sensing in ZF-RSMA with Imperfect CSIT

Reusing the Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) common stream for sensing eliminates dedicated probing signals in Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC), but creates a feasibility bottleneck: the common-power fraction must simultaneously support common decoding, private decoding, and target detection. This paper investigates this tradeoff in downlink zero-forcing RSMA with imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). With the common beam fixed over a sensing dwell through sensing geometry, the common-power fraction becomes the sole design variable. We prove that the communication-feasible set is either a closed interval or empty. Analytical outage expressions localize these endpoints, revealing a high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) floor-ceiling effect: common decoding dictates a common-power floor, while imperfect CSIT and SIC impose a private-decoding ceiling. For sensing, the conditional detection constraint is affine, preserving the interval structure. A geometry-matched common beam ensures monotonic detection improvement, reducing joint-feasibility check to the communication-feasible upper endpoint. Simulations validate our analysis, identifying regimes where common-stream-only sensing is viable.
On unitary representations of $p$-adic $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}$ and $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ of purely bad parity

Let $G$ be $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$ or split $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$ over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We classify the irreducible unitary representations of $G$ of purely bad parity: such a representation is unitary if and only if it is of Arthur type, except for one additional family when $G=\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$. In particular, we confirm the remaining case of Ciubotaru's conjecture for $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$, namely that every unitary unipotent representation with integral infinitesimal parameter is of Arthur type.
A note on rational wavefront sets for finite special orthogonal groups

We study rational wavefront sets of irreducible representations of finite special orthogonal groups over $\mathbb F_q$. We assume that $q$ is odd and that both $q$ and its characteristic are sufficiently large. Using {the second author's} results for full orthogonal groups, we determine the maximal rational wavefront sets and the dimensions of the corresponding generalized Whittaker models. We show that each rational wavefront set is the rational closure of its maximal elements. For unipotent representations, we describe the maximal rational wavefront sets in terms of Lusztig's canonical quotient and their behavior under Alvis--Curtis duality.

We endow a tropical curve with the structure of a ringed space and establish analogues of Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for these ringed spaces. As a corollary, we give a cohomological proof of the tropical Riemann-Roch theorem.
Maximum edge overlap between independent random regular graphs

Optimising the vertex correspondence can substantially increase the number of edges shared by two independent realisations of the same random graph. We quantify this phenomenon for uniformly random $d$-regular graphs and derive corresponding results for their edge-based graph edit distance. For every fixed $d\geq 3$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n+Θ_{\mathbb P}(n/\log n)$, where the leading term $n$ arises from Hamiltonicity, while the surplus captures the optimal order of the excess beyond it. We establish explicit upper and lower bounds on the surplus. The upper bound is obtained by counting common cores of minimum degree at least two, while the lower bound is established using spanning factors consisting of cycles of the same logarithmic length. For the special case $d=2$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n-(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))\log n$. The additional overlap achievable is also studied by rotating aligned Hamilton cycles, using a contiguity argument. As a by-product, we determine the asymptotic maximum overlap between unions of independent random perfect matchings under cyclic shifts.
Deformations of Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms

Recent work of Brantner and Taelman shows that derived deformation theory and period maps can recover strong mixed-characteristic lifting results. In this paper, we develop a prismatic version of this method for Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms, constructing compatible deformations over $A/I^n$ for every $n$ under suitable hypotheses. We also apply our method to $F$-split Calabi--Yau varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. In particular, we consider an $F$-split smooth proper variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$, with $H^{d-1}(X,O_X)=0$ and trivial canonical bundle. We show that $X$ admits a lift to $W_3(k)$.
An extension of the classic Buneman theorem from phylogenetic trees to networks

Phylogenetic networks provide a natural framework for representing reticulate evolutionary events such as horizontal gene transfer and hybridization. In the present manuscript, we investigate the identifiability of phylogenetic networks under (hardwired) parsimony, a natural extension of Maximum Parsimony from trees to networks. More precisely, we ask which structural features of a network can be uniquely inferred from so-called $A_k$-alignments under this criterion. While identifiability has been studied extensively for phylogenetic trees under parsimony, little is known about the identifiability of networks under hardwired parsimony. We take a first step towards addressing this gap by developing a general framework for studying identifiability under hardwired parsimony. We then use this framework to show that the tree of blobs of a phylogenetic network can be reconstructed from its $A_1$-alignment. This result can be viewed as a natural extension of Buneman's well-known splits equivalence theorem. Finally, we show that, under hardwired parsimony, cycles of length at least $5$ cannot in general be uniquely identified from character data, establishing a fundamental limitation of hardwired parsimony.
Relative Du Bois complexes over higher dimensional bases

We extend the notion of the right relative Du Bois complex to a smooth base of arbitrary dimension. We further show that this complex satisfies base change in the sense of Kovács--Taji, for flat families with strict higher Du Bois fibers, extending the result by Ning over a smooth curve.
Effective threshold dynamics for the cubic nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in three dimensions

We consider the focussing cubic Klein-Gordon equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$ in the radial setting. Foundational work by Nakanishi-Schlag gives a complete qualitative characterisation of the dynamics near the ground state $Q$, in particular revealing a threshold phenomenon, whereby a co-dimension one Lipschitz manifold separates finite time blow up from scattering solutions in forward time. Our aim in this paper is to derive an effective bound for the scattering norm $\|u\|_{L_t^3([0,\infty);L_x^6(\mathbb{R}^3))}$, for scattering energy class solutions $u$ with data sufficiently near $Q$ and close to the threshold manifold. This requires the development of an induction on energy strategy in a setting where an alternative to the usual Morawetz approach appears necessary.

We obtain series of new completely regular codes in Cayley graphs of the groups $Z_q^n$ with the Lee metric. Combined with binary linear programming methods, the constructions lead to enumeration of all completely regular codes in such graphs for the groups $Z_q^4$, $q\leq 7$ up to parameter matrices.
Numerical analysis of linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem

In this paper, we analyze the standard and the mass-lumped linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem. For the standard method, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of the discrete ground state up to sign for sufficiently small mesh sizes, which only requires the $H^1$-convergence of the discrete ground states. For both methods, we establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-norms for $1 \le p < \infty$. Under additional regularity assumptions on the potential, we further obtain an optimal convergence rate in the $W^{1,\infty}$-norm and an almost optimal convergence rate, up to a logarithmic factor, in the $L^\infty$-norm. Moreover, we prove that the discrete ground states superconverge to the Ritz projection of the exact ground state in the $W^{1,p}$-seminorm. The analysis is based on a perturbation argument. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
Extending Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization to Systems of Linear Equations

Solving systems of linear equations, $Ax=b$, is a ubiquitous task in computational science. The Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd algorithm requires phase estimation, controlled rotations, and post-selection, impractical on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware. We extend sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), developed for quantum chemistry, to linear systems. Following the sample-based Krylov variant, the Hermitian matrix $A$ is decomposed in the Pauli basis, the Trotterized time evolution of $|b\rangle$ is sampled at several times to select computational-basis configurations, and the system is solved classically by a Galerkin projection onto the selected subspace. We prove that the subspace solution is exact when the sampled configurations contain the Krylov support of $b$ and optimal in the energy norm for symmetric positive-definite matrices, so that noise-induced configurations cannot degrade it as long as they do not displace the ideal ones. On IBM Quantum hardware, the sampled distribution of a $4\times4$ example deviates from the exact one by eleven times the shot-noise level, yet the solution is recovered exactly. For a localized problem of dimension $N=1024$, SQD selects 33 configurations, reaches a relative error of $10^{-5}$, and its truncated subspaces coincide with the optimal choice; readout errors enlarge the subspace without degrading the accuracy. The tests also show the limitations: the selected subspace coincides with that of inexpensive classical selection, banded matrices require exponentially many Pauli terms in the binary encoding, and Trotter errors populate spurious configurations unless the circuits are deep. An MIT-licensed Python package and notebooks that reproduce the numerical results are provided.
First and second order firing statistics of large neuronal networks with community structure
Thiago H. N. Coelho; Daniel Figueiredo; Giulio Iacobelli; Guilherme Ost; Conrado C. Pinto

We study a discrete-time stochastic model for the spiking activity of a network of $n$ interacting neurons partitioned into $k$ communities. The interaction network is a random directed weighted graph generated by a Stochastic Block Model with $k+1$ edge types ($k$ intra-community, $1$ inter-community). Each edge is present independently with a probability that depends only on its type. When present, an edge carries a type-dependent deterministic weight scaled by $n^{-1}$, which is excitatory or inhibitory depending on an independent random sign. Given the interaction network, the spiking process is a stationary Markov chain. Our results describe how the network's community structure manifests itself in the first- and second-order statistics of this chain, as $n \to \infty$ with $k$ fixed. Representing these statistics as explicit functions of the random interaction network, we prove that, with high probability: (i) the vectors of mean firing activity and firing variances are approximated in supremum norm by deterministic vectors that are constant within each community, with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n}$; (ii) the off-diagonal part of the $0$-lagged firing covariance matrix is approximated in max norm, with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n^3}$, by a deterministic community-block matrix (constant on each block defined by a pair of communities), with block values determined by the unique solution to a $k \times k$ Stein matrix equation; (iii) in contrast, the $t$-lagged covariance matrix, for every lag $t \ge 1$, is approximated in max norm, again with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n^3}$, by a random matrix built from two components: a random matrix capturing the interaction network and a deterministic community-block matrix. Finally, we discuss conditions on the model parameters under which these limiting statistics enable the identifiability of the community structure.
Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras

We classify the connected components of support $τ$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components. For every nonzero $τ$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra, the graph of $τ$-tilting completions is connected. More generally, we classify the completion components for an arbitrary surface rigid algebra and a fixed $τ$-rigid pair. For partial tagged triangulations with all endpoints at punctures, we express the Cartan matrix and $g$-vectors by signed endpoint data. We prove that $τ$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates. Trees give type A, and a criterion on the original partial tagged triangulation distinguishes types D and C in the unicyclic case.
Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes
Juliana G. F. Souza; Yu-Chih Huang

We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. For uniform finite inputs, we derive a controlled high-SNR expansion of the information variance and determine its limiting ratio to the mutual information deficit. The mutual information expansion specialises arbitrary input fading results and gives an explicit remainder. Standard random-coding and second-order achievability tools relate these quantities to reliability over independently faded Alamouti blocks. All alphabets preserve symbol-wise maximum-likelihood detection at the Alamouti level. Numerical energy, mutual information, and error-rate comparisons support the analysis. Centred comparisons with classical Alamouti, Golden, and Silver codes illustrate the trade-off between reliability, symbol rate, and decoding effort.
A Preconditioned Quantum Linear Solver for Periodic Two-Phase Heat Conduction with Mesh-Independent Condition Number

We consider here computational homogenization of a periodic two-phase conduction problem. Quantum linear-system algorithms for its finite element discretization are limited by the condition number of the stiffness matrix. This condition number grows quadratically with the number of elements per side. Classically, preconditioning by the homogeneous (single-phase) operator bounds the condition number by the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size. On a quantum computer, however, a preconditioner encoded as a separate factor multiplies the subnormalizations, and the quadratic dependency returns. In this paper, we absorb the closed-form inverse square root of the homogeneous operator into the finite element factors. The preconditioned operator then becomes the product of a norm-preserving gradient operator $\mat{V}$, a diagonal matrix of scaled conductivities, and $\mat{V}^T$. Each factor has norm at most one. The block encoding therefore has subnormalization one, and its condition number is bounded by just the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size and in every dimension. The operator $\mat{V}$ is applied as a quantum Fourier transform, a small rotation at each wavenumber, and an inverse transform. Quantum singular value transformation then block-encodes the inverse of the preconditioned operator. We test the method numerically on three periodic cells with up to $10^6$ unknowns. The results confirm that the condition number does not depend on the mesh, and the energy-norm error of the inverse is below the polynomial tolerance at every mesh. On meshes of $4 \times 4$ and $8 \times 8$ elements, we also build the entire inverse as one Qiskit circuit and simulate it by state vector, with the rotation at each wavenumber built from uniformly controlled rotations. The output state agrees with the finite element solution to within the polynomial tolerance.
Inviscid limit for the hyperbolic Keller--Segel equations in $B_{\infty,1}^{1}$

In this paper, we study the inviscid limit for the hyperbolic Keller--Segel equations with logistic sensitivity $1-u$. We establish a common existence time and a priori estimates uniform with respect to the diffusion coefficient in the critical Besov spaces $B_{p,1}^{1+d/p}(R^d)$ with $1\le p\le\infty$. For $1<p<\infty$, we obtain explicit convergence rates in $B_{p,1}^{0}$, and we also give estimates for the case $p=1$. For initial data in $B_{\infty,1}^{1}$, we prove convergence at rate $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ in $L^\infty$, a bound of order $O(\varepsilon^{1/2}\log(e/\varepsilon))$ in $B_{\infty,1}^{0}$, and strong convergence in $L^\infty(0,T;B_{\infty,1}^{1})$. Additional regularity of the initial data yields improved convergence rates. We construct a fixed initial datum showing that the exponent $1/2$ in $L^\infty$ is optimal.
Proper conflict-free degree-choosability of graphs with maximum average degree less than $8/3$

A proper coloring $φ$ of a graph $G$ is called proper conflict-free if, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood $N_G(v)$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable if, for every list assignment $L$ satisfying $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)+k$ for each $v\in V(G)$, there exists a proper conflict-free coloring $φ$ of $G$ with $φ(v)\in L(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$. We prove that every connected graph other than the $5$-cycle $C_5$ with maximum average degree less than $8/3$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable. This improves the maximum average degree bound $18/7$ of Kashima, Škrekovski and Xu, and removes the assumption $g(G)\ge7$ from the $8/3$ theorem of Qi, Song and Cao. As an immediate consequence, our theorem also yields that every planar graph of girth at least $8$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable.
Bridging rough stochastic differential equations and rough semimartingales
Jannis R. Dause; Peter K. Friz; Jost Pieper

We bridge the gap between the mixed-moment theory of càdlàg rough stochastic differential equations (short:RSDEs), introduced by Friz, Hocquet and Lê (2021) and extended to the càdlàg setting by Allan and Pieper (2026), and the theory of rough semimartingales (short:RSMs), introduced by Friz and Zorin-Kranich (2023), by investigating the intersection of these two theories for the first time. By introducing the concept of good solutions to RSDEs, solutions which are simultaneously both mixed-moment solutions and RSMs, we develop a solution concept, which allows for good control on both moment-based and pathwise properties of solutions. The well-posedness of good solutions is proven using a fixed point argument on the space of $L^{2}$-martingales by suitably leveraging previously known mixed-moment estimates. Based on these insights we further characterize a large class of good solutions of semi-linear RSDEs through a novel rough stochastic Duhamel's principle.
Elliptic Fekete points: separation, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning

Elliptic Fekete configurations minimize logarithmic energy on the sphere. They also provide a natural source of complex polynomials with controlled Shub--Smale condition number. The link between these two problems is the product of the distances from each point to all the other points: logarithmic energy controls the geometric mean of these products, whereas local conditioning depends on each product separately. This paper studies the passage from global information to uniform estimates at individual nodes, exploring its connections with quantitative equidistribution, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning. We improve separation bounds for elliptic Fekete configurations and obtain quantitative Riesz-energy estimates for both these configurations and spherical roots of polynomials with optimal-order global conditioning. For $0<s<2$, these estimates also improve explicit upper bounds for the minimal Riesz $s$-energy.

The reduction number of the maximal ideal of a localization (or even faithfully flat extension) need not increase under specialization. Nevertheless, for each fixed local ring the reduction numbers of the maximal ideals of all its localization have a finite common bound.
Estimates of Lucas series and expansions in non-integer bases

Special Fibonacci and Lucas type expansions proved useful to ``correct'' some theorems on the number of expansions in non-integer bases \cite{BaiKomLor2021, KomLorPed2024, KomLorPed2025}. The proof of a key lemma was non-constructive. It was made constructive in the Fibonacci case by giving a precise estimate of the growth of the partial sums of the series of the inverses of the Fibonacci numbers \cite{KomPed2025}. In this paper we extend this result to the general case.
Mathematical foundations of second quantization: an introduction through spin-boson models

These lecture notes originate from a one-semester course on the mathematical foundations of second quantization, first given at the Department of Physics of the Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg in the Winter Semester 2025/26 to a mixed audience of physics and mathematics students. Their guiding thread is a class of physical models: spin-boson models, describing a two-level system coupled to a boson field. After summarizing the necessary background on unbounded operators, up to the Kato-Rellich and KLMN theorems, and developing direct sums and tensor products of Hilbert spaces and of unbounded operators, we treat single-mode boson fields, constructing the ladder and number operators and characterizing their domains, before moving to Fock spaces, second quantization, bosonic and fermionic annihilation and creation operators, and the canonical (anti)commutation relations. Throughout, spin-boson models provide both the motivation and the test bench for the formalism: we rigorously establish their self-adjointness, solve the pure dephasing and Jaynes-Cummings models explicitly, deriving their spectra and the qubit channels they induce, show how their multimode counterparts display irreversible decoherence and decay, and, in an appendix, prove the rotating-wave approximation for the quantum Rabi model with an explicit error bound. Finally, we use the KLMN theorem to construct spin-boson models with non-normalizable form factors, and briefly discuss stronger ultraviolet divergences and the need for renormalization. Exercises with full solutions are included.
Genetic weight of a mutant in a biparental Moran model with infinite selection

We study, after Coron Le Jan (2024), the genetic contribution of a single strongly advantageous mutant in a biparental Moran model under infinite selection. We prove a functional limit theorem for the entire beneficial mutation spreading period: after normalization by \(\sqrt N\), the contributions carried by the advantaged and disadvantaged subpopulations converge jointly in law to a non-degenerate random multiple of an explicit deterministic profile. Randomness is generated during the initial microscopic growth of the mutant lineage and subsequently propagated through the population along a deterministic macroscopic trajectory. At the heart of this phenomenon is an eigenmode martingale that measures the imbalance between the mean genetic weight of the founding ancestor within the two classes; its limiting value provides precisely the random amplitude of the macroscopic profile and is characterized by a smoothing equation.
Risk-Sensitive Mission Planning for Multi-Target On-Orbit Inspection via Distributional Reinforcement Learning

Multi-target on-orbit servicing missions require planning tools that can adapt to evolving operational conditions while accounting for the outcome variability inherent to safety-critical spaceflight. This paper presents an adaptive planning approach for multi-target servicing campaigns in low Earth orbit and applies it to inspection missions flown by a low-thrust servicer. The approach is based on Distributional Reinforcement Learning, which learns the full distribution of mission returns and thereby supports explicit risk-sensitive decision-making at each planning step. Specifically, a Quantile-Regression Deep Q-Network (QR-DQN) agent selects which target to inspect next by jointly considering the expectation and the variance of the predicted return through a mean-variance criterion. The mission environment models circular orbits with a spread in inclination and uses Edelbaum's combined-manoeuvre low-thrust transfer estimates. The observation comprises the orbital elements, the visit history, the observed risk state of each target and the remaining mission-time budget. The risk state of each target changes stochastically during the campaign, making the outcome of an inspection uncertain and creating operationally meaningful distinctions between risk-neutral and risk-averse planning strategies. Because the mission-time budget generally admits only a subset of the candidate targets, the planner must also select which targets to inspect. Numerical experiments on scenarios with five target satellites show that one risk-aversion weight moves the policy across a range of mean return and return variance, over an unchanged environment and reward. Risk-averse agents reduce the variance of the episodic return by approximately one half relative to risk-neutral agents and lower the probability of a mission loss, at a cost in mean return. To validate the learned policies, the efficient frontier, which gives the highest mean return attainable at each level of return variance, is computed exactly by enumerating the admissible visit orders. At equal variance, the learned policies lie close to this frontier in mean return, and the risk-averse policies have a lower probability of a mission loss than the frontier policies.
Secure Deterministic Identification with Feedback and Sensing over State-Dependent Wiretap Channels
Vida Gholamian; Yaning Zhao; Christian Deppe; Holger Boche; Rafael F. Schaefer

Identification differs from classical transmission in that the receiver determines whether a particular identity was sent rather than recovering a message. We study secure deterministic identification over state-dependent discrete memoryless wiretap channels with private noiseless feedback and a sensing distortion constraint. The encoder has no local randomness and uses only the identity and past feedback. A symbol-wise input restriction guarantees the sensing constraint. We show that the secure deterministic identification capacity equals its non-secure feedback counterpart when the admissible main channel has positive ordinary transmission capacity and H(Y|Z,X=x)>0 for some fixed admissible input x. This equality does not require positive classical wiretap secrecy capacity. For achievability, noiseless feedback generates common randomness for identification and enables secret-key extraction by privacy amplification. The extracted key one-time-pad encrypts a short identification tag, whose reliable transmission requires only a sublinear number of additional channel uses. We also present an alternative construction in which feedback-generated randomness replaces the local randomization of a stochastic wiretap encoder. We further prove that secure identification capacity vanishes whenever non-secure identification capacity is zero. We also identify a class of channels with input-independent wiretapper observations that achieves full non-secure identification capacity even when the private conditional feedback entropy is zero, illustrated by a binary state-dependent wiretap channel. Thus, feedback can support both identification and secrecy without local encoder randomization while satisfying sensing constraints.
P-generalized determinant over quaternions and its applications

This paper introduces the ${\rm P}$-generalized determinant, a more general class of quaternion determinants. It unifies several classical quaternion determinants proposed between 1922 and 2008, including the Moore determinant, the Xie determinant, the Chen determinant, and the Kyrchei row--column determinants, thereby revealing the essential nature of quaternion determinants as multivariate polynomial-type functions with a fixed ordering of products. We provide equivalent characterizations of the expansion of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant along a given row or column, and establish conversion relations between the $\mathrm{P}_{l}$- and $\mathrm{P}_{r}$-generalized determinants. We prove that the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant of a quaternion Hermitian matrix is a real number independent of the choice of cycle representation rule. We further investigate the behavior of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant under elementary row and column operations on quaternion Hermitian matrices, as well as its linearity in rows and columns. Finally, using the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant, we derive determinantal representations of the inverse of an invertible quaternion Hermitian matrix and of the unique solution to the quaternion matrix equation $AXB=C$. In particular, this yields Cramer's rule for the left and right linear systems $Ax=b$ and $xA=b$.
Chance-Constrained Inspection Viewpoint Sequencing for On-Orbit Servicing via Safe Reinforcement Learning

Autonomous inspection of a target spacecraft is typically the initial step in on-orbit servicing. Planning close-proximity observation viewpoints involves a complex combinatorial problem constrained by coverage, fuel, and safety considerations. This paper models the viewpoint selection as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) and applies Proximal Policy Optimization with Lagrangian relaxation to solve it. The system combines a high-level planner, which sequences camera viewpoints on an observation sphere around the target, with a low-level model that assesses each transfer using the Clohessy--Wiltshire (CW) equations for relative motion. The deterministic constraints on single-impulse reachability and $Δv$ cap are enforced directly on the action set. Safety margins are affected by navigation and manoeuvre errors, making the actual clearance stochastic. To address this, a chance constraint on the realised trajectory is implemented, with a Lagrangian multiplier governed by PID control to adapt the penalty during training. The approach is tested on a Galileo-class navigation satellite in medium Earth orbit, modelled as a point cloud where visibility from each viewpoint considers field-of-view and line-of-sight occlusion. Across various risk budgets, the trained policy maintains the keep-out violation rate within the specified limit, achieving coverage close to its maximum and staying within the mission $Δv$ budget. Compared to the usual practice of applying a fixed margin to the keep-out radius and planning deterministically, the chance-constrained policy attains less than half the violation rate at comparable coverage. This makes the collision risk an explicit design parameter, eliminating the need for re-tuning per case. The learned policy selects a viewpoint without the repeated Monte Carlo risk estimates required by a greedy, chance-constrained planner at every decision point.
Spectral theory for transmission problems and resonances for transparent balls

We construct generalized eigenfunctions and a spectral calculus for the transmission problem on Lipschitz domains. Then, focusing on the specific example of the ball, we prove a high-frequency resonance dichotomy for Maxwell's equations for a ball with positive, piecewise constant permittivity and permeability. If the product of these coefficients is no larger inside the ball than outside, the cutoff resolvent extends holomorphically to a strip of fixed width below the real axis, including the case of equal products. If the interior product is larger, we construct whispering-gallery resonances exponentially close to the real axis. The proofs use estimates for the transverse electric and transverse magnetic determinants that are uniform in angular momentum and complex frequency, together with a quasimode construction and Rouché's theorem. Explicit generalized eigenfunctions identify these determinants with the scattering poles and give the spectral resolution and the normalization relating the scattering amplitude to the Mie T-matrix.
Global existence and uniqueness of Lions' weak solutions for the 2D inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations in bounded domains

The global well-posedness for Lions' weak solutions to the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in two-dimensional bounded domains is concerned. When the initial density $0\leq ρ_0\in L^\infty(\Om)$ (allowing for vacuum) and initial velocity $u_0\in L^2_σ(Ω)$, the global existence, regularity, and exponential decay-in-time rates of weak solutions are established via a priori estimates, which rely crucially on the duality of BMO and Hardy space for the pressure term, and the classical Sobolev extension theorem. In particular, for the non-vacuous case where $0< ρ_0\in L^\infty(\Om)$ is bounded away from zero, we further prove the uniqueness of weak solutions in the sense of approximation by strong solutions, based on the key estimate \(t^{1/2}\nabla u\in L^2(0,T;L^\infty(Ω))\), which essentially follows from a delicate localized point-wise bound for \(\nabla u\) near the boundary. The latter bound is derived by the Green functions estimate for the nonhomogeneous Dirichlet Stokes problem, and the uniform \(C^1\) boundary estimate on the remaining homogeneous Stokes problem, through a Stokes decomposition on suitably constructed local \(C^2\) domains.
Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
Joseph T. A Peterson; Manoranjan Majji; John L. Junkins

Although nonconservative forces and extended phase space are individually common topics in Hamiltonian dynamics, their combination is seldom developed explicitly. This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion for nonconservative and nonautonomous dynamical systems formulated on extended phase space. Particular attention is given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. The classic analytical dynamics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates (i.e., canonical coordinates) or functions thereof.
Boundary stabilization of a moving interface in a 2 x 2 weakly hyperbolic system of balance laws: application to continuous sedimentation
Mohand Ouidir Amirat; Vincent Andrieu; Mathieu Bajodek; Claire Valentin

We design a boundary feedback for the level of the sediment bed of a continuous settler and prove that it exponentially stabilizes the linearized closed loop under a small-gain condition. The unit is modeled by a 2 x 2 system of balance laws in which the bed surface, the interface, is not a smooth part of the solution but a moving shock between a weakly hyperbolic free-settling zone and a strictly hyperbolic compression zone. We describe it by the Rankine-Hugoniot relations and map the problem onto a fixed domain. Moreover, we prove local well-posedness with a continuation criterion given by a single margin function. Then we linearize the system near an equilibrium. The linearization couples a dissipative distributed layer to one scalar, the interface position, whose equation does not contain the control. We solve this by infinitedimensional forwarding: a Sylvester kernel cancels the interface trace and isolates the interface pole, and a proportional feedback then sets its decay rate. Every hypothesis is verified on an illustrative example, a laboratory-scale continuous settler containing a bed of compact polystyrene beads.
Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids

We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.
Push forwards of smooth measures on the unitary group in odd characteristic under the Chevalley map are almost bounded
Avraham Aizenbud; Nir Avni; Dmitry Gourevitch; David Kazhdan; Eitan Sayag

In this paper we study analytic properties of the Chevalley map $p:\mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{c}$ where $\mathfrak{u}$ is the Lie algebra of a unitary group over a local field of odd characteristics. This map essentially sends a matrix to its characteristic polynomial. Our main result is that smooth compactly supported measures on $\mathfrak{u}$ are pushed by the Chevalley map to measures on $\mathfrak{c}$ with density functions in $L^q(\mathfrak{c})$ for all $q < \infty$. We also provide similar results for the Chevalley map attached to the unitary group. An important consequence is an odd characteristic analogue to results of Harish-Chandra stating the local integrability of the orbital integrals on the unitary group and its Lie algebra. Further possible applications to local integrability of characters of admissible representations of unitary groups over local fields of odd characteristic are also discussed.
A Gaussian Process Regression-Enhanced Two-Sweep Parameterized Power Method for Computing Extreme Eigenpairs
Tiantian Sun; Xiaofei Peng; Juan Zhang; Seakweng Vong

For computing the dominant eigenvalue and the corresponding eigenvector of a real and symmetric matrix, inspired by the parameterized power method and multistep iteration, we propose a two-sweep parameterized power method, and establish its convergence theory. To further improve the convergence speed of the new method, we use Gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict the quasi-optimal parameter and give a version of the proposed method based on GPR. Numerical experiments show that the two-sweep parameterized power method with quasi-optimal parameters outperforms some existing methods in terms of computing efficiency.
List 3-Coloring in tame classes of graphs in quasipolynomial time

A class of graphs $\mathcal{G}$ is tame if there is a constant c such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ has at most $n^c$ minimal separators. Many important graph classes are tame, including chordal graphs, permutation graphs, and circle graphs. Several fundamental problems, most notably Max Weight Independent Set, can be solved in polynomial time on every tame class, which explains in a unified way their tractability on all these classes. We show that List 3-Coloring can be solved in quasipolynomial time on every tame class of graphs.
Distributed Zeroth-Order Composite Finite-Sum Optimization via Incremental Variance Reduction

We study decentralized composite finite-sum optimization over a fixed connected undirected network, where agents access local component functions through function evaluations and share a possibly nonsmooth convex regularizer. In this setting, standard two-point gradient estimators can retain nonvanishing variance at a solution, complicating their integration with gradient tracking. We propose Distributed Zeroth-Order Incremental Variance Reduction (Distributed ZIVR), which combines incrementally updated component-gradient estimates with a proximal gradient-tracking scheme. The method admits an implementation using a constant number of function evaluations per agent at every iteration, without intermittent full-component or full-coordinate refreshes. For convex smooth component functions and strongly convex local averages, we establish linear convergence up to a controllable finite-difference error. With the finite-difference radius chosen for the target accuracy, Chebyshev-accelerated mixing yields a per-agent oracle complexity of $\widetilde{O}(d(m+κ)\log(1/ε))$ for expected squared solution error $ε$, where $d$ is the dimension, $m$ is the number of components per agent, and $κ$ is the condition number. This matches the centralized ZIVR oracle bound, while the communication bound has only an inverse square-root dependence on the network spectral gap. Experiments on logistic and robust regression demonstrate rapid reduction of solution and consensus errors.
Quasi-projective dimensions over homological ring epimorphisms

In this paper, we study quasi-projective dimensions of modules over rings connected by homological ring epimorphisms. We establish several inequalities relating the quasi-projective dimensions over the source and target rings. As applications, we investigate the quasi-global dimension of triangular matrix rings and provide examples showing that the class of modules with finite quasi-projective dimension does not satisfy the 2-out-of-3 property in general.

This paper addresses the expressivity and representation gap in Quantum Neural Networks by establishing a quantum analogue of the classical Kolmogorov--Arnold representation theorem. We propose a constructive approximation framework over fixed input coherent states, where the dependence of the function argument is embedded entirely in coordinate qubits, while the target function dictates a single outer unitary evolution. By applying a Sprecher-type representation to the rotation angle of the state, we demonstrate that the multidimensional operator factorises into \(2d+1\) commuting universal inner observables. We prove that the resulting measurement probability precisely reproduces the multidimensional Bernstein polynomial of the target function. For any continuous multivariate function, the joint quantum state converges uniformly to the target output register, linking classical superposition theory with probabilistic and coherent quantum circuits.
An energy-constrained implicit step-and-truncate algorithm and its robust error estimates

Deriving mesh-robust error bounds is an open problem for low-rank methods, including dynamical low-rank (DLR) and step-and-truncate (SAT) approaches, as highlighted in a recent review. Existing bounds can depend on Lipschitz constants that grow with inverse mesh size, making them impractical, particularly for kinetic equations, a major application of low-rank methods. We develop a unified framework for implicit SAT that provides a discrete counterpart of energy-localization analysis for nonlinear partial differential equations. By restricting numerical solutions to energy-localized regions, we obtain one-sided Lipschitz stability with constants independent of spatial resolution. The resulting error estimates and time-step restrictions are mesh robust, answering this open problem for the class of implicit SAT schemes covered by our assumptions. We emphasize that energy localization provides a general mechanism for mesh-independent robust error estimates in low-rank approximation, extending beyond the SAT methods considered here. Analogous results for DLR methods will be presented in subsequent work. Returning to implicit SAT, we demonstrate the broad applicability of the framework through error estimates for different classes of equations. Specifically, for semilinear parabolic and Vlasov--Poisson equations, we establish robust first-order error bounds for backward-Euler SAT under suitable regularity assumptions. Energy localization also has practical implications. We design an energy-constrained implicit SAT algorithm. Implicit SAT methods without energy constraints can select incorrect solution branches even when their algebraic residuals are small. Moreover, time-step reduction can be essential for continuation into larger energy regions. Numerical experiments support these conclusions.
Restricted conformal blocks and the braiding on Zhu algebra modules

Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra (VOA), not necessarily rational or $C_2$-cofinite, such that the category $\mathcal C_1(V)$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is semisimple and contains the generalized Verma modules associated to finite-dimensional modules over the Zhu algebra $A(V)$. Such VOAs include affine VOAs at admissible and generic levels. We prove that the bottom degree of Huang-Lepowsky's $P(w)$-tensor product module $M^1\boxtimes_{P(w)}M^2$ is isomorphic to the left $A(V)$-module $M^1\odot_{w,0}M^2$ arising from the restricted conformal blocks on $(¶^1,\infty,w,0)$. By shifting the marked points and using the parallel transport of the restricted conformal blocks, we construct an explicit braiding isomorphism on the category of finite-dimensional $A(V)$-modules, which is the restriction of the braiding isomorphism of Huang-Lepowsky-Zhang to the bottom degrees. For the affine VOA $L_k(\mathfrak g)$ at a positive integral level, it is given by the Casimir tensor of $\mathfrak g$ on certain quotients of tensor products of finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules, and at generic levels it recovers Drinfeld's commutativity isomorphism.
Worst-Case Relative Growth of Functionally Generated Portfolios under Restricted Market-Weight Dynamics

We study the worst-case relative growth rate of a fixed functionally generated portfolio under restrictions on market-weight dynamics over a compact convex market state space. For a nonempty compact forward shift-invariant path family, the pathwise wealth decomposition identifies the global rate with the minimum invariant average of the one-step $L$-divergence. For paths generated by a compact one-step transition relation, this rate is also the minimum over balanced transition measures, and a minimizing measure can be chosen on one relation basic set. For a fixed initial state, we study the lower limit of the minimum average $L$-divergence over the first $t$ periods as $t\to\infty$. We represent this value using empirical transition laws generated from that state. Their common state marginals are supported on chain-recurrent states that are chain-accessible from the initial state. The lower bound is obtained by minimizing the average $L$-divergence over balanced transition measures on chain-accessible basic sets. Finite exact reachability gives an upper bound. Examples show that both bounds can be strict. We also give a finite exact reachability condition under which the minimum average $L$-divergence over the first $t$ periods converges for paths confined to a basic set.
Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters

We prove that the shifts $ζ(s+id_jτ)$, $1\le j\le n$, are jointly universal for any nonzero real parameters $d_j$ with pairwise distinct absolute values. These restrictions are best possible. As an immediate consequence, we obtain generalized strong recurrence for arbitrary finite families of nonzero real parameters. Our proof uses Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem and a new variant of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem.
Underdamped Stochastic Optimal Transport with Landauer boundary conditions: machine learning and analytical solution
Julia Sanders; Dario Lucente; Marco Baldovin; Paolo Muratore-Ginanneschi

Finding optimal transport protocols for underdamped stochastic processes is a difficult yet important problem in control theory. In this paper we develop a direct method, based on machine learning, to find the optimal solution of the problem in the presence of non-linear boundary conditions, including those modelling the Landauer bit-erasure problem. The dynamics is steered from a single-peak to a double-peak distribution in position space, by only acting on a controllable external potential. The problem is highly non-linear, and analytical solutions are not available in general. We benchmark our numerical results with a perturbative expansion, which is expected to hold in a suitable overdamped limit.
On reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale flocking dynamics
Kamran Arora; Federico Cornalba; Ana Djurdjevac

Flocking refers to a phenomenon in collective motion where particles align their velocities with each other, commonly modelled using Cucker-Smale dynamics. In this work, we introduce and analyse two general reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale particle dynamics that encompass environmental and i.i.d.-type noises. Our models are computationally cheaper alternatives to the underlying particle system and preserve the flocking behaviour. To derive our reduced models, we consider suitable empirical particle densities which depend on position and time, but feature velocity dependency in a multiplicative fashion: this setup crucially allows for a very intuitive and convenient notion of flocking at the SPDE level. In $d=1$ we prove flocking of the reduced SPDE models, and, for the environmental noise, we also quantify the discrepancy between the reduced SPDE and mollified particle system. We also discuss the technical modifications required to extend the results to higher dimensions. We then provide extensive numerical experiments to verify our theoretical results in $d=1$ and to explore the behaviour of our models in $d=2$.
Uncertainty Quantification for Topological Treatment Effects

We present a unified framework for uncertainty quantification over filtration scale, extending the topological average treatment effect (TATE) analysis of \citet{kim-lee} to conditional mean confidence and individual effect prediction. For the conditional topological average treatment effect (CTATE), we derive multiplier confidence bands at a fixed covariate value, simultaneous over filtration scale, and prove validity in a correctly specified finite-dimensional regression regime, with explicit control of smoothing bias and nuisance-estimation error. For the individual topological treatment effect (ITTE), we integrate existing weighted and functional split-conformal methods to obtain finite-sample marginal prediction coverage under known target-to-calibration likelihood ratios, with a total-variation bound for estimated ratios. We also extend the current TATE silhouette stability analysis to the diagram-independent bound $\|Φ_r(D)-Φ_r(D')\|_\infty \le (1+2r)W_1(D,D')$ for $r\geq1$, recovering the known $r=1$ constant, and propagate diagram approximation error to prediction bands. The installable Python library \texttt{tcda\_uq} integrates mean confidence, individual prediction, and topological preprocessing, with tutorials and reproduction materials. Simulations and a PACCE lesion-measurement application illustrate the distinct coverage targets and the importance of declaring the target population.
Exact construction of quasi-uniform designs over polytopal domains

We develop two sampling algorithms for constructing extensible designs with mesh ratio at most two on finite unions of full-dimensional rational convex polytopes. Starting from a rational initial point, both algorithms produce rational coordinates and perform the geometric comparisons governing point selection exactly. This ensures that distance ties and geometric degeneracies are handled without rounding ambiguity, preserving the prescribed selection rules and mesh-ratio guarantee at every stage. The first algorithm, Local Exact Farthest-Point Sampling (LEFPS), implements a prescribed farthest-point rule by local updates of the restricted Voronoi diagram. The second algorithm, Arithmetic-Aware Admissible Sampling (AAS), minimizes the representation length of reduced rational coordinates over admissible fragment vertices and edge midpoints. Since the cost of exact arithmetic depends on coordinate lengths, we analyze both operation counts and bit complexity. For fixed dimension and input, each sampling rule admits an $O(N\log N)$ unit-cost implementation and a separate implementation with $\widetilde O(L_N)$ bit complexity, where $L_N$ is the total length of the output coordinates. On rational interval covers, every admissible sequence from the vertex-midpoint candidate set has logarithmic coordinate height. We also identify the ordered sequences explicitly for LEFPS on interval unions and four-dimensional coordinate-order domains, and for AAS on a rectangle and a nonconvex cross. These descriptions yield direct generation with $O(N)$ unit-cost work and optimal $Θ(N\log N)$ bit work, including exact quality measures at every prefix. Numerical experiments compare local Voronoi maintenance, coordinate growth, and direct generation.
Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules

For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.
On sparse universally rigid graphs in $\mathbb{R}$
Ole Gabsdil; Ezra Hirschi; Julien Portier

A graph is said to be 1-universally rigid if, for any generic realization of its vertices on the real line, the realization cannot be deformed out of the line in any higher-dimensional Euclidean space while preserving all edge lengths. In this paper, we investigate the sparsity of 1-universally rigid graphs in different manners. First, we show that an Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ is 1-universally rigid with high probability whenever $p \geq C\log n \cdot \log\log n/n$ for some sufficiently large constant $C>0$. These techniques also imply the existence of 1-universally rigid graphs of arbitrarily large girth, which resolves a problem suggested by Dantas e Moura, Jordán, and Silverman in a non-constructive manner. We also study how sparse a 1-universally rigid graph can be, proving that there exists an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every sufficiently large 1-universally rigid graph on $n$ vertices has at least $(3/2+\varepsilon)n$ edges. This breaks the natural $3/2$ barrier arising from degree-2 extensions and makes progress towards a question of Jordán and Nguyen.
Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras

We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $Γ$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.
A Fan-Type Theorem for Hamiltonian Berge Cycles in 3-Uniform Hypergraphs

Let $H$ be a simple $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n\ge7$ vertices, and put $τ_n=\binom{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}{2}$. We prove that $H$ has a Hamiltonian Berge cycle if its $2$-shadow is $2$-connected, every pair at Berge distance two has an endpoint of hypergraph degree at least $τ_n+1$, and every pair of codegree one has both endpoints above $τ_n$. The distance-two threshold is sharp, and the order range cannot be extended to $n=4,5,6$. The proof separates two structural arguments. A low-degree endpoint of an extremal longest Berge path forces Hamiltonicity, independently of the order and the degree threshold. For high-degree endpoints, injective charging and its equality cases force pairs of codegree one that permit further rotations. The cases $n=7,8$ are settled by exhaustive verification, with a completeness proof and a second implementation using direct vertex--hyperedge cycle search. Keywords: Hamiltonian Berge cycle; Fan-type condition; 3-uniform hypergraph; longest-path rotation; exhaustive verification.
Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields

We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Thélène, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.
Perfect state transfer on unicyclic graphs

We characterize adjacency perfect state transfer in connected unicyclic graphs: the transfer vertices are opposite degree-two vertices of a four-cycle, and the two attached trees satisfy a characteristic-polynomial condition. Except for the four-cycle, the transfer pair is unique and the minimum transfer time is $π/\sqrt2$. Outside the four-cycle, we obtain sharp lower bounds of $46$ on the order and $10$ on the maximum degree, and classify all examples of maximum degree at most $20$. A finite inverse construction enumerates all realizations of a prescribed eigenvalue support at the transfer vertices. For supports of size at least seven, we establish the sharp maximum-degree lower bound of $21$. Every seven-element support $\{0,\pm\sqrt2,\pm u\sqrt2,\pm v\sqrt2\}$, with odd integers $3\leq u<v$, is realizable, and every such realization has attachment depth at most four. Explicit branching rules give a minimum-order recurrence. Among all connected unicyclic graphs admitting perfect state transfer with seven-element eigenvalue support, the minimum order is $218$, attained uniquely up to isomorphism.
On sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of theta quotients
Koustav Banerjee; Kathrin Bringmann; Bernhard Heim; Ben Kane

Motivated by conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou on sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of infinite products, we study two families of theta quotients and their positive integral powers. We determine asymptotic formulas for their Fourier coefficients and use them to obtain explicit eventual periodic sign patterns. Our results provide new instances of the sign phenomena observed by Schlosser and Zhou and illustrate how dominant cusps determine the resulting sign patterns. These results were formalized and verified in Lean by AxiomProver.
The role of symmetry in the performance of the Thresholding Greedy Algorithm
José L. Ansorena; Miguel Berasategui; Alejandro Marcos

This paper continues the study of conditional symmetric systems initiated in arXiv:2601.15784 and solves several problems posed there. While the interaction between unconditionality and symmetry is well known in the Banach setting following the work in arXiv:2304.05888 and arXiv:2601.15784, we broaden the scope and address similar questions for spreading systems in the more general setting of quasi-Banach spaces. Our aim is twofold. On the one hand, we characterize which spreading systems of Banach spaces are unconditional. On the other hand, we provide examples of quasi-Banach spaces equipped with conditional systems with symmetry-related properties to illustrate the connections between symmetry, greedy-like properties, and the Schauder basis property in the absence of local convexity.
The coanalyticity of the reduced K-theory on modules over free tensor algebras of dualizable t-categories

In this paper, we formulate Land-Tamme's $\boxtimes$-construction and $\odot$-construction for continuous exact monads on dualizable stable $\infty$-categories, and establish the behaviour of localizing invariants on pushouts of left modules over continuous exact monads on dualizable stable $\infty$-categories. Combining the Land-Tamme theory of continuous exact monads with the theory of analytic functors in Goodwillie calculus, we show that the reduced K-theory on modules over free tensor algebras of dualizable t-categories is modified 1-coanalytic or modified 2-coanalytic, depending on the coconnectivity of the base algebras. In particular, this answers Efimov's question concerning coanalyticity in the affirmative.
Polynomially Solvable Cases of the Quadratic Binary Optimization Problem with a Fixed Cardinality Constraint
Thi Thanh Tu Le; Thorsten Koch

Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problems and their variant with a fixed cardinality constraint are both well-known NP-hard problems. While certain structural properties of the cost matrix can make some QUBO instances solvable in polynomial time, this advantage typically disappears once a cardinality constraint is added. In this work, we investigate specific structural conditions on the cost matrix under which the constrained version-quadratic binary optimization with a fixed cardinality-remains tractable.
A complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free motion for two robots
Jan Kamm; Antonio Terpin; Raffaello D'Andrea

Collision-free motion planning for multi-agent robotic systems remains an active research area because of the complexity of coordinating robot trajectories, with applications ranging from coordinated drone shows to autonomous operations on land, in the air, and on water. Importantly, the analytical difficulty of nonconvex collision-avoidance constraints has so far driven the development of exclusively numerical methods. We derive a complete analytical characterization of the optimal trajectories for two robots that start and end at rest, under double-integrator dynamics and a squared-acceleration objective. We prove that these trajectories belong to eight distinct contact families and determine which family applies for each configuration of initial and final positions. We analyze the geometrical properties of the optimal trajectories, provide a numerical algorithm for computing them, and discuss how these insights may improve the performance of existing numerical trajectory optimizers.
Haiman's conjecture for n <= 10: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity of monomial immanants

Haiman conjectured that for every partition $λ\vdash n$ and every $w\in S_n$ the polynomial $c_{λ,w}(q)$, a monomial character of the Hecke algebra evaluated at the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, has non-negative integer coefficients and is symmetric and unimodal, and he verified this by computer for $n\le7$. We verify it for every $n\le10$. Every stored Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial agrees with du Cloux's Coxeter3, and the coefficients pass several independent checks, including a comparison at all 16,796 codominant $w$ with chromatic quasisymmetric functions computed from colourings. Consequently, for $n\le10$ every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants, Stembridge's monomial immanant conjecture holds, and a class-function immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices if and only if it is non-negative at the block matrices $J_μ$. We use this to describe the order of normalised irreducible-character immanants on totally non-negative matrices for $n\le10$, and to prove Pate's inequalities there. On the full span of permutation monomials we give a Newton-polytope criterion for the coefficient of $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ to be non-negative throughout the totally non-negative cone, show that for $n=4,5$ this happens exactly when $X_w$ is smooth, and check by exact computation for $n\le10$ the proof of this for all $n$ given in a companion paper.
An Efficient Randomized Hierarchical Tucker Decomposition
Bram Leys; Karl Meerbergen; Nick Vannieuwenhoven; Mathijs Vivet

We introduce randomized algorithms for computing the hierarchical Tucker decomposition of high-order tensors. Unlike traditional algorithms performed in a sequential leaves-to-root direction, our algorithms traverse the dimension tree in a root-to-leaves direction, leveraging randomized sequential projections to accelerate the computation of intermediate subspaces. This strategy can reduce the computation time by an order of magnitude relative to prior randomized algorithms using the leaves-to-root direction, while guaranteeing quasi-optimal approximation. Although the theoretical error bound is slightly larger than for leaves-to-root methods, in all our experiments the practical error adheres to the classic bound. Our results highlight the method's potential for scalable tensor decompositions in high-dimensional data analysis.

Many kinds of generalised syntax, including internal categories, T-categories or polynomial monads, arise as monads in bicategories of a certain flavour: maps are some kind of span, and composition is some kind of pullback. We explain the pattern behind these similarities: each bicategory is stitched together from two simpler pieces by a distributive law, where the distributivity is governed by pullback. A key novelty is in the kind of distributive law we consider; where Rosebrugh and Wood considered distributive laws between categories, we instead consider pseudo-distributive laws between double categories. A key construction, drawing on work of Weber, obtains such a distributive law from a so-called co-crossed double category: one whose codomain functor is a fibration, and whose cartesian cells are stable under horizontal composition. We show the horizontal Kleisli double category of a monad T is co-crossed just when T is cartesian, and that the composite double category recovers T-spans; that the double category associated to an identity-on-objects functor is co-crossed just when that functor is a calibration in the sense of Bénabou; and that Street's calibrated bicategories yield co-crossed double categories in a similar manner, recovering the double category of polynomials of Gambino--Kock.
Numerical methods for nonlinear stochastic differential equations driven by subdiffusion
Qian Guo; Wei Liu; Ruchun Zuo

Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) driven by subdiffusion see great applications in anomalous transport and asset price dynamics. Trusted numerical methods are essential for their application in practice. In this paper, for SDEs driven by subdiffusion with superlinear coefficients, we propose a brand-new explicit numerical method. The sharp convergence rate is proved with new techniques. The potential application of the proposed method in numerically solving a generalized Fokker-Planck equation is also illustrated. Numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the theoretical results.
The virial--Kato method and the asymptotic stability of solitons of the generalized Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation
Scipio Cuccagna; Daniele Del Santo; Masaya Maeda

We apply to the generalized pure power Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation our method of combining high energy virial estimates with Kato smoothing, which closes the virial estimates in a natural way and allows us to prove a result of asymptotic stability for all the stable solitons with $c>1$ for all the exponents $p>1$.
A Parallel Heuristic for the Fixed Cardinality Binary Quadratic Program
Thi Thanh Tu Le; Thorsten Koch

The Fixed Cardinality Binary Quadratic Program (FCBQP) is an optimization problem that requires a prescribed number of variables to take the value 1. We propose a parallel CPU-based heuristic that combines impact-based variable selection, tabu search, guided restarts, and a shared elite pool. Computational experiments on 342 benchmark instances from the maximum dispersion problem, k-clique problem, and minimum graph bisection problem show that the new algorithm is competitive and can reach best-known or reference values on instances with more than 20000 variables within one minute.

We study self-orthogonal $t$-$(v,k,λ)$ designs satisfying the condition that the codes generated by the designs are self-orthogonal codes whose codewords of minimum weight $k$ correspond to the blocks. A classification of such designs is given under the conditions that $t\geq \lfloor k/4\rfloor+1\geq2$ and $t \le 11$. This yields a classification of self-orthogonal codes of minimum weight $k$ whose codewords of minimum weight form a $t$-design under the same conditions.
AMPERe: an exactly divergence-free quadrature-by-expansion evaluator for near-surface Biot--Savart and virtual-casing fields in fusion geometries
H. Betar; Y. Sarazin; V. Grandgirard; D. Zarzoso

Accurate magnetic-field evaluation on and near current-carrying surfaces is a recurring computational bottleneck in magnetic-confinement fusion. As targets approach the source surface, Biot--Savart and virtual-casing kernels become singular, causing standard Gauss--Legendre and upsampled trapezoidal quadratures to lose accuracy. We introduce AMPERe, a quadrature-by-expansion (QBX) evaluator for vector magnetostatic kernels on general three-dimensional, non-axisymmetric tokamak and stellarator geometries. The method develops a spherical-harmonic QBX formulation for the vector Biot--Savart and virtual-casing (Stratton--Chu) fields and expresses the resulting magnetic field as the analytic curl of a regular-solid-harmonic vector potential. This construction yields a divergence-free discrete field at every expansion order, provides analytic derivatives, and enables an a priori separation of truncation, quadrature, and geometric errors. On the rotating-ellipse benchmark of Malhotra et al. [1], QBX maintains a relative error of 2--5 x 10^{-6} throughout the near-surface regime at distance-independent cost, whereas upsampled trapezoidal quadrature exhibits O(1) errors and requires node counts scaling as (h/d)^2. AMPERe is implemented as a header-only, performance-portable Kokkos library supporting CPU and GPU backends, with target-specific and local-correction accelerations validated against the baseline. The method is further demonstrated on realistic Wendelstein 7-X configurations, including sheet-current and virtual-casing field evaluations.
Distributed Grid Search for Hyperparameter Tuning
Constança De Herdeiro Cachim; Andrea Martin; Nicola Bastianello

The performance of many distributed optimization algorithms over peer-to-peer networks strongly depends on the choice of their hyperparameters. However, existing selection rules often require global quantities, yield conservative choices, or are tied to specific algorithms and hyperparameters. We propose Distributed Grid Search (D-GS), a consensus-based search method that evaluates and selects hyperparameter configurations across the network, requiring only the ability to run the tuned algorithm and evaluate local gradients. We also propose a zoom-in variant, Distributed Zoom Grid Search (D-ZGS), which improves empirical performance at a reduced cost. We prove that both methods terminate in finite time with all agents holding the same hyperparameter configuration, and quantify the (sub)optimality of this configuration. Numerical experiments on linear and logistic regression show that D-GS closely matches a centralized reference and that tuning and deployment cost a fraction of deploying algorithms with hyperparameters tuned using theoretical results.
Truncated Dirichlet estimates for Bloch functions
Iason Efraimidis; Adrián Llinares; Alejandro Mas

We study the truncated Dirichlet functional \[ Φ_n (f) = \sum_{k = 1}^n k |a_k|^2, \quad f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^\infty a_k z^k, \] when $f$ belongs to the Bloch space. If $n \geq 27$, we find a normalized Bloch function $f_n$ such that \[ Φ_n (f_n) > n B_n^2, \] where $B_n = \max \{ |a_n| : \| f \|_{\mathcal{B}} = 1 \}$, thus proving that an inequality by Kayumov and Wirths cannot be extended to large values of $n$. Nevertheless, we show that the inequality $Φ_n(f) \leq n B_n^2$ holds for all normalized functions when $n \leq 9$.
Direct and indirect operator learning strategies for parametric optimal control problems
Juan J. Forero-Hernández; Francisco Guillén-González; Élder J. Villamizar-Roa

This paper focuses on the use of learning nonlinear operators via Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) for approximating the solutions of optimal control problems. We study two operator learning strategies, namely, indirect and direct, both based on DeepONets, for parametric families of optimal control problems where the same problem must be solved many times for different initial data, different parameters, different cost function weights, and different bounds defining the set of the admissible controls. In the indirect strategy two DeepONets approximate the solution operators of the state and adjoint systems, and their predictions are used inside iterative projected gradient algorithms for finding the optimal control. In the direct strategy, a single DeepONet approximates the operator that maps directly to the optimal control generated by a reference solver; consequently, a new control is obtained through a single evaluation of the network. In order to analyze the computational cost, the efficiency, the speed and the accuracy of the learning strategies, we consider an optimal control problem related to an ordinary differential system that describes the temporal evolution of the glioblastoma growth subject to therapeutic interventions. For this specific optimal control problem we propose a discretize-then-optimize strategy, based on an implicit-explicit finite difference method, and then, we develop several numerical experiments in order to compare the two DeepONet learning strategies for this problem. The proposed operator learning DeepONet strategies can be adapted to approximate large classes of optimal control problems related to diverse differential systems.
Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes

Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective. In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes.
