We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csiszár, Körner, Lovász, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lovász theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tunçel on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph-energy conjecture.
Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits for the total edge-length of random directional nearest-neighbour graphs
Nicholas Georgiou; Qasem M. Tawhari; Andrew Wade

We study planar random spatial graphs defined by inserting an edge between every point of a homogeneous Poisson process on the unit square and a nearest-neighbour within a fixed cone of directions (if there is such a point). We prove large-sample distributional limit theorems for the total Euclidean edge length of the graph, where the limit distribution is either Gaussian (due to contributions from the bulk) or, when one or both of the boundaries of the cone of directions align with the edges of the square, a convolution of Gaussian with a non-Gaussian law arising from boundary effects due to long edges near a boundary. This work extends previously known cases, including the ordinary nearest-neighbour graph (full cone of directions), where the Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Bickel & Breiman and Avram & Bertsimas, and Bhatt & Roy's minimal directed spanning forest (with 'south-west' directions), where the non-Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Penrose & Wade.
The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$

We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two. We also prove numerical dimension zero and construct the unique projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal minimal model. Its Picard number is one and its canonical divisor has order two. The perfect cone compactification is a Mori dream space, and the birational automorphism group of $\mathcal{A}_6$ is trivial. The proof combines normal vanishing on the Prym locus, polar intersections on abelian boundary fibers, and an exact theta calculation. A discrepancy estimate recovers the modular open subset from the minimal model.
Local $Tb$ theorems in non-homogeneous metric spaces, and applications to caloric measure
Andrea Merlo; Mihalis Mourgoglou; Carmelo Puliatti

We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calderón-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. As an application in the parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(σ)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $σ$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.
Integer-Quantized Hierarchical Matrices with Adaptive Bit Allocation
Erin Carson; Xinye Chen; Ritesh Khan

We present an adaptive bitwidth allocation method for quantizing low-rank factors in hierarchical matrices in order to decrease storage while meeting a given constraint on their reconstruction error. For the bitwidth allocation we formulate a discrete storage minimization problem and show that an optimal assignment can give larger singular values at least as many bits as smaller ones. We further develop a greedy algorithm that meets the specified max-norm quantization error budget. We investigate a hierarchical block partition in which all of the non-diagonal blocks are represented by quantized low-rank factors and only dense blocks remain dense; in this way a global reconstruction bound related to $η_k$ and $R_k$ is obtained, with the former and latter being bounds on the truncation and reconstruction arithmetic errors, respectively. Extensive simulations, carried out with kernel and BEM matrices under block-relative budgets, indicate that the proposed method achieves a reduction in storage of up to $44.3\times$ when compared to storing the complete matrix densely in FP64, and a reduction of up to $5.70\times$ when compared to the FP64 low-rank factors within the same partition, together with measured reconstruction errors that remained below the maximum norm bounds in all the hierarchical tests.
Full immersions in Eulerian group-labeled graphs
Ioannis Eleftheriadis; Rose McCarty; Caleb McFarland; Evangelos Protopapas; Paul Wollan

An immersion of a graph H in a graph G is full if the immersion uses every edge of G. We give a structure theorem for group-labeled Eulerian graphs excluding a fixed group-labeled graph as a full immersion.
Hypersurface and Foliation Isoparametric Transfer for Generalized $(α,β)$-Metrics

Let $F=αΦ(q,s)$ be a regular generalized $(α,β)$-metric, where $q=\|β\|_α^2$ and $s=β/α$, endowed with the Busemann--Hausdorff or Holmes--Thompson volume. We derive explicit comparison formulas for the induced hypersurface volume and the associated volume mean curvature and use them to study two transfer problems suggested by the Randers case. The first asks whether the same hypersurface is isoparametric for $α$ and $F$; the second asks whether the same regular foliation is isoparametric for both metrics. Exact local and global criteria are obtained. Their Randers specializations recover the corresponding hypersurface transfer and the condition $df(W)=φ(f)$. We also prove an all-normal induced-volume rigidity theorem and construct a complete non-Randers example realizing both transfer mechanisms.
Graphical Models Induced by Irreversible Event Accumulation on Trees

Decomposable graphical models are usually adopted for their computational convenience rather than derived from a data-generating mechanism. We show that a special class of them arises naturally from the irreversible accumulation of events along a branching history. Each event is attached to an edge of a latent rooted tree and is inherited by everything below that edge; an observation records which events have occurred at a randomly chosen node, not necessarily a leaf. When the tree is a path, this is the cumulative coding of an ordinal variable, whose indicators form a Markov chain; in the general tree case the Markov chain is replaced by a junction tree. The conditional independence graph of the event indicators is always decomposable and, in fact, is the line graph of the tree (maximal cliques correspond to nodes where two or more edges meet and separators are the single events on the edges joining two such nodes). The graph determines the tree up to the choice of root. A connected graph arises in this way if, and only if, it is chordal, any two of its maximal cliques share at most one vertex, no vertex is in three maximal cliques, and the graph is such that any two maximal cliques share at most one vertex. This provides a simple graphical test for compatibility with the mechanism (necessary but not sufficient, as irreversibility also constrains the distribution's support). The structure breaks down if we look at just the leaves, and measurement error destroys the exact screening and leads to a denser graph rather than simply a weaker dependence. We discuss inference, provide diagnostics for departures such as recurrent events, illustrate them on some simulated data and discuss their application in the context of mutation accumulation and lineage tracing where both ancestral and descendant types are sampled together.
Asymptotically Compatible Variational Energy Dissipation Laws and Structure-Preserving Variable-Step Linear Relaxation Schemes for a Subdiffusive Tumor-Nutrient Model
Hui Yu; Zhaoyang Wang; Ping Lin

In this work, we develop a mass-conservative subdiffusive tumor-nutrient model coupled through chemotaxis and memory-dependent reaction exchange, together with structure-preserving variable-step linear relaxation schemes. A weighted Riemann-Liouville identity is proved and used to construct a variational energy and the associated energy dissipation law for the proposed model. Both the model and the associated variational energy dissipation law are asymptotically compatible with their integer-order counterparts as the fractional order approaches one. For numerical approximation, we discretize the Riemann-Liouville fractional derivatives using the L1R formula on nonuniform time meshes and derive the associated discrete weighted inequality. We first construct a variable-step linear relaxation scheme for the subdiffusive model. Then, to mitigate alternating perturbations induced by the auxiliary-variable error and amplified by the L1R convolution at small fractional orders, we construct a temporally damped linear relaxation scheme. Since temporal damping leaves the auxiliary-variable recurrence unchanged, we further introduce an a posteriori relaxation correction to reduce alternating errors in the auxiliary variable. All three schemes preserve total mass, are proven to satisfy discrete variational energy dissipation laws using the discrete weighted inequality, and remain consistent with the integer-order limit. Several numerical examples are presented to validate the accuracy and stability of the proposed schemes.
Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators.
Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation

With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.
Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$

The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.
Failure of the $H^1\times H^1\longrightarrow L^{1/2,\infty}$ estimate for the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal function and applications
Sanghyuk Lee; Ji Li; Chaojie Wen; Liangchuan Wu

In contrast to Christ's theorem that the lacunary spherical maximal operator is bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ ($d\geq2$), we show that the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal operator $$ \mathcal B_{\mathrm{lac}}(f,g)(x) =\sup_{\ell\in\mathbb Z} \Bigl|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-2^\ell y)\,g(x-2^\ell z)\,dσ(y,z)\Bigr| $$ is not bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)\times H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ for any $d\geq1$. In particular, it is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, we construct two finite linear combinations of smooth, compactly supported, mean-zero $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$-atoms for which the ratio of the weak $L^{1/2}$ quasinorm to the product of the two Hardy norms is at least $c_d\log(N+1)$. This lower bound holds already for the supremum over a suitable set of $N$ dyadic radii. For $d=1$ this answers the case $p=q=1$ of a question in Borges's survey. For every $k\ge3$ and $d\ge1$, a modification of the construction proves that the lacunary $k$-linear spherical maximal operator does not map $(H^1(\mathbb R^d))^k$ into $L^{1/k,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. We also indicate extensions to certain hypersurfaces and to horizontal spherical averages on the Heisenberg group.

Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $χ$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$. To the character $χ$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_χ=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $χ$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_χ$. We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition. As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.
Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on Kähler manifolds
Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected Kähler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.

The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem is a classical extremal problem in discrete geometry. We prove that, for all positive integers $n$ and $r$, every sequence of $4^r n$ lattice points in $\mathbb{Z}^r$ contains $n$ points whose centroid is again a lattice point.
Rota universality of shifts on trees

We consider shift operators on infinite directed trees. We prove that under very mild assumptions on the structure of the tree, the resulting operator is universal (in the sense of Rota). We show connections between the spectrum of the operator and the frequency of branching in the tree.
Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms

We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.
Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity

The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic invariant measure is subsequently established by constructing a generalized coupling through a controlled auxiliary equation. Finally, the results are extended to other types of viscosities as well as to different stochastic hydrodynamical models.
Multi-excited random walks on general trees

We study multi-excited random walks on infinite locally finite trees. The model is described by placing a stack of ``cookies'' at each vertex, with one cookie consumed on each successive visit. As long as cookies remain, the walk is in an excited regime and makes nearest-neighbour steps according to a prescribed sequence of biases. Once the stack is exhausted, the walk is in a non-excited regime and moves uniformly among the neighbouring vertices. The model is closely connected to foraging ecology, where repeated visits to a location can deplete local resources and thereby influence the attractiveness of that location for future visits. We prove that the process exhibits a sharp phase transition between recurrence and transience. The critical threshold is determined by the branching-ruin number of the tree, which is equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the tree's boundary under a suitable metric. Our result substantially extends Zerner's recurrence-transience criterion for multi-excited random walks on $\mathbb Z$ [Probab. Theory Related Fields 133 (2005)] to general trees.
A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials

Let $π_n$ be a uniform parking function of size $n$. We determine the scale at which its first $k$ coordinates cease to be close in total variation to $k$ independent uniform variables on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The distance is comparable to $1\wedge \sqrt{k\log(k+1)/n}$, uniformly for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and tends to one above the scale $n/\log n$. At the critical scale $k\simλn/\log n$, it converges to $2Φ(\sqrt{λ/π})-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. A key ingredient is the Lorentzian property of the occupation generating polynomial of parking functions. Together with a strengthened Han inequality, this yields a relative entropy estimate for approximation by the product of the one-coordinate marginals.
An HDG-type discretization of 1D embedded blood flow in complex networks with Riemann-coupled junctions
Raksha Devi; Luca Heltai; Lucas O. Müller

We present a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for one-dimensional blood flow in arterial networks with Windkessel boundary conditions. The scheme uses a Harten--Lax--van Leer (HLL) numerical flux and implicit time integration. After spatial discretization, the complete network---including cell states, hybrid traces, junction conditions, and dynamic $\mathrm{RCR}$ terminal pressures---is written as a residual index-one differential--algebraic equation (DAE) and integrated with variable-step, variable-order backward differentiation formulas. The implicit formulation removes the CFL stability restriction of explicit schemes and allows variable-order, variable-step solvers. The resulting single global residual and Jacobian for the network and its terminal dynamics also provide a natural interface for monolithic coupling with external nonlinear models. We establish local solvability and a semi-discrete energy balance, and show numerically optimal convergence rates for both solution variables in the $L^2$ norm and the broken $H^1$ seminorm. The solver is validated against established benchmarks, including an aortic bifurcation and a $37$-artery network, and is further applied to a cerebral arterial network. Mass conservation is observed in a synthetically generated anatomical liver network of $8\,\mathrm{k}$ vessels, and strong-scaling studies are performed on synthetic networks of $50\,\mathrm{k}$ and $100\,\mathrm{k}$ vessels.
The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
Shane Chern; Trieu Nguyen; Chanh Tran; Tanay Wakhare

Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.
Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids
Aidan Looney; Annie Weathers; Nicholas Judson

Military installation energy readiness depends on having sufficient resources to sustain mission-critical loads throughout a prolonged utility outage. This paper develops a method to help operators manage energy resources during normal grid-connected operation while preserving islanded readiness. A robust viability kernel identifies combinations of battery energy, fuel, and load-shifting capability sufficient to sustain critical load under uncertain demand and photovoltaic generation. A probability bound translates stochastic generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count selected to meet a specified availability requirement at islanding. Case studies for a fourteen-day islanding requirement at 0.999 islanding-entry availability show that advance warning of an outage can be used to prepare resources to meet a higher readiness requirement before islanding begins. The case studies further demonstrate that economic-only operation and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy can fail to sustain critical load for the required duration, whereas enforcing the resource-dependent requirement preserves readiness at a modest increase in modeled grid-connected operating cost. These results demonstrate how active resource management can preserve long-duration energy readiness. The framework also helps commanders understand how readiness changes with operating conditions, even when the available resources remain the same.
A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$

Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.
Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces

We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface. Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve. Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is constant in linear series on K3 surfaces.
Graphical Modeling from Marginal Information via Optimal Transport
Ulysse Naepels; Paul Freulon; Victor M. Panaretos

A graphical model represents multivariate interactions through conditional independence, but requires jointly observed samples to be fitted to data. When individuals cannot be tracked and only marginal observations are available, as with destructive measurements leading to cross-sectional data, the problem of graphical modeling is confounded with that of assembling a joint law. We show how simultaneous graphical modeling and joint law assembly can be realized via a multi-marginal optimal transport problem with graphical cost. Focusing on Gaussian marginals, we generate a joint law satisfying the Markov properties prescribed by a given graph. Within the class of joint distributions respecting the graph and marginals constraints, our construction selects a member by making the interactions set by the graph as strong as possible under a dependence budget measured by relative entropy. In the empirical setting, where only estimates of the marginals are available, we examine the stability of the problem under perturbations of both the marginals and of the graph weights. The resulting error splits into an estimation term, vanishing with the sample size, and a specification term, which quantifies the cost of a misspecified graph. Finally, we illustrate these findings by numerical experiments.
Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces

We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.
Higher-order jet and its application to the Novikov conjecture

In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the deffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher order $μ$-discreteness for subgroup $Γ< {\rm Diff}(M)$. As applications, we show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher order $μ$-discreteness.
Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions

We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.
Invariant probability measures on holomorphic functions on the unit disk

We study probability measures on the space of holomorphic functions on the unit disk that are invariant under pre-composition by conformal automorphisms and give no mass to constant functions. We determine the slowest possible growth of functions supported by such measures. Let $M_f(R)$ denote the maximum modulus of $f$ on the hyperbolic ball of radius $R$ centered at the origin. We show that given a non-decreasing function $G:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$, there exists an $\textrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$-invariant probability measure $μ$ on $\textrm{Hol}(\mathbb{D}, \mathbb{C}) \setminus \{\textrm{constant functions} \}$ such that $\log^+ M_f(R)=O_f(G(R))$ for $μ$ almost every $f$ if and only if $\int_1^\infty (R/G(R)) \, dR <\infty$. For the lower bound, we use a mass transport argument to show that almost every trajectory of the gradient flow of $\log |f|$ has finite energy. To establish sharpness, we construct holomorphic functions of slow growth on infinite Riemann surfaces.
Bjarki Geir Benediktsson; Dugald Macpherson; Isolde Adler

A \emph{Johnson graph} $J(n,k)$ is a graph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of an underlying set of size $n$ where two vertices are adjacent if they intersect in a subset of size $k-1$. We extend the definition to allow infinite parameters and we study a natural limit theory $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ of Johnson graphs. We show that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is complete and we give an axiomatisation of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, from which we obtain a complete description of the models of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$. We use this to show tameness properties of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, namely that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is $ω$-stable of Morley rank $ω$, but not monadically dependent. In particular it follows that the class of all finite Johnson graphs is stable, and therefore dependent but not monadically dependent.

In many applications, we are interested in studying an object of interest $x$. However, its properties are often not directly measurable. Instead, we only observe $y = F(x)$, where the (known) function $F$ is referred to as the forward mapping. To infer about $x$ from the observation $y$, we seek an (approximate) inverse mapping $x \approx F^{-1}(y)$. This process is known as solving the inverse problem. In practice, the inverse mapping $F^{-1}$ may be ill-defined or discontinuous, which forces us to choose a certain solution from many possible ones based on prior assumptions on $x$. Such assumptions about $x$ are typically incorporated into the inversion process through regularization. Therefore, the first part of this course focuses on the classical regularization theory of inverse problems. In the second part, we transition to algorithmic approaches for solving inverse problems. The foundation for this lies in the variational formulation of inverse problems, where reconstructions are obtained by minimizing specific functionals. Here, we will explore key optimization principles, discuss their practical implementation, and examine how they contribute to robust reconstructions. Today, classical methods are often modified to incorporate data-driven machine learning techniques, which improve the empirical performance. However, this often comes at the cost of explainability or convergence guarantees. Such properties are critical, for example, in medical applications, where one wants to be confident that reconstructed abnormalities are of physical nature and not phantoms resulting from the method. For these reasons, we discuss a number of machine learning methods for inverse problems, such as unrolling techniques, learned regularizers and plug-and-play methods, and explore their performance guarantees.

Let $Σ\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact $C^2$ hypersurface with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We prove the sharp matrix-dimension-independent Schatten-valued Stein--Tomas range \[ R_Σ:L^p(\mathbb R^3;S^a)\longrightarrowγ(L^2(Σ),S^a), \qquad 1<a<\infty,\quad 1\le p\le\min\{a,4/3\}. \] The core endpoint is $E_Σ:γ(L^2(Σ),S^4)\to L^4(\mathbb R^3;S^4)$. After squaring the quartic norm, multiplication lands in the Hilbert--Schmidt class. A local coarea argument splits resonant quartets according to the shorter adjacent frequency chord, producing a dimension-free row/column estimate for elliptic and hyperbolic curvature. We also show that Gaussian type $4/3$ alone does not characterize the corresponding endpoint for arbitrary Banach spaces. Applications include matrix Herglotz waves, a two-dimensional Schrödinger $L^4$ estimate, and free spectral-measure bounds.
G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension

For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.
The Torelli Group and Euler Class Zero $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Representations
Marit Bobb; James Farre; Peter Smillie

We prove that every representation of a closed surface group of genus at least $3$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ that is sufficiently close (but not equal to) a representation that has non-compact solvable image has a simple closed separating curve that is mapped to a non-trivial elliptic element in $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. This can be seen as evidence for an affirmative answer to a question of Bowditch and a conjecture of Goldman.
Degenerate complex structures on surfaces and stability conditions

Physical heuristics suggest that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions of a projective Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ should be related to the moduli space of complex structures on its mirror $X^\vee$. On the other hand, recent work in the literature introduces a modular partial compactification, $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$, of a quotient of the space of stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}^{b}(X)$. We provide some mathematical evidence for the aforementioned heuristics by proving that for curves and surfaces, certain boundary strata in $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ describe degenerate complex structures on $X^\vee$. Along the way, we introduce a criterion for producing boundary points of $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ when $\mathcal{D}$ is an arbitrary $k$-linear triangulated category. As a byproduct, we deduce the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on certain quotients of the derived categories of K3 and Enriques surfaces.
Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
Antun Milas; Jan-Willem M. van Ittersum

Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems. To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables. The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank. The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.
The S-function at arbitrary order: hyperplanes of symmetries and the realisability condition
L. G. S. Duarte; L. A. C. P. da Mota

For a scalar equation $y^{(n)}=φ(x,y,\dots,y^{(n-1)})$ the $S$-function of the extended Prelle--Singer method is a vector $S=(S_0,\dots,S_{n-2})$, the null-form vector of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Lakshmanan and collaborators, and the jet gradient of a first integral solves the adjoint of the variational equation. We describe the solutions of the system satisfied by $S$ intrinsically, and determine which of them come from first integrals. Over the field $C$ of first integrals the solutions are exactly the hyperplanes of the $n$-dimensional space $VV$ of symmetry characteristics, recovered from $n-1$ independent characteristics by a Plücker formula; in flow-box coordinates they are the hyperplane fields on the local space of leaves. A solution is the $S$-vector of a first integral if and only if the corresponding hyperplane field is integrable. This Frobenius condition splits into the $S$-system itself plus $\binom n3$ further differential conditions, so it is vacuous for $n=2$ and a genuine restriction for every $n\ge3$, for which we give an explicit non-realisable solution. The same picture explains why $λ$-symmetries and $S$-functions coincide only when $n=2$: line fields and hyperplane fields agree only on surfaces. For the computation of $S$ we record that the system is equivalent to one scalar equation for the last component, which is the Riccati form of the adjoint variational equation, and we spell out what this does and does not imply for a rational search.
Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
Guoqing Wang; Linlin Wang; Jun Yue

Bérczi, Gehér, Imolay, Lovász, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,α}$, $0<α<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.
On Terao's conjecture for at most nine planes

In this note we show that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of at most nine planes in the complex projective $3$-space. Moreover, we show that every essential and irreducible free arrangement of at most nine planes in $\mathbb{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is divisionally free, and we list all intersection lattices of such arrangements. Our approach is based on Ziegler's restriction theorem and a simple count involving the numbers of multiple lines. As a by-product, we show that Cynk--Szemberg octic arrangements are never free. Finally, motivated by a recent work of Dimca and Pokora, we present examples of weak Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements, including pairs of octic arrangements leading to rigid double octic Calabi--Yau threefolds.
One Polynomial Field for Every Euler Step and the Flow: Polynomial Dynamics for P and PSPACE

We construct, for each deterministic Turing machine that halts on all inputs, one polynomial vector field with rational coefficients that performs the same logical computation at unit Euler step, at every smaller or variable step in $(0,1]$ with divergent sum, and along the flow. This unifies discrete-time and continuous-time computation by polynomial dynamics, which earlier characterizations treated separately. For a machine making $T$ transitions in space $H$, a logical scale $h=2^{-s}$ with $s=O(H)$ suffices, with physical time $O(s(T+s))$, drift disturbances up to $h^{2K}$ for a fixed exponent $K$, and $2Ks+3$ fractional bits at unit step. On a fixed compact domain, polynomial time and robust eventual decision characterize P and PSPACE, respectively, with polynomial scale thresholds and no supplied stabilization horizon in the space case. Without sign, floor or conditional primitives, margin amplification at bounded speed, overlapping polynomial gates and interval-product estimates give the common realization, from which we derive shared logical traces, fixed-field PSPACE-complete prediction and a robust safety family with polynomial certificates common to all Euler steps and the flow.

Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_μ$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor. Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation. We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$. In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.
A nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth
Barbara Niethammer; Lorena Pohl; Juan J. L. Velázquez

We study a nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth in a biological membrane exposed to a periodic electric potential, where the growth term is modified through the first moment of the solution $n_1(t)$. We show that for initial data $f_0$ with noncompact support it holds $n_1(t) \rightarrow \infty$ , whereas for $f_0$ with compact support the limit of $n_1$ depends sensitively on the data. For a broad class of initial data we additionally obtain $n_1 \sim t^{\frac{1}{2}}$. In the case of a constant external potential we further prove that solutions converge to the self-similar solution having the same tail behaviour as $f_0$.
Hilbertian Fields and Profinite Iterated Monodromy Groups Over Transcendental Elements with Specializations of Infinite Index

Given a field $L$ and polynomial $f(x)/L$, one can consider the indices of the profinite iterated monodromy groups formed over the ground field within the profinite iterated monodromy groups over elements transcendental over $L$. For any countable Hilbertian field $k$, we show random Galois fixed field extensions almost surely make the indices infinite over all ground field elements, with certain conditions on $f(x)$. This is a generalization of a result in arXiv:2012.03076 by Dittmann and Kadets.
Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups

We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.
Measuring the Value of Communication in Multi-Agent Tracking Under Finite-Rate Belief Sharing
Danial Dehghani; Maximilian Lübke; Zahra Seifaei; Norman Franchi

This paper investigates the value of communica- tion (VoC) in cooperative multi-agent tracking under rate- constrained information exchange. Although prior work has studied distributed tracking, quantized communication, and robust fusion, it remains unclear at what communication rate most of the achievable tracking gain is obtained, beyond which additional communication resources yield only marginal benefit. We consider stationary agents that observe a moving target through heterogeneous range and bearing measurements, perform local extended Kalman filtering (EKF), quantize their posterior state means, and fuse exchanged information via covariance intersection (CI). Performance is evaluated versus communication rate relative to no-communication baselines, a centralized oracle, and a CI-perfect reference. The results show that communication is not uniformly beneficial: very low rates can degrade performance due to coarse quantization, whereas moderate rates recover most of the achievable gain. In the considered scenario, increasing the rate from 4 to 12 bit/s per agent reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 13.93 m to 6.35 m, while a further increase to 32 bit/s per agent improves it only marginally to 5.93 m. This reveals a clear knee region at moderate rates, beyond which the remaining loss is mainly due to the conservatism of the fusion architecture. Overall, the proposed framework characterizes low-rate degradation, communication-efficient operation, and diminishing returns, while highlighting the joint role of rate and sensing geometry in determining communication benefit.
A Liouville theorem for plurisubharmonic functions with periodic complex Monge-Ampère measure

We study entire continuous plurisubharmonic solutions of the complex Monge-Ampère equation $(i\partial\bar\partial u)^n=2^n n!μ$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$, in the Bedford-Taylor sense, where $μ\not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite Borel measure periodic with respect to a lattice of full real rank. We assume that $μ$ is locally dominated by complex Monge-Ampère measures of Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic functions, a condition under which the existence theorem of Demailly et al. yields Hölder continuous periodic correctors. Under this assumption, we prove that every such solution with positive two-sided quadratic growth can be written uniquely, up to an additive constant, as the sum of a real quadratic polynomial and a Hölder continuous periodic function.

We prove an equivalence between the existence of a unique Kähler-Einstein metric on a degeneration of Fano varieties and uniform CM minimization. This proves a discretely valued analogue of the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture, in the sense of non-Archimedean geometry. As a main tool, we prove that Ding stability of a degeneration implies uniform Ding minimization, proving a converse to work of Blum-Xu. We also prove an analogous result in geometric invariant theory (GIT), stating that uniform GIT height minimization of a family of points is equivalent to GIT stability, proving a converse to work of Wang, Wang-Xu and the author.
Multi-split Multiple-sets Implicit Convex Feasibility Seeking As Split Inverse Problems

We introduce a new class of problems, termed multi-split multiple-sets implicit convex feasibility problems (MSMS-ICFPs), define a proximity function for it and analyze its properties under certain assumptions on the involved general point-to-set operators. Additionally, we discuss its properties for a special class of point-to-set operators. For these kinds of point-to-set operators, we deploy a new iterative algorithm to solve the associated MSMS-ICFP and show that any sequence generated by it converges in norm to a solution of the MSMS-ICFP whenever a solution exists (i.e., in the consistent case). We also define a generalized proximity function for the MSMS-ICFP using the Bregman distance. Based on this function, we present a generalized simultaneous projection gradient algorithm for the split feasibility problem with multiple output sets, by examining various related results. We conclude by discussing several further special cases of the MSMS-ICFP.
Rigidity of Kähler-Finsler Metrics with Constant Radial Curvature
Jinling Li; Longjie Li; Chunhui Qiu

In this paper, we prove that a smooth strongly pseudoconvex Kähler--Finsler metric $F$ satisfying the constant radial curvature condition \[ Ω(χ,\barχ)χ=cF^2χ, c\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}, \] is induced by a Hermitian Kähler metric of holomorphic sectional curvature $2c$. Under the Abate--Patrizio curvature symmetry \[ \langleΩ(\cdot,\barχ)χ,χ\rangle =\langleΩ(χ,\barχ)\cdot,χ\rangle, \] this result gives Hermitian rigidity for nonzero constant holomorphic sectional curvature and the classification of complete simply connected metrics of negative curvature. As an application, we show that the Kobayashi metric of a bounded strongly convex domain with smooth boundary is Kähler--Finsler if and only if the domain is biholomorphic to the unit ball. We also prove that the universal cover of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain $D $ with smooth boundary is biholomorphic to the unit ball if and only if its Kobayashi metric is a smooth strongly pseudoconvex Kähler--Finsler metric. Furthermore, we give two explicit examples to illustrate the distinction between the weakly Kähler--Finsler and Kähler--Finsler conditions.
Complexity of finding color-avoiding connected components
Panna Tímea Fekete; Roland Molontay; Kitti Varga

Two vertices of a (not necessarily properly) arc-colored digraph are called arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected if, after the removal of the arcs of any at most $\ell$ colors, they remain strongly $k$-arc-connected. The arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components are maximal sets of vertices such that any two of those vertices belonging to the set are arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected in the graph. We investigate the problems of finding the arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components and the maximal arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected subgraphs of an arc-colored digraph. We also consider possible generalizations to $k$-vertex-connectivity and to vertex-colored digraphs. We show that despite the seemingly minor differences in definitions, the complexity of these problems varies significantly: some can be solved in polynomial time, while others are NP-hard. It also turns out that in some cases the problem is NP-hard when multiple colors can be assigned to each vertex, but the problem becomes polynomial-time solvable when each vertex is single-colored.
The Hénon equation beyond the critical Sobolev exponent

We consider the Dirichlet problem $-Δu=|x|^αu^p$, $u>0$ in $Ω$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, where $Ω\subset R^N$, $N\ge 3$, is a bounded domain containing the origin and $α>0$. We prove that a solution exists for every exponent $1<p<p_α=\frac{N+2+2α}{N-2}$, in particular in the whole Sobolev-supercritical range $\frac{N+2}{N-2}\le p<p_α$, provided $Ω$ is invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and satisfies an angular monotonicity condition. This class contains the balls, the oblate ellipsoids of revolution, lens-shaped domains, and non-convex, non-smooth and non star-shaped domains. The solution is obtained by minimizing the Rayleigh quotient on a suitable closed convex cone.

We classify connected, simply connected, noncompact three-dimensional trans-Sasakian $η$-Einstein manifolds. In [1], we showed that, in the compact case, such a manifold is either of $β$-Kenmotsu type or homothetic to a Sasakian manifold. In this paper, in the noncompact case, we find families of trans-Sasakian $η$-Einstein manifolds that are neither $β$-Kenmotsu nor homothetic to Sasakian manifolds. These families have infinitely many degrees of freedom. We give these nontrivial metrics explicitly. We also give a structure theorem for the case in which the characteristic vector field is Palais-nonregular.
Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five

Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.
On the maximum interval index of a graph
Martin Knor; Jelena Sedlar; Riste škrekovski

For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value. We also prove that, for every n >= 31, the maximum interval index among graphs without pendant vertices equals (n^3 - n)/6 - 2(n - 4) and it is attained by a dumbbell graph, obtained by joining two 4-cycles by a path.
Mean-Square Convergence Analysis of a Three-Level MGRIT Method for Linear Stochastic Evolution Equations with Additive Noise

We investigate the mean-square convergence of a three-level multigrid reduction-in-time (MGRIT) method based on F-relaxation for linear stochastic evolution equations driven by additive Gaussian noise. The method combines exponential Euler time stepping on the finest grid with implicit Euler discretizations on the two coarser grids. The inexact solution of the intermediate-level full approximation scheme problem gives rise to coupled error recursions involving two interlevel propagator discrepancies. Under a common spectral decomposition of the drift and noise covariance operators, we establish a geometric contraction estimate in a modal mean-square norm, with a contraction factor uniform in the temporal grids and both coarsening factors. We further derive fixed-iteration temporal error bounds that are uniform in the first coarsening factor and explicitly quantify the dependence on the second. For a fixed iteration count $k$ and a fixed second coarsening factor, we prove an $O(ΔT_1^r)$ error bound relative to the finest-grid reference solution for $0<r\le k+1$ provided that $\mathcal R_{r,B}<\infty$. We also prove that the error-propagation operator is nilpotent on each fixed temporal grid, ensuring finite termination of the iteration. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence behavior and compare temporal critical-path work under a unit-cost model.
Vanishing near the virtual cohomological dimension of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$

We prove the Church--Farb--Putman conjecture that \[ H^{N_n-i}(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z);\mathbb Q)=0, \qquad N_n=\binom n2,\quad n\ge2,\quad 0\le i<n-1. \] The proof relies on Franke's filtration of the weighted automorphic cochain complex, developed in his proof of Borel's conjecture. We treat trivial and nontrivial cuspidal support separately. For nontrivial support, we combine a degree calculation with the Chenevier--Lannes lower bound of $11$ for the motivic weight of level-one regular algebraic cuspidal representations of rank at least two. This reduces the contributing inducing data to a trivial factor and a Speh factor attached to such a representation. We construct primitives for closed lifts of cohomology classes in the filtration quotients by combining an Eisenstein residue identity with a cochain homotopy and finite distributions in the spectral parameters. A finite-filtration lifting argument then yields vanishing for nontrivial cuspidal support. The trivial-support case is treated using Franke's topological model.

Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_α(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $αd$ for any fixed $0<α<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $Ω(\sqrt{d\,C_α(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.
When to spend privacy: optimal allocation in private learning

Privacy accounting bounds the cumulative privacy cost of Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent but does not determine how to allocate a fixed budget across iterations. We formulate the complete Gaussian noise-variance schedule as an open-loop control under a composed zero-Concentrated Differential Privacy constraint, explicitly accounting for schedule selection. For expected quadratic terminal tracking, we prove that every local minimizer exhausts the certified budget, yielding an exact-budget simplex formulation. We introduce Privacy-Budget Adjoint Mirror Descent (PB-AMD), combining pathwise adjoint gradients with entropic updates that preserve positivity, charge floors, and the prescribed budget. Under regularity and coercivity assumptions, we establish existence and budget stability of optimal schedules, design-to-training utility stability, and deterministic, stochastic, and sample-average stationarity guarantees. A linear-quadratic reduction yields an explicit square-root allocation law. Experiments demonstrate tracking improvements over several allocation rules and predictive improvements over uniform allocation in a learning-rate restart setting, where learning-rate allocation performs similarly. Comparisons at a common stationarity tolerance show lower schedule-optimization times than projected gradient descent on the tested problems. The framework connects certified privacy accounting with optimization through nonlinear training dynamics.
On self-similar random quotients of the line

A surprisingly wide variety of important random fractal metric spaces in modern probability theory can be viewed as self-similar random quotients of the real line, including the continuum random tree, Liouville quantum gravity surfaces, the trace of Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and self-similar ($s=2d$) long-range percolation on $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that the metric and resistance growth dimensions are well-defined in a certain sense for every random metric space in a class containing all of the above examples. Our results are new for the trace of Brownian motion.
On the variational characterization of a laminated core model in ferromagnetic materials

Accurate prediction of iron losses in transformers, electric motors, and generators at elevated frequencies requires accounting for eddy currents in laminated magnetic cores during field simulation. We study local material models for these lamination losses that resolve the inhomogeneous magnetic-field distribution across the thickness of the respective steel sheets via one-dimensional diffusion equations. This allows to incorporate skin-effect and eddy-current losses in the laminations at each material point of a two- or three-dimensional magnetic-field simulation. The macroscopic material response is described implicitly through a minimization problem involving a set of internal variables which encode the load history and current state of the material. The variational structure of these problems allows us to prove well-posedness, to include anisotropy and hysteresis, and to develop efficient globally convergent solvers for the evaluation of the macroscopic material response. The proposed framework thus allows to efficiently and reliably predict magnetic behaviour of laminated core material over a wide frequency range and is well-suited for integration into nonlinear magnetic field solvers.
Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes

We develop a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are first derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, requiring only factor-wise crossing statistics. We then introduce the drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, in which each conditional derivative is Gaussian with possibly nonzero drift. For products of DGD factors, an exact Gaussian-mixture representation yields bounds that jointly capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. The lower bound reduces under stationarity to a known $\ell_2$ bound, whereas, to the best of the author's knowledge, the upper bound is new even in the stationary case. Furthermore, the bounds are asymptotically exact in drift-dominated regimes. The framework is specialized to nonstationary Double-Rayleigh fading and to quasi-identically distributed DGD factors, with closed forms for products of $α$-$μ$ envelopes. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.
Sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplacian with Morrey data

We obtain sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplace equation with a right-hand side belonging to a Morrey space. We derive local $C^{σ+λ-n}-$regularity of solutions when $σ+λ-n\neq1$, where $σ\in(0,2)$ is the order of the operator and $λ\in(n-σ,n)$ is the Morrey decay rate of the right-hand side. In the case $σ+λ-n=1$, we show that solutions are locally in the Zygmund class, and hence are Log-Lipschitz continuous. Explicit examples attest to the sharpness of the conditions.
Compatibility of Perverse Truncation of Ngô Fibrations
Bin Wang; Shihao Wang; Chenglong Yu

We study compatibility of perverse truncations for morphisms between Ngô fibrations with rationally smooth total spaces. We show that, under an effective rank inequality, equivariant pullbacks preserve the normalized perverse truncations. Applied to the diagonal, this gives multiplicativity of perverse truncations for Hitchin systems with rationally smooth total spaces.
Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
Haobo Ma; Wenlin Zhang; Charles E. Hughes

For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact. We prove an explicit repair for an infinite periodic degree-three family. Computer-assisted results establish first-mask descent through combined length seventeen over every alphabet, degree-three first-mask descent through length thirty, and a uniform repair of all degree-three failures through length thirty, including all further letter identifications. Counterexamples to arbitrary, first, and last minimum-mask choices explain the need for alternative masks. Finally, we prove that minimum iteration depths have no gaps for arbitrary languages. General block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap remain open.
Variational characterization of principal eigenvalues for a general class of linear weighted BVP's under mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type

The main goal of this paper is to characterize the existence of principal eigenvalues of $$ \left \{ \begin{array}{ll} -\mathrm{div}\left(A\nabla u\right) +qu=λm u \quad & \hbox{in} \;\; Ω,\\[1ex] \mathscr{B} u = 0 \quad & \hbox{on} \;\; \partial Ω, \end{array} \right. $$ where $m\in L^\infty(Ω)$ satisfies some of the conditions (A1)-(A3) below, as well as to deliver their variational characterizations whenever they exist. As we are dealing with general boundary operators of mixed non-classical type, in the general setting of this paper our results are far more general than all existing results. The case when $m$ satisfies (A2) has not been previously explored in the literature.
A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
Iryna Karpenko; Dmitry Shepelsky; Gerald Teschl

We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate a matrix Riemann--Hilbert problem whose solution provides a reconstruction formula for the solution of the original Cauchy problem.
A New Invariant for Doubly Periodic Solutions of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
Nicolas Hasse; Ross Ogilvie; Martin U. Schmidt

Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. These transcendental period conditions are studied through Whitham deformations, which deform the curve while preserving the periods. We extend Whitham deformations to all real hyperelliptic curves of this type, by holding fixed the plane spanned by the periods, or this plane together with its complex structure. Under mild nondegeneracy conditions the resulting isoperiodic sets are manifolds of dimensions three and one, respectively. Along the one-dimensional isoperiodic sets, a generalization of the Willmore energy is a local parameter away from its critical points, to which the spectral curves of tori belong. Finally, using homology bases adapted to the branch points, we find discrete invariants of the isoperiodic sets of doubly periodic curves: a triple of integers and a refined conformal type.
Iterative Methods for Solving New Generalized Absolute Value Equations

In this paper, we propose two iterative methods, the modified Picard method (MPM) and the generalized Traub method (GTM), to solve a new generalized absolute value equation (NGAVE). We establish their convergence under appropriate assumptions. Additionally, numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the developed algorithms.
On record behaviours of returns for interval maps

Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $μ$, a $μ$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.
Lie point symmetry analysis of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model with exponential claim sizes
Aminu Ma'aruf Nass; Kassimu Mpungu; Rahmatullah Ibrahim Nuruddeen; Yaqoob Al Rahbi

We carry out a Lie point symmetry analysis of the coupled integro-differential system satisfied by the conditional Gerber--Shiu functions of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model. In the model, claim sizes are exponential, the intensity of the next claim arrival depends on whether the current claim exceeds a random threshold, and both the volatility and the premium rate may depend on the surplus. We write the system as the restriction to the half-line of a far-field operator with prescribed exterior data, derive the complete set of determining equations, including the condition imposed by the nonlocal convolution term, and solve them. The resulting group classification holds for every surplus-dependent volatility and premium of the form considered and for every absolutely continuous or constant threshold distribution. A non-trivial symmetry beyond scaling and superposition exists if and only if the volatility and the premium rate are constant, and it is then exactly the translation in the surplus variable. We construct the optimal system of one-dimensional subalgebras. We show that the invariant solutions of the combined translation--scaling generators exist precisely when a $2\times2$ generalized Lundberg determinant vanishes, and we give this determinant for an arbitrary threshold distribution, with explicit forms for the constant and exponential thresholds. We prove existence and sign properties of the adjustment coefficient, derive its sensitivities to all model parameters, and establish Cramér--Lundberg-type asymptotics for the Gerber--Shiu functions, including the limit of the ratio between the two regimes. A numerical study shows that claim-size-driven dependence lowers the adjustment coefficient markedly below that of an independent model with the same mean claim intensity.
Least common multiples of polynomial values: averaging, ray classes, and Galois statistics

We study analogues over number fields and the probabilistic congruence input that enters averaged versions of this problem. We prove an asymptotic formula for the least common multiple of ideals in a fixed ray class, record local equidistribution estimates for random $S_n$-polynomials, and give a conditional reduction of the averaged higher degree problem to explicit dispersion and large prime collision estimates. We also formulate an individual quadratic number field analogue and reduce it to a prime ideal quadratic root equidistribution statement together with a geometric pair counting estimate. The Galois group counting input is updated using Bhargava's theorem over $\mathbb Q$ and the determinant method estimates of https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35030 .
Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$

Let $p$ be a prime such that $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$. We prove that, for every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ and every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh for all such primes and, in particular, settles the case $L=\{1,4,6\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{19}$ singled out on his problem list. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines a geometric construction in characteristic two with an incidence matrix factorization over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The same construction yields integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $Ω_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.

The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.
Split Quaternion Toolbox: A MATLAB Implementation
Salman Ahmadi-Asl; Abbas Moradi; Yang Zhang

This paper presents a MATLAB toolbox for working with split quaternions and split quaternion matrices. Split quaternions, also known as coquaternions, form a four-dimensional associative non-commutative algebra over the real numbers with a signature (+,+,-,-). The toolbox provides two main classes: SplitQuaternion for scalar-valued split quaternions and SplitQuaternionMatrix for matrix-valued split quaternions. The implementation includes arithmetic operations, algebraic functions, matrix operations, linear algebra utilities, and various conversion methods. The toolbox is designed to be intuitive for users familiar with MATLAB's standard matrix operations while providing the full power of split quaternion algebra. This paper details the implementation, provides numerous examples, and demonstrates the toolbox's capabilities through practical demonstrations. The MATLAB toolbox is accessible at https://github.com/SalmanAhmadi-Asl/Split_Quaternion.git.
Interacting particles in random irregular media
Luca Bondi; Elena Issoglio; Francesco Russo

In this paper, we first develop novel tools of independent interest in the field of stochastic calculus related to SDEs with distributional drift, namely the formulation of a quasi-Stroock-Varadhan martingale problem in the sense that the test functions are of class $C^{1,2}$ instead of solutions of Kolmogorov type PDE. This has several applications, among which, the time restriction and the notion of conditional rough martingale problem and related solution.
Efficient Low-Rank Approximation of Quaternion Matrices via Adaptive Cross Approximation

The adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm is a powerful tool for constructing low-rank matrix approximations using only a small subset of matrix entries. While extensively studied for real and complex matrices, its extension to quaternion algebras, remains largely unexplored. This paper presents the first comprehensive framework for adaptive cross approximation operating natively in the quaternion algebra H. Unlike approaches that rely on real embeddings or complexifications, our method preserves the algebraic structure of quaternions throughout the computation, avoiding information loss and maintaining the natural correlations between quaternion components. We develop a fully quaternionic ACA algorithm with rigorous theoretical foundations, including convergence analysis, error bounds, and complexity estimates. The algorithm achieves O(r(m+n)) complexity per iteration and demonstrates quasioptimal approximation properties comparable to the quaternion singular value decomposition (QSVD), but with significantly reduced computational cost. We provide a detailed MATLAB with numerical experiments on color image compression. Our results show that native quaternion ACA outperforms significantly the basic SVD algorithm in terms of computational efficiency, with very close approximation accuracy.

We provide a sharp estimate for the asymptotic number of lattice zonotopes inscribed in [0, n] d as n tends to infinity. Our estimate refines the logarithmic equivalent established by B{á}r{á}ny, Bureaux, and Lund when the sum of the generators of the zonotope is prescribed. As we shall see, the exponential part of our estimate is a polynomial of degree d in n 1/(d+1) , plus a term involving the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Our analysis is based on a correspondence between power sums over primitive vectors (vectors with coprime coordinates) and Eulerian polynomials. We also analyse some combinatorial properties of lattice zonotopes. In particular, we compute the asymptotic mean and variance of the diameter of the graph of a random lattice zonotope inscribed in [0, n] d as n goes to infinity, and show that this diameter satisfies a central limit theorem.
Data-driven Random-feature Approximation of Koopman Generators of Nonlinear Continuous-time Systems
Ana Čukarska; Maximilian Gollwitzer; Viola Muning Li; Vladyslav Fediukov; Zahra Monfared; Felix Dietrich

Learning continuous-time dynamical systems from data is an active area of research. The Koopman formalism is often used here, because it is a flexible approach that is informative about the system's fundamental properties. The formalism represents dynamical systems through linear operators acting on a suitable function space. A practical difficulty arising in the numerical approximation of Koopman operators is the choice of a ``dictionary'', meaning an effective finite-dimensional representation of the function space. In this paper, we focus on learning dynamical systems in continuous-time, and so we consider numerical approximations of the Koopman generator instead of the Koopman operator. Our main contribution is a data-driven random-feature method to obtain a parsimonious and effective function representation for Galerkin approximation methods such as gEDMD. The representation we construct is data-informed, which allows us to improve upon data-agnostic methods. We empirically demonstrate the suitability of our method for forecasting tasks and system analysis. The numerical experiments show that our approach is accurate, and faster than iterative optimization. Further, we prove convergence of our approximation of the vector field and the resulting trajectories. In addition to the numerical results, we also make theoretical contributions, including a general convergence criterion for the semigroup generated by the gEDMD approximation and a counterexample showing that gEDMD does not generally preserve exponential boundedness. With our contribution, we advance the frontier of efficiently learning continuous-time dynamics from data, towards interpretable and mathematically robust modelling based on the Koopman framework.
Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales

For one-dimensional strict local martingales of the form $\mathrm{d} X_t=σ(X_t) \mathrm{d} W_t$ starting from $X_{0}=x_{0}>0$, we prove the strong rate $\mathbb{E}\left[|X^h_N-X_T|\right] \lesssim h^{\min\{θα,\frac{1}{2}\}}$ for a discrete scheme~$X^h$ truncated at a level $h^{-α}$, with time step~$h$, as $h\downarrow 0$, where~$θ$ depends on the truncation property. For the CEV model $σ(x)\equiv x^{1+γ}$ in particular, the rate is~$\frac{1}{2}$ for any $γ\in (0,1)$ (up to a logarithmic pre-factor at $γ=\frac{1}{2}$).
Randomized Symplectic Model Reduction: One-Pass Basis Construction and Sketched Hamiltonian Assembly
Robin Herkert; Bernard Haasdonk; Jörg Fehr

Symplectic model order reduction of Hamiltonian systems yields reduced dynamics that conserve the reduced Hamiltonian along exact trajectories, avoiding the artificial energy drift that can arise from conventional projection methods.
