The local theory relies on spatial localization near the origin and therefore does not capture the global geometry of the real zero set of the Hessian. For globally defined operators, unbounded real zero curves of the Hessian can make the global decay strictly slower than the local decay or destroy \(L^2\)-boundedness altogether. We establish a global analogue of the Phong--Stein theory for quasi-homogeneous polynomial phases. We introduce a family of Newton polygons adapted to the regions near and away from the real zero curves of the Hessian, together with the corresponding box-area scales. The relative geometry of these Newton polygons and area scales characterizes global \(L^2\)-boundedness and determines the sharp \(L^2\)-estimates in the high- and low-frequency regimes. As an application, we determine the exact range of anisotropic homogeneous \(L^2\)-Sobolev estimates for the associated global Radon transform.
Compact generation and perfect objects in homotopy categories of exact model structures

Compact generation allows large triangulated categories to be studied through suitably small objects. For homotopy categories arising from exact model structures, a natural question is how this intrinsic notion of smallness relates to finite presentation in the underlying exact category. In this paper, we investigate this relation for hereditary projective model structures generated by finitely presented Gorenstein projective objects. We establish compact generation and study the stronger requirement that every compact object admits a finitely presented cofibrant representative. We call objects with such representatives perfect. Under local coherence and the existence of enough projectives among the finitely presented objects, the finitely presented cofibrant objects form a Frobenius category whose stable category describes the perfect objects and whose idempotent completion recovers all compact objects. The relative $Q$-shaped setting, for suitable small categories $Q$, makes explicit how these finiteness properties depend on the choice of exact structure. The pure exact structure yields a compactly generated homotopy category, called the $Q$-shaped pure derived category. On the other hand, the split exact structure yields the $Q$-shaped homotopy category, which is compactly generated only in the pure semisimple case, analogously to the classical homotopy category of complexes. Finally, for acyclic $Q$ and for left artinian rings, we show that every compact object admits a strictly perfect representative. In particular, we establish that compact and perfect objects coincide, proving the conjecture of Holm and Jorgensen under these hypotheses.
Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions

How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? Over complex parameters, the admissible equations of a finite loopless multigraph form an algebraic family whose generic degree we determine: it is a graph state sum over edge sets without vertices of degree one, each vertex of positive degree contributing one less than its degree. We give two geometric realizations of this state sum. The first is the total Betti number of a universal edge-incidence ring constructed without parameters. Its full graded Betti table is the state sum, its Tor algebra is natural for noncontracting graph maps, the alternating numerator recovers the graph polynomial of Watanabe and Fukumizu, and an Artin reduction by a regular sequence realizes the one-variable specialization, corrected for tree components. The second lies in the actual family: at the strong-field boundary each state factor is a ramification index, and at sufficiently strong field the state charts exhaust the admissible complex fiber. For fixed nonzero real couplings, every Eulerian message-sign sector contains a real fixed point at every external field, and strong fields attain this lower bound: one admissible real fixed point per element of the binary cycle space and one positive fixed point. For graphs of maximum degree at most three, this minimum equals the number of minimal module generators of the edge-incidence ring. One state decomposition connects the complex degree, graded syzygies, and an attained minimum real count. The degree, selected ring and resolution statements, and the real counts are formalized in Lean 4.
Characterization of Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
Satyajyoti Achar; Md Hasan Ali Biswas; Ramesh Manna

The aim of this paper is to obtain the characterization of Fourier transform for functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $H$, defined on the groups $G=\R^n,\,G=\Z/n\Z$. In the first part of the paper, we consider the Fourier transform as a bijective mapping on $S_H$, the space of all $H$-valued smooth rapidly decaying functions on $\R^n$, which naturally extends bijectively to the dual space $S_H'$. Within this framework, we characterize the Fourier transform in terms of the convolution theorem, supplemented by additional structural properties of the Fourier transform. In the second part of the paper, we consider the discrete setting, where the Fourier transform is an operator on $L^1(\Z/n\Z, H)$, and we provide corresponding characterization based on its essential properties. In contrast to the classical setting, a key assumption in our framework involves the interplay between two distinct convolution operations. As a consequence, the structure of our proof diverges notably from the classical case and introduces additional complexities.
Multilevel Monte Carlo methods for random nonlinear eigenvalue problems

We develop a multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) estimator to compute statistical quantities of interest of solutions to parameter-dependent nonlinear eigenvalue problems. The main difficulty for this problem is that parametrized eigenpairs often lack a globally well-defined parameter-to-solution map due to crossings and bifurcations. These phenomena render eigenvalue-tracking infeasible in multi-dimensional parameter domains. To overcome this issue, we propose both an Eulerian and a Lagrangian perspective on parameter-to-solution maps for nonlinear eigenvalue problems, which remain well-defined even in the presence of local crossings and bifurcations. Their implementation is based on a straightforward modification of Beyn's contour integral approach. Building on these maps, we propose an MLMC estimator that does not rely on matching eigenvalues or eigenvectors across samples or discretization levels. Nested approximation spaces and inter-level prolongation are only required when statistical quantities of interest related to the eigenspaces are of interest, but not for quantities of interest related to the eigenvalues. We demonstrate the feasibility and validity of our approach by numerical examples using a quasi-Monte Carlo method, including a nonlinear formulation of the Laplace Dirichlet eigenvalue problem on random domains in three dimensions motivated by the work of Steinbach and Unger. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work considering the approximation of statistical quantities of interest for random nonlinear eigenvalue problems.
A characterization of equality between de Branges--Rovnyak and Dirichlet spaces
Carlo Bellavita; Eugenio Dellepiane; Shuaibing Luo

We characterize when a de Branges--Rovnyak space coincides with a harmonically weighted Dirichlet space. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for this identification, which settles a long-standing open problem. We illustrate the result with several examples, that include measures supported on uncountable sets.
Homotopy operations on higher Lie algebras

We determine the multiplicative structures of the homotopy operations on derived Lie algebras, derived restricted Lie algebras and partition Lie algebras, as well as the relation between these. Under Koszul duality, this follows from a calculation of the homotopy operations on derived rings, p-truncated algebras and divided power algebras over $\mathbb{F}_p$.
Highest weight vectors in queer Howe duality
Minghao Bi; Hongjia Chen; Longhui Wang; Yongjie Wang

We use Gauss decomposition to study the singular vectors in the regular representation on the coordinate superalgebra of the big cell of the queer supergroup. This gives explicit bases for the highest weight spaces in queer Howe duality. As an application, the same method recovers the explicit highest weight vectors in the general linear case obtained by Cheng and Wang.
Acceleration of the Method of Alternating Projections on subspaces by GMRES
Luis Manuel Hernández-Ramos; Maryam Calles-Cabriles; Gorka Emaldi-Porco

In this paper we propose a GMRES-accelerated version of the Method of Alternating Projections (MAP) for subspaces. It is proved that the accelerated version not only converges to a feasible solution, but also solves a best approximation problem. Comparisons are made with other accelerations proposed in the literature, for solving saddle point problems.
Emergence of large densities in a chemotaxis system with signal-dependent motility

In this paper, we focus on the emergence of large densities of a cell population in finite time in the following parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system with signal-dependent motility and a source term of logistic type \begin{equation} \begin{cases} u_{\varepsilon t} = Δ(e^{-v_\varepsilon}u_\varepsilon) + \varepsilon(κu_\varepsilon - μu_\varepsilon^2) ,\\ 0 =Δv_{\varepsilon}-v_\varepsilon+ u_{\varepsilon}. \end{cases} \end{equation} in a smooth bounded domain $Ω\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ with homogenuous Neumann boundary conditions and parameters $κ,μ>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. We will show that the solution $u_\varepsilon$ can exceed any certain value $M>0$ before a time $T(M)>0$ under the condition that $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small. To prove the result, we show convergence of classical solutions of the first system to classical solutions of the corresponding limit system as $\varepsilon\searrow 0$ \begin{equation} \begin{cases} u_t=Δ(e^{-v}u),\\ -Δv+v=u. \end{cases} \end{equation} The main challenge is to find suitable bounds for $u_\varepsilon$ and $v_\varepsilon$, that are $\varepsilon$-independent, in Lebesgue and Hölder spaces, whereas for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ global existence and boundedness is known.
From Walks to Skeletons: A Reusable Transport Architecture for Interactive Monte Carlo PDE Solvers
Yunfeng Liao; Yucheng Wu; Xiucheng Li

Walk-on-Spheres (WoS) enables mesh-free solutions of elliptic PDEs, but conventional methods repeatedly discard sampled trajectories, limiting their efficiency in interactive applications. We introduce reusable transport skeletons, a persistent representation that organizes stochastic walks into a shared computational graph. Our framework enables efficient reuse across spatial queries and boundary conditions, while supporting progressive refinement, structure-preserving compression, and local adaptation to dynamic geometry. It further enables interactive editing of transport between selected regions. Experiments demonstrate substantial computational savings while preserving solution accuracy. By transforming transient stochastic trajectories into reusable transport structures, our method provides a flexible foundation for interactive Monte Carlo PDE solving.
Near-quadratic sum-product estimates in fixed number fields
Kaiqiang Zhang; Yuanguo Zeng; Yuyu Wang

Let $K$ be a fixed number field. We prove a quantitative expansion theorem for mixed sumsets $A+B$, assuming only that $A$ is covered by relatively few cosets of a multiplicative group of small finite valuation rank. The constants are independent of the generators, their heights, and their prime ideal supports. As a consequence, if $A\subset K^\times$, $|A|=N\ge 3$, and each element has nonzero valuation at at most $k$ finite places, then every $B\subset K$ with $|B|=N$ satisfies $$ \max\{|A+B|,|AA|\} \ge N^2\exp\left[-C_K\left((k+1)\log(\log N+2)+\sqrt{(k+1)\log N}\right)\right]. $$ This is $N^{2-o(1)}$ for $k=o(\log N/\log\log N)$. We also obtain a trade-off between the additive and multiplicative deficits, estimates for iterated linear sumsets, and a transfer theorem for product constructions $A=PG$ in terms of the multiplicative deficit of $P$. The proof recovers local scales from an exact sum and bounds the remaining conditional entropy by the overlap of entropy measures on fixed trees.
A class of degenerate elliptic problems involving the Grushin operator: critical mass and ground states
Aleks Jevnikar; Senli Liu; Yu Su

We study the following degenerate elliptic equation with combined nonlinearities and prescribed mass \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \begin{cases} -Δ_γu+ωu+|u|^{p-2}u=|u|^{q-2}u \ \ \mbox{in }\mathbb{R}^{N}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N}} |u|^{2} \mathrm{d}z=c, \end{cases} \end{aligned} \end{equation*} where $Δ_γ$ is the Grushin operator and $ω\in\mathbb{R}$ appears as an unknown Lagrange multiplier. We characterize the critical mass threshold and the energy ground state solutions. Firstly, we prove the existence of optimizers for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality involving the Grushin operator together with estimates for the related best constant. Secondly, we characterize the critical mass by the best constant of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality and prove the existence of $x$-radial energy ground state solutions. Finally, we describe the relation between the $x$-radial action and energy ground state solutions, and the optimizers of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. The strategy developed here is based on the interplay between the mass-preserving scaling and a sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. It therefore suggests possible extensions to other prescribed-mass problems with competing homogeneous terms and threshold-mass phenomena.
Dynamic Properties of Numerical Solution for Stochastic Epidemic Models with a Fully Implicit Form
Zeyao Jin; Zhiming Li; Shenglong Chen

This paper establishes a fully implicit model to investigate the spread of epidemics and studies its dynamic properties, extending the semi-implicit model in Yang et al.(Commun. Nonlinear Sci. Numer. Simul., 152 (2026) 109140 ). We first employ the split-step backward Euler method to address the non-adaptability arising from backward Euler discretization and ensure the global convergence of the numerical solution. By linearizing the model, the computational cost is reduced at the expense of a slight increase in error, effectively avoiding complex iterative solution processes. Then, we derive the existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness of the numerical solution, and obtain its global convergence order. On this basis, the extinction and persistence of the disease are investigated under three different scenarios. The results indicate that environmental noise is a key factor leading to disease extinction. Finally, numerical simulations visually verify the obtained theoretical conclusions.
Exploring Neural Dynamics with Time Delays: A Numerical and Bifurcation Analysis Approach
Martin R Nelson; Jonathan J Crofts

The Wilson-Cowan model is a classic example of a ``neural mass model'' - a simplified yet powerful way to describe the activity of large networks of neurons. It is particularly interesting because, even in its relatively simple form, it can produce a surprising variety of behaviours, from steady rhythms to complex oscillations. A key factor influencing these dynamics is the presence of time delays, reflecting the time it takes for signals to travel between neurons. This article offers an accessible introduction to the Wilson-Cowan model, focusing on how these time delays affect its behaviour. We explore the core concepts behind the model, survey the existing literature, and introduce some numerical techniques specifically designed for analysing such delay differential equations. We also provide a practical, hands-on tutorial on using the DDE-BIFTOOL software package, demonstrating its application to the Wilson-Cowan model. Downloadable code allows the reader to reproduce our results and to explore the model's dynamics further, including MATLAB code for all computations, using DDE-BIFTOOL for the continuation, and Python versions of simulation codes.
On the Minimum Speed for a Fire Blocking Problem

We consider a dynamic blocking problem: a fire, starting on a bounded open set $R_0\subset\mathbb R^2$, propagates in the plane with unit speed in all directions. To block it, a barrier can be constructed in real time, at speed $λ>0$. A long standing conjecture by the first author states that the fire can be entirely surrounded by the barrier, in finite time, if and only if $λ>2$. The present paper improves on earlier lower bounds. Namely, if $λ\leq Λ=1.62621170228\ldots $ we show that the fire cannot be blocked. We also prove that, if $λ\leq 2$, the fire cannot be blocked by constructing a barrier which is a simple closed curve. More precisely, if the barrier does not contain purely delaying arcs, i.e.~arcs which are eventually surrounded by the fire on both sides, then for $λ<2$ the region burned by the fire at time $t>0$ has area $A(t)>(2-λ)t^2/4$.
The sharp exponent for the Banach--Mazur distance to the cube

Let $R_\infty(n)$ be the maximal Banach--Mazur distance from an $n$-dimensional real normed space to $\ell_\infty^n$. We prove that $R_\infty(n)\ge cn^{2/3}(\log(2n))^{-10}$. Together with the upper bound of Friedland, Naor, and Youssef, this gives $R_\infty(n) = n^{2/3+o(1)}$. The examples are polars of symmetric Gaussian polytopes with $2n$ generators, and the lower bound holds with exponentially high probability. A joint minimization over coefficient representations and positive weights yields an exact second-variation identity and sparse coefficients. A Gaussian projection argument controls all low-rank completions of the recorded matrix. An adaptive choice of exceptional generators then reduces the remaining case to a fixed-shift Gaussian small-ball estimate over two finite nets.
Topology of rational equivalence closures and Lawson homology

Rational equivalence need not be closed in the Chow topology, and its closure can have infinitely generated homotopy groups. For a connected reduced complex projective variety, we prove that this closure is locally contractible and that its quotient in the algebraically trivial cycles is a finite or countable weak product of circles. The quotient map admits a global continuous section. Consequently, the higher homotopy of the cycle space is carried by the closure and is canonically identified with Lawson homology. We describe the remaining fundamental group quotient and its integral Walker comparison. Applications include smooth projective examples with infinite rank closure homotopy throughout prescribed finite intervals and a family of abelian threefolds with four simultaneously dense, nonconstructible quotient rank strata.
A characterization of equality in the edge-localized Bollobás-Nikiforov inequality

Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge2$. Let $e(G)$ and $ω(G)$ denote its number of edges and clique number, respectively. Let $λ_1(G)\ge\cdots\geλ_n(G)$ be its adjacency eigenvalues. In 2007, Bollobás and Nikiforov conjectured that every graph $G\neq K_n$ satisfies $λ_1^2(G)+λ_2^2(G)\le2\left(1-\frac1{ω(G)}\right)e(G).$ This conjecture was recently completely resolved by Coutinho, Liu, Spier, Tang and Zhang. For every edge $e\in E(G)$, let $c_G(e)$ denote the maximum order of a clique containing $e$. Kannan, Kumar and Pragada proposed the edge-localized conjecture $λ_1^2(G)+λ_2^2(G)\le2\sum_{e\in E(G)}\left(1-\frac1{c_G(e)}\right)$ for every graph $G\neq K_n$. This conjecture was subsequently proved by Shaik. In this paper, we provide complete structural characterizations of the equality cases in both the Bollobás-Nikiforov inequality and its edge-localized version.
On finite covers of projective spaces, generic outside of codimension three

In the article, we generalize to an arbitrary dimension results obtained by the author and S.Yu. Nemirovski that related to Chisini's conjecture claimed that if $B$ is the discriminant of two generic covers $f_i:X_i\to \mathbb P^2$, $i=1,2$, and $\max (°f_1,°f_2) \geq 5$, then $f_1$ and $f_2$ are equivalent covers.
Digital Twin-Guided Wireless Localization via Probabilistic Inverse Learning
Mahmoud Saad Abouamer; Henrik C. M. Frederiksen; Robin J. Williams; Shashi Raj Pandey; Petar Popovski

This work investigates how site-specific digital twins (DTs) can support wireless localization using simplified distributed infrastructure. We propose PRISM (Probabilistic Refinement using Inverse learning and a Site-specific Model), a DT-guided probabilistic localization scheme with single-antenna access points (APs). Localization is formulated as a probabilistic inverse problem in which a conditional proposal distribution over UE locations is learned from multi-node channel impulse responses (CIRs). The proposal generates candidate locations, with its spread regularized during training and DT consistency used to reweight candidates and refine the estimate at inference. The DT serves as an approximate forward-consistency model, avoiding assumptions of exact channel fidelity or differentiability with respect to user position. Numerical experiments demonstrate gains over data-driven and classical fingerprinting benchmarks, while achieving a median error of approximately $0.7$ m using 10 single-antenna APs. Without retraining, PRISM remains effective under degraded inference-time DT features. PRISM also yields uncertainty estimates from its proposal covariance, with empirical $χ^2$ calibration approaching ideal behavior as APs increase.
The Kothe Radical in Novikov Algebras

We study the Kothe radical (the upper nil radical) in the variety of Novikov algebras. We prove that the class of weakly right nilpotent Novikov algebras coincides with the class of r-nil algebras and forms a radical class. We establish that the Kothe radical is a hereditary radical in the variety of Novikov algebras. Furthermore, we obtain a structural description of the Kothe radical as the intersection of ideals whose corresponding quotient algebras are prime K-semisimple algebras. Finally, we construct an example of a prime r-nil Novikov algebra over a field of characteristic p>0, which implies that the Baer radical is strictly contained in the Kothe radical in this case.
Jørgen Bang-Jensen; Xiaoying Chen; Panpan Cheng; Jin Yan

We study a new variant of the classical linkage problem for digraphs, which we call {\bf unilateral linkages.} A digraph $D$ is {\bf unilaterally $\bm{k}$-linked} if it satisfies that for every choice of $2k$ distinct vertices $s_1,s_2,\ldots{},s_k,t_1,t_2,\ldots{},t_k$ there are vertex disjoint directed paths $P_1,\ldots{},P_k$ in $D$ such that $P_i$ is either an $(s_i,t_i)$-path or a $(t_i,s_i)$-path for each $i\in [k]$. This is a relaxation of the property of $D$ being $k$-linked, where we insist that each $P_i$ must go from $s_i$ to $t_i$. Clearly every $k$-linked digraph is also unilaterally $k$-linked. It is easy to see that the unilateral linkage problem is NP-complete for general digraphs and that it is trivial for semicomplete digraphs (digraphs with no pair of non-adjacent vertices). We show how Thomassen's construction of highly connected digraphs which are not 2-linked can be modified to show that there is no connectivity which guarantees that a digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. We show that every 4-strong split digraph and every 5-strong semicomplete multipartite digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. Both bounds are best possible. A digraph is {\bf co-bipartite} if its vertex set can be covered by two induced semicomplete digraphs. We prove that every 6-strong co-bipartite digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. Here we do not know whether the correct answer is 5. We also prove that every 16-strong digraph with independence number at most 2 is unilaterally 2-linked.
Geometric structures, orbit closures and invariant measures in moduli spaces

Building on the seminal work of Eskin, Mirzakhani and Mohammadi in the context of dynamics on moduli spaces, we introduce linear loci and linear measures to provide a relatively basic description of orbit closures and invariant measures in strata of translation surfaces. We use this to discuss geometrical properties of orbit closures and invariant measures from the perspective of geometric structures.
Large number of hyperbolic and periodic solutions of sine-Gordon equation with nontrivial time dependence

By using suitable ansatz which reduces the problem of obtaining exact solutions of the sine-Gordon equation with nontrivial time dependence to obtaining exact solutions of two first order symmetric $ϕ^4$-like coupled equations in $x$ and $t$, we obtain a large number of hyperbolic and periodic solutions of the sine-Gordon equation. Large values of Hardy's Function from the Selberg class

Let $Z_F(t):=F(1/2+it) H(1/2+it)^{-1/2}$ denote Hardy's function, where the function $F(s)$ belongs to the Selberg class with polynomial Euler product and satisfies the functional equation $F(s)=H(s)\overline{F}(1-\bar{s})$. RoRo stowage planning: a systematic study of mathematical formulations

The target classes are unit balls of weighted variation spaces that can enlarge classical spaces by incorporating domain geometry into constraints on output coefficients. We establish upper and lower bounds for arbitrary convex bodies and determine the optimal polynomial approximation exponents for all planar convex bodies and their products with polytopes, including cubes and circular cylinders. When all principal curvatures are positive, the result extends to every finite $q\ge2$. For these classes, the dependence of the optimal exponent on the domain is captured by a single geometric growth exponent associated with small boundary caps. For periodic coefficients, the period map is a compact perturbation of the no-jump map. We construct separate receiving and sending characteristic scans: under a two-tree condition based at one active component, a positive Floquet profile exists exactly when the full period map has strictly larger spectral radius than its no-jump part. The other jump rates may vanish. The scans provide an integral minorant and positive jump return; a separate coefficient inequality verifies the spectral gap. Autonomous nonzero velocities and union-graph connectivity yield a simple principal pair; one active component suffices for exponential mixing. We also prove local perturbation results. A minimising principle for interval covers of zigzag persistence modules

The fundamental theorem of persistent homology states that any zigzag persistence module decomposes into a direct sum of simple building blocks called interval modules. We consider an interval cover, a possibly redundant family of interval submodules spanning every vertex space of a finite zigzag persistence module. We give an elementary descent argument that replaces a redundant cover with a minimal one that is an interval decomposition. The numerical range of limits of real rational functions

Hence a manifold with nonzero rational Pontrjagin class cannot carry such a spray; in particular, it admits no Riemannian metric whose geodesic spray is locally spherically symmetric. This paper is concerned with the simultaneous recovery of the trajectory and intensity of an unknown moving point source in an inhomogeneous acoustic medium. We prove that the whole-boundary measurements over a finite time interval uniquely determine the moving source. Furthermore, under suitable propagation and rank assumptions, Lipschitz stability of determining both the trajectory and intensity is derived using waveforms measured at four fixed receivers outside the source region. A novel Volterra--Euler reconstruction scheme is developed for solving the inverse problem, and the error estimate is derived for the proposed scheme. In this paper, we study the spherical maximal operator $\mathcal{M}_{S^{d-1}(A)}$, which is associated with the sphere $S^{d-1}$ embedded in the horizontal plane of some nilpotent group $\mathbb{G}_A$. Here, $\mathbb{G}_A$ is the group identified with $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, and its group law is determined by the $d\times d$ real matrix $A$. Specifically, when $A$ is a skew-symmetric matrix $J$, which is the case of the Heisenberg group, it was known that the spherical maximal operator $\mathcal{M}_{S^{d-1}(J)}$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb{G}_J)$ for $p$ in the range $(\frac{d}{d-1},\infty]$. In this paper, we extend the results from the skew-symmetric matrix $J$ to a more general class of invertible matrices $A$. R. Prabha; B. Sandhiya; Paul Manuel

For a given connected graph $G(V,E)$, the geodesic transversal problem finds a set $S$ of vertices of $G$ with minimum cardinality such that every maximal geodesic of $G$ contains at least one vertex of $S$. The cardinality of such a smallest set $S$ is called the gt-number of $G$ and is denoted as $gt(G)$. In this paper, we introduce the \textit{Edge geodesic transversal problem} as the edge-based extension of the geodesic transversal problem. The problem of determining a set $S\subseteq E(G)$ with minimum number of elements such that every maximal geodesic $P$ in $G$ traverses at least one edge of $S$ is called the edge geodesic transversal problem, and the cardinality of such a set is called the edge geodesic transversal number or the $gt_e$-number of $G$, denoted as $gt_e(G)$. Further, we investigate the effect of an edge cut of a graph on the edge geodesic transversal problem and prove a novel result called the edge cut transversal theorem which is used in the computation of edge geodesic transversal number of hypercube, stacked prism and ladder graph.

This paper is concerned with the dissipative weak solutions to the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations. For any $γ\in \left[ {0,\frac{1}{5}} \right)$, we establish the existence of $γ$-Hölder continuous weak solutions that exhibit a strict energy dissipation in expectation. For any $γ> \frac{1}{3}$, we prove that the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations do not possess dissipative solutions satisfying the corresponding spatial $γ$-Hölder regularity. It is well known that the stochastic forcing inevitably gives rise to additional stochastic effects to the Reynolds stresses, which cannot be treated by the differential estimates in the classical convex integration scheme introduced by Buckmaster, De Lellis, Isett and Székelyhidi (Ann. Math., 182(1):127--172, 2015). To address this difficulty, we develop a novel material integration technique into the stochastic convex integration scheme, so that those stochastic Reynolds stresses are quantified.

The receiver selects one channel at each time, conveys the selection over noiseless feedback, and must learn the channel qualities while decoding, to avoid overusing suboptimal channels. Large deviations from a stable steady state for damped dispersive PDEs with vanishing random kicks

We study the behaviour of stationary measures for a class of dispersive PDEs damped by a linear zero-order term and perturbed by a small kick noise. Under some natural assumptions on the law of the noise, we prove that any family of stationary measures satisfies the large deviation principle in the vanishing noise limit. The result highlights the role of nonlinear smoothing and applies to the nonlinear Schrödinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations, and to a variety of random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.

These theorems determine statistical structures up to local statisticmorphism by comparing the curvature of an alpha-connection and the skewness tensor using radial geodesics and parallel displacement of that connection. Decompositions of birational toric morphism between threefolds

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a birational morphism between smooth projective threefolds, Kollár asked that if $f$ could be decomposed into smooth blow-downs and smooth flops. In this paper we show that the toric version is true.
Density and Defect Distribution of Reduced Ideals Missed by the Reduction Algorithm in Real Quadratic Fields

Laws of the iterated logarithm for the range of once-reinforced random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$

In this paper, we study once-reinforced random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$, and prove sharp Chung-type and Hartman-Wintner laws of the iterated logarithm for the range. Let $R_n$ denote the range at time $n$ and let $c>0$ be the reinforcement parameter. Then, almost surely, \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n}{\sqrt{n/\log\log n}}=\fracπ{\sqrt{2}}, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{cR_n}{\sqrt{2n\log\log n}}=1. \end{equation*} The proofs are based on the independent increment decomposition of the inverse range and sharp generating function estimates.
Pointwise decay of cumulants and scaling regimes of chaotic states

We consider nonequilibrium chaotic states of classical interacting particles in a family of scaling limits motivated by kinetic theory. The particle activity and the strength of the pair interaction are rescaled simultaneously, allowing for both dilute and non-dilute regimes. Using cluster expansion, we derive pointwise bounds for truncated correlation functions (cumulants) of arbitrary order. Rethinking Channel Estimation for Fluid Antenna Systems: A Physics-Informed Operator Learning

The proof combines an endpoint sign calculation for the resonance polynomial with an algebraic argument showing that the third root is distinct from the two explicit ones. Sensitivity of RMS Delay Spread Estimation to Power Delay Profile Thresholding in Time-Varying Channels at 33 GHz

This establishes a fundamental computational complexity barrier for set-theoretic control. As an immediate consequence, the exact computation of maximal control invariant subsets of H-polytopes is \textsc{coNP}-hard. These hardness results hold regardless of whether the input constraint set is given in H- or V-representation.

We construct a bounded closed convex set in $c_0(\mathbb{C})$ on which no nonzero continuous complex-linear functional attains its maximum modulus. Consequently, this answers in the negative the two longstanding questions raised by Deville, Godefroy and Zizler in \cite[p. 35]{DGZ}. The construction uses a small perturbation of the identity on $c_0(\mathbb{R})$.
On surfaces, that fill the space

The article is devoted to the construction of dimension-raising maps of cubes with the highest possible Holder exponent. In particular, a square-to-cube mapping with a Holder exponent of $2/3$ is constructed, which is a solution to the V.I.Arnold problem.

We characterize the Green's functions of all strictly positive real self-adjoint realizations of this operator. The kernels are in one-to-one correspondence with positive-semidefinite $2\times2$ endpoint covariance matrices. We call the associated centered Gaussian processes Brownian processes. Each is a standard Brownian bridge plus the affine interpolation of an independent Gaussian endpoint vector. Singular endpoint covariance matrices give hard endpoint constraints, such as the pinned start $X(0)=0$ of Brownian motion. This parametrization gives explicit operator domains and energy spaces. On every mesh it gives an exact sparse precision matrix, so the likelihood of $n$ observations can be evaluated in $O(n)$ operations. Nonnegative realizations with a null space are treated separately through orthogonally normalized pseudoinverses, which are proper Gaussian covariances.

Averaging observations at fixed grid points can introduce errors, and motion estimates alone do not determine how the physical field values change. In this work, we study whether learning to correct a simple numerical interpolation improves the reconstruction of intermediate scientific fields. We prove strict pairwise negative correlation under both the uniform forest measure and the uniform connected-subgraph measure on the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$ for all $m,n\geq2$. Under the connected-subgraph measure, any two distinct edges of a fixed copy of $K_{2,2}$ remain strictly negatively correlated after conditioning on the subgraph induced by the remaining vertices.

Open Data Analysis Tool for Science and Engineering (ODAT-SE) is an open-source Python framework for inverse problems that are solved by repeated forward simulations. The framework connects optimization and sampling algorithms to solvers through a common interface for parameter mapping, constraints, and objective evaluation, so that an existing simulation code can be used with any of the algorithms. Relative to the previously published 2DMAT, it provides two-level MPI parallelism, which distributes candidate evaluations over processes and each evaluation over a parallel solver, checkpoint and continuation facilities, random search, global optimizers from SciPy, tensor-train optimization, and a Bayesian workflow that estimates partition-function ratios, model evidence, effective noise levels, and marginal posterior distributions. We validate the Bayesian workflow against closed-form results for a linear regression, benchmark tensor-train optimization on continuous, binary, and mixed-integer problems, and verify the two-level parallelization by the same optimum for all process decompositions. Taking up the positron-diffraction example of the 2DMAT paper, the workflow identifies the correlated structural solutions and an effective noise scale close to the imposed perturbation, while exposing incomplete convergence of symmetry-related mode weights. Solver packages, templates, and a gallery of examples support the use of the framework as a general platform for inverse-problem analysis.
When do token systems stabilize? Compatibility constraints and community structure
Flore Sentenac; Mingwei Yang; Sophie H. Yu

Token systems support repeated service exchange without monetary transfers, but their viability depends on the stability of token balances. We study token systems with compatibility constraints among agents. A requester is randomly sampled in each period, and only a few randomly sampled agents are available to provide service. We establish a necessary and sufficient condition for stability and show that the minimum-token rule, which selects the available provider with the lowest token balance, achieves the optimal stability region. We then apply this stability criterion to a random token system generated from stochastic block models with uniformly sampled requesters. We tightly characterize the stability regime by identifying two obstructions to stability: insufficient service opportunities for a group of communities or for an individual agent.
The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends

An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.
Different approach to certain problems in univalent function theory

Using different approach we consider some problems for the class $\mathcal{S}_{ex}^{\star}$ defined by the condition $\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\prec e^{αz}$, $0<α\leq1.$ Our method is more simple than that used by Das and Sarkar in their work: \textit{Sharp coefficient estimates for the exponential starlike class $S^\star_{ex}$} (\cite{DS26}).
The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian Conjecture

Let $h\in\C[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ have constant nonzero Hessian determinant, let $h^{*}$ be its formal Legendre transform and $g=\vv{X,\grad h}-h$. The Nambu derivations of $\grad h$ satisfy $δ_i(g)=X_i$ and $δ^α(g)=(\partial^αh^{*})\circ\grad h$. Consequently, in the gradient case the differential Galois criterion of \cite{ACH19}, consisting of $n$ membership conditions, reduces to a single membership condition. Equivalently, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $g\in\C[\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh]$. Moreover, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $δ^α(g)=0$ for $|α|=(°h-1)^{n-1}+2$, and then the coefficients $δ^α(g)(x_0)/α!$ of $h^{*}$ at $\grad h(x_0)$ determine the inverse. If the Hessian determinant of $h$ is merely a nonzero polynomial, then $g$ is still a primitive element of $\C(X)$ over $\C(\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh)$. For the Nambu-tower criterion, doubling a Keller map yields no independent conditions. After an affine change of coordinates putting $\grad h$ in the normal form $X+H$, the formal Legendre transform is the sum of the formal Pascal difference series of $g$, and the termination of this series implies polynomial invertibility. In at most three variables the normal form of every gradient Keller map has strongly nilpotent Jacobian part and is therefore Pascal finite, by a theorem of de Bondt, and an explicit gradient automorphism in four variables has a normal form which is not Pascal finite. The five-variable counterexample of Meng and Yang shows that the properties used here do not imply the Hessian conjecture. The results do not settle the open cases $\JC_2$ and $\HC_4$.
Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure

This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.
Grassmannian Realizations of Classical Pseudo-Riemannian Symmetric Spaces

We establish a unified fixed-point Grassmannian framework for the classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces from Berger's classification. For a classical group $G=\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(V,b)$, we identify $G$ with the open graph-like locus inside an ordinary or maximal-isotropic Grassmannian $\overline{G}$. Natural involutions of $\overline{G}$ are constructed via classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations. We explicitly describe the full fixed loci of these involutions in terms of classical Grassmannians. The corresponding graph-like fixed loci (or their signature strata) are identified, respectively, with the moduli spaces of classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations; these moduli spaces coincide with classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces. In summary, the 54 classical series are organized into four families: 10 group-type models, 7 classical-form Grassmannians, 20 scalar-structure Grassmannians, and 17 subspace-configuration Grassmannians.
Robust Log-Contrast Regression for High-Dimensional Compositional Microbiome Data with Outliers
Xuke Hua; Yunhai Xiao; Xin Xin

It is well known that microbiome sequencing data are naturally compositional and often have a complex subcomposition structure, as well as a lot of noise and some outliers. These characteristics make classical log-contrast regression difficult to apply, because it is sensitive to extreme values and cannot fully meet the linear constraints of compositional predictors. To tackle these issues, in this paper, we propose a robust log-contrast regression framework that incorporates the Huber loss function along with a Lasso penalty, which not only boosts resistance to outliers but also facilitates sparse variable selection. It is important to note that the general linear constraints, which are explicitly imposed, serve to preserve the algebraic coherence of compositional and subcompositional covariates. Under some mild assumptions, we theoretically prove that the proposed method achieves non-asymptotic guarantees in finite samples, comparable to those of Huber loss estimators, ensuring robustness. To implement the method efficiently, we develop a symmetric Gauss--Seidel-based alternating direction method of multipliers based on its dual formulation with a convergence guarantee, and it is also easy to implement in the sense that each subproblem admits a closed-form solution. To evaluate the statistical performance of the proposed method, we conduct a series of numerical experiments using simulated data and gut microbiome data, which show that the proposed method achieves better estimation accuracy, competitive prediction performance, and more reliable outlier identification than the benchmark method RobRegCC.
Ancestor Lifting of Quasi-Cyclic Additive Codes and Certified Quantum Codes
Liangdong Lu; Ran Xu; Ruipan Yang; Qiang Fu

Additive codes over $\Ffour$ that are self-orthogonal under the trace inner product correspond to binary quantum stabilizer codes. We study 1-generator $(1,2)$-quasi-cyclic (QC) additive codes and their exact quantum distances. For composite lengths $n=\ell m$, an ancestor-lifting theorem transports dual words of the folded ancestor to the length-$n$ code. A two-layer decomposition for $\ell=2$ and a CRT splitting for odd $\ell$ yield dimension laws and explain equality, escape, and mixed-branch behavior in the certified examples. A palindromic criterion ensures symplectic self-orthogonality, while reversal pairing and a symplectic Gram rank formula describe broader construction families. Exact distances are established by information-set decoding screening, Brouwer--Zimmermann computation on the additive dual, and independent witness verification. We certify twenty-one record-breaking binary quantum codes across twenty entries of Grassl's code table, with twenty-eight certified members in total. Propagation improves thirty-four further entries, and explicit constructions are supplied for three table-tying GV entries marked Code Missing Construction. Six additional candidates are reported only with rigorous upper bounds and heuristic screening evidence. The results connect divisor-lattice structure in additive quasi-cyclic codes with reproducible certification of exact quantum distances.
Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator

Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

For conjugate shapes $λ$ and $λ'$, Stanley's duality relates the Jack symmetric functions $J_λ(x;α)$ and $J_{λ'}(x;1/α)$. Through Stanley's combinatorial formula, it is an identity between the sums of the weights of the semi-standard Young tableaux giving the same monomial. We introduce the Jack multiple zeta functions, which keep these weights separate, and prove that Stanley's duality lifts to them, including the case of skew shapes. Thus the duality holds before the weights are summed up, and in fact step by step along chains of partitions. Since the duality is an identity among formal symbols, the same duality holds when the multiple zeta functions are replaced by other functions, and replacing them with the monomial quasi-symmetric functions recovers Stanley's duality. Hence our duality is a refinement of Stanley's duality which contains it as a special case. In particular, we obtain a duality for the Schur multiple zeta functions and the classical relation between the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions. We next show that any expansion of a Jack symmetric function in terms of Schur functions can be lifted to Jack multiple zeta functions, yielding an analog of a formula conjectured by Stanley and proved by Koike. We also show that the Jack multiple zeta functions of one-row shape give a one-parameter family interpolating the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions, and we discuss their values at $\{2\}^r$ and at $\{2\}^a,3,\{2\}^b$.
The Exact Weight Spectrum of $\RM(m-7,m$): A Counterexample to the Carlet-Solé Conjecture

Boolean functions are widely used in cryptography and coding theory. A key challenge lies in finding the weight spectrum for all $n$-variable Boolean functions of degree at most $r$, also known as the Reed--Muller code $\RM(r,n)$. In 2023, Carlet and Solé determined the weight spectra of $\RM(n-c,n)$ for $c=3,4$, and conjectured the weight spectrum of $\RM(n-c, n$) for $n\ge2c$. The weight spectra of $\RM(n-5, n)$ and $\RM(n-6,n)$ were determined by Carlet in 2024 and by Lou and Wang in 2025, respectively, confirming the Carlet-Solé conjecture for the cases $c=5,6$. Very recently, Leuenberger et al. and Wei et al. investigated the weight spectrum of $\RM(7,14)$ independently, and there are eight potential weights which have not been determined. Up until now, the weight spectra of the Reed--Muller codes $RM(r,n)$ are still unknown for $r=3,...,n-7$. In this paper, we determine the exact weight spectrum of $\RM(m-7, m)$ for every $m\ge 14$. By combining affine geometry and Fourier analysis, we exclude the conjectured eight weights for $\RM(7,14)$. We then extend the exclusions to all higher dimensions using a geometric transfer. Consequently, we provide a counterexample to the Carlet-Solé conjecture.
An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem

Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $σ$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner. A pairing-valued approximate identity yields fullness and nondegeneracy.
Sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation in $H^{1/2}_\bullet$

We prove sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation on the real line $\R$ in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\). This regularity threshold for global well-posedness is optimal, as we show by constructing examples of ill-posedness in \(H^s_\bullet\) for any \(s<1/2\). Moreover, with the spectral assumption satisfied by a dense set of initial data in the energy space, we prove that solutions in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\) asymptotically decouple as an infinite superposition of solitons. Our results extend the known global well-posedness and finite soliton resolution for rational data in \(H^\infty_\bullet\) to sharp global well-posedness and soliton resolution for general data in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\). Different from rational solutions, general data can also involve an infinite discrete spectrum, which makes the reduction analysis framework on the finite rank no longer applicable. For sharp well-posedness, we present a new isometry criterion and stability results for resolvent transform in the explicit formula. For soliton resolution, we develop a spectral method for this equation based on direct resolvent analysis and a novel trace norm estimate that upgrades energy convergence to uniform convergence. Our argument also yields sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the generalized half-wave maps equation with targets in the complex Grassmannians, extending the classical sphere-valued case.
New upper bounds for average kissing numbers

A packing of balls in Euclidean space is a set of balls with non-overlapping interiors. For a finite packing of balls, its average contact number is the average number of balls tangent to a ball in this packing, that is, twice the total number of tangencies divided by the number of balls. The average kissing number of the space is defined as the supremum of average contact numbers over all finite ball packings. In this paper, we present a new semidefinite programming approach to average kissing numbers and improve upon known upper bounds in all dimensions \(3\) through \(30\). In particular, we provide the first improvements to the upper bounds in dimensions \(10\) through \(30\) obtained from kissing numbers. We also fully solve the average kissing number problem in dimensions \(8\) and \(24\) by showing that the average kissing numbers coincide with the kissing numbers, 240 and 196560, respectively. These values are limits of average contact numbers of finite subpackings from the \(E_8\) and Leech lattices.
Design of DoF-Robust MIMO via Generalized Pinching Antennas
Zhiguo Ding; Robert Schober; H. Vincent Poor

Spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) are fundamental to the performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. However, the use of conventional fixed-location antennas introduces disparities in the users' distances to a common base station, which makes the multi-user channel matrix more susceptible to rank deficiency and, consequently, a loss of spatial DoF. This paper shows that generalized pinching antennas can be used to design a new form of MIMO robust to the loss of spatial DoF. In particular, by deploying pinching antennas in close proximity to the users, the resulting multi-user channel Gram matrix can have a well-conditioned, almost diagonal structure, which reduces its sensitivity to the users' spatial deployment as well as the risk of rank deficiency. Two performance metrics, namely the rank-deficiency probability and the outage probability, are used to evaluate the performance of pinching-antenna-assisted MIMO transmission. The presented analytical and simulation results demonstrate the capability of pinching antennas to preserve spatial DoF and provide ubiquitous connectivity by effectively supporting users at spatially separated locations.
PDE-Based Bounds on Optimal Exponents in Active Simple Hypothesis Testing

We present general upper and lower bounds on the optimal error exponent for the Active Simple Hypothesis Testing (ASHT) problem. ASHT has been extensively studied across diverse fields including Information Theory, Bandits, and Operations Research, a precise characterization of this optimal exponent has remained elusive. This work combines a recent Partial Differential Equation (PDE) characterization of the optimal exponent by Vijayan (2025) with the comparison principle of viscosity solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi PDEs. This leads to bounds that are parametrized by convex functions, sets and lower Hamiltonian relaxations, a flexibility that generalizes many known results in the literature.
Eduardo Alves da Silva; Fernando Figueroa; José Ignacio Yáñez; Joaquín Moraga

We prove that most rational smooth Fano threefolds are compactifications of $\mathbb{G}_m^3$. More precisely, we study which smooth Fano threefolds are cluster type, i.e., for which smooth Fano threefolds $X$ one can find a boundary $B\in |-K_X|$ and an embedding $\mathbb{G}_m^3\hookrightarrow X\setminus B$. We prove that many important classes of smooth Fano threefolds are cluster type. For instance, a smooth Fano threefold which is the blow-up of either $\mathbb{P}^3$ or $\mathbb{Q}^3$ and is general in its deformation space is of cluster type. As a consequence, we show that among the $105$ families parametrizing all smooth Fano threefolds, the general element of precisely $87$ families is of cluster type. We prove that a general prime smooth Fano threefold of genus $7$ is not of cluster type. This is the only family whose general element is rational but not of cluster type. Finally, we prove that cluster type projective klt varieties are cylindrical and we give a criterion for such a cylinder to be anticanonically polar. Using this, we reduce the cylindricity problem for smooth Fano threefolds to the families $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.3$, $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.5$, and $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.6$.
On the Pontryagin Maximum Principle for Rough Stochastic Differential Equations
Peter K. Friz; Ulrich Horst; Stefanos Theodorakopoulos; Huilin Zhang

We establish first- and second-order Pontryagin (a.k.a. stochastic) maximum principles for rough stochastic control problems with general nonlinear $\mathrm{Lip}^γ$-rough vector fields. This complements the dynamic programming approach of Friz-Lê-Zhang [FLZ26b], and extends the maximum principle of Horst-Zhang [HZ26] beyond affine rough vector fields. The paper concludes with applications to pathwise stochastic optimal control.
An upper bound of 61 for the Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$

We improve the upper bound on the classical Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$ from 62 to 61. The proof is based on a global incidence count, classifications of small neighborhoods and exhaustive SAT computations. We formalize the mathematical reductions in Lean and refute every resulting formula with two SAT solvers.
Reflection equations and Littlewood identities for spin Hall-Littlewood and $q$-Whittaker functions

We describe two-parametric Littlewood identities for inhomogeneous stable spin Hall-Littlewood and inhomogeneous spin $q$-Whittaker symmetric functions. These identities generalize the Littlewood identity found by Warnaar (2006) for the ordinary Hall-Littlewood polynomials. However, instead of Rogers-Szegö coefficients used by Warnaar, coefficients in our identities are given by products of Al-Salam-Chihara polynomials. Our proof relies on integrable lattice models. A key step includes three new solutions to the reflection and boundary equations for the fully fused six-vertex model. To find these solutions we use isomorphisms between tensor products of evaluation $U_q(L\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-modules, as well as covectors stable under a $q$-Onsager coideal subalgebra.
Fluid Problems Posed on Closed Hypersurfaces: Circumventing the Saddle-Point Structure

For a $d$-dimensional closed hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, we reformulate the (stationary) tangent Stokes, transient tangent Stokes, and transient tangent Navier-Stokes equations by replacing the divergence equation with a pressure Poisson equation, thereby circumventing their saddle-point structure. The pressure Poisson equation hinges on a commutator identity between the divergence and the surface diffusion operator, whose lower-order term depends on the Ricci curvature, and requires no boundary conditions for the pressure. We show that the reformulated operator is the composition of a linear, block-triangular data map with the primal operator. Consequently, each reformulation is well-posed if and only if the primal problem is, and solving it with arbitrary data amounts to solving the primal problem with a modified divergence datum. For hypersurfaces of class $C^2$ and data of the pressure Poisson equation in $H^{-1}$, the tangent Stokes reformulations can be posed in $H^1$-based spaces, which paves the way for conforming discretizations that do not require a discrete inf-sup condition.
Young's lattice, invariant ideals, and weak identities

For a $d$-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field of characteristic zero, we show that $GL(V)$-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra of the free two-step nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_2(V)$ are in natural correspondence with filters in Young's lattice of integer partitions with at most $d$ rows. The same classification holds for $GL(V)$-stable Poisson ideals of $S(V\oplusΛ^2(V))$ with its natural Poisson bracket. As applications, we determine all weak polynomial identities of the $n$-th Weyl algebra relative to its standard generating subspace and of the universal enveloping algebra of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra relative to the Lie algebra itself.

We study the relationship between semisimplicity and non-degeneracy for finite-dimensional Hopf triplets over a field of characteristic zero. The non-degeneracy condition appears in the construction of \(4\)-manifold invariants from Hopf triplets, and it was not known whether non-semisimple examples satisfying this condition exist. We prove that a Hopf triplet is non-degenerate if and only if it is semisimple.
Time-Periodic Chemotaxis in Shifting Environments: Propagation and Planar Forced Waves in $\R^N$

We study time-periodic Keller--Segel dynamics in a translating KPP environment. In the parabolic--elliptic regime, we prove global boundedness, identify the sharp speed \(c_*=2\sqrt{\bar a\,\bar r}\), establish persistence in the interior region \(|s|<c_*\), \(s\cdot e<c\), and derive the complementary sharp upper bounds; for a moving favorable slab, the sign of a principal Floquet exponent determines persistence or extinction under the stated weighted-resolvent condition. For every fixed \(τ\ge0\), under constant population diffusivity and sufficiently weak taxis, we further construct locally unique planar forced time-periodic waves in \(\mathbb R^N\). The main new analytic mechanisms are an exact Yukawa first-contact estimate, which controls the chemotactic drift at the KPP leading-edge scale without losing the sharp propagation threshold, and a two-sided weighted Fredholm--monodromy continuation framework for the temporally nonlocal signal equation, with explicit control of the far-field spectral gaps and the translational neutral mode. To the best of the author's knowledge, planar forced time-periodic waves in \(\mathbb R^N\) for shifting Keller--Segel systems have not been investigated in any previous studies; earlier forced-wave results are confined to substantially more restrictive settings, in particular one-dimensional parabolic--elliptic models. Thus the present construction provides the first multidimensional planar forced-wave theory for a time-periodic shifting Keller--Segel system with temporal signal memory.
Diameter Bounds and Finiteness of Graphs from Local Intersection Data

We extend the Bakry--Émery curvature framework on graphs, broadening its applications and strengthening the resulting diameter bounds. We study diameter bounds and finiteness for amply regular graphs, distance-regular graphs, $(s,c,a,k)$-graphs, and locally strongly regular graphs. In particular, for an amply regular graph with parameters $(v,k,λ,μ)$, we prove that \[{\rm{diam}}(G)\le4+8\log\frac{k}{λ+2}\] when $μ>2$ and $k\ge3λ^2/μ$, improving the previous linear bound $4k/(λ+4)$ to a logarithmic bound. We also address several related conjectures. In their monograph \emph{Distance-Regular Graphs}, Brouwer, Cohen, and Neumaier conjectured that every amply regular graph with $μ>1$, except the icosahedron, satisfies ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le2k/(λ+2)$. We confirm this bound when $μ>λ+1$ and give counterexamples to the conjecture with $μ=λ$. For amply regular graphs with $μ\geλ$ and $μ>1$, we obtain ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le 2k/μ+1$. This proves the Qiao--Park--Koolen conjecture. In 1983, Terwilliger conjectured that every $(s,c,a,k)$-graph with $c>1$ is finite. We prove this conjecture when $s>2$, $c>2$, and $(s,c)\ne(4,3)$. Moreover, we prove Weetman's finiteness conjecture for locally strongly regular graphs when the local parameter $μ>1$, and disprove his stronger conjecture that every strongly regular graph is an $\mathscr{S}$-graph. We also prove that every graph whose local graphs all have rank 3 is finite, which in particular proves a conjecture of Soicher in 1992.
On extended interpolation properties of the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function

We describe extended interpolation properties of the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function over an imaginary quadratic field. We have three applications. Firstly, we give an elliptic analogue of the Coleman-Ihara formula. Secondly, we extend Kato's explicit reciprocity law for elliptic units and give a proof of the Tamagawa number conjecture for critical Hecke motives. Finally, we prove a large part of the $p$-adic Beilinson conjecture for the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function.

We formulate Poisson summation with periodic weights in forms adapted to arithmetic sums (arithmetic Poisson summation formulas, APSF), in scalar, polynomial-congruence and vector-divisibility versions, extending Berndt's arithmetic Poisson formula. We use APSF as a common framework to rederive Ramanujan's formula for $ζ(2m+1)$ and its character analogues due to Katayama and Berndt-Straub, the functional equations of $ζ$, of Dirichlet's beta function and of Estermann's function, and the exponents of Tolev and Chen-Wang for power-free values of $x^2+y^2+1$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2+k$. It also gives reciprocity laws with Kelvin-function kernels for Lambert series twisted by a Dirichlet character over imaginary quadratic fields of arbitrary class number; asymptotic formulas with error terms for $r$-free values of $x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2+k$, with Gaussian-weighted versions and the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series; an argument of Terras, relating two-dimensional Bessel series for all odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values; and a Gaussian representation of a Mersenne-Fermat prime detector.
Integral Forms of Twisted Quantum Affine Algebras and Quantum Frobenius

For twisted quantum affine algebras, we compare Lusztig's restricted integral form with the integral form generated by group-like toral elements and divided powers of real Drinfeld current modes. The two forms coincide over $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ outside type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$. In type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$, the smallest ordinary localization over which they coincide is $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][Φ_{4r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n=1$, and $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][Φ_{8r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n\geq2$, where $Φ_k(q)$ are cyclotomic polynomials. In particular, no localization obtained by inverting finitely many nonzero Laurent polynomials suffices in this family.
Axiomatic Learning and Probabilistic Structures with first applications to variants of Arithmetic Machine Learning and beyond

We introduce the Axiomatic Learning Structures (ALS) and Axiomatic Probabilistic Structure (APS) in order to study the interactions of Machine Learning, Optimization, with research frameworks- which, we take the view, can be characterized at the core by the corresponding axioms. The ALS explores the interplays between structures that one is interested in Learning Theory such as Loss functions and the axioms of the objects and transformations involved in these functions. The APS studies the interaction between structures of interest in Probability Theory such as Gibbs distributions, equations with noise, etc. and the axioms of the corresponding objects and transformations. We also introduce in Section 6 Transformations-Axiomatic Based Learning (TABLe) on Mathematical data-sets. One feature of this approach is the ranking of transformations from a table for a certain task based on scores which reflect which transformations work better than others, similarly to when human investigators try various methods on a task. We also study structure recovery from noisy data. In particular, to exemplify the ideas, we consider loss functions which contain derivations and derivations-like transformations. As a first application we study recovery in the context of polynomials with integer coefficients using standard derivatives along with other types of derivations which appear in Arithmetic: the p-derivations which satisfy \textit{different axioms} from the usual derivatives. As a first application of the APS we study a class of noisy (partial/mixed) derivations equations. In the last sections, to provide further potential applications of this framework, we give an overview of an initial simplified Opinion Dynamics model and its (simultaneous) study of rules of updates.
On the interpolation property of Kupferer's Lubin-Tate regulator maps

Generalizing both [LZ14] and [ScV26, SaV24] we prove the interpolation property at Artin characters of Kupferer's regulator map [Ku20] over a fixed local field $L$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for $p$ any prime. Since our methods cover the case $p=2,$ we in particular close a gap in the literature even for the (cyclotomic) 2-variable regulator map from [LZ14]. Moreover, we study big (dual) Bloch-Kato exponential maps for unramified towers and we use them to improve Colmez' reciprocity law in the Lubin-Tate setting from [SaV24]. Finally, we compare Kupferer's regulator map with the 2-variable regulator map of Loeffler-Zerbes when $L=\mathbb{Q}_p$.
CLT for quadratic additive functionals of three-dimensional and four-dimensional voter models

In this paper, we prove central limit theorems for the quadratic additive functionals of the three-dimensional and four-dimensional voter models. Our main results show that, under proper time-space scalings, the centered quadratic additive functional of the four-dimensional voter model converges weakly to a Brownian motion and that in the three-dimensional case converges weakly to a Gaussian process without independent increment. The proof of the main result in the four-dimensional case extends the martingale decomposition method. In the three-dimensional case, we introduce a quadratic fluctuation limit theorem which shows that the quadratic fluctuation density field of the voter model converges weakly to a generalized Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Then our main result in the three-dimensional case follows from an argument where the quadratic additive functional is approximated by an integral of a test function with respect to the quadratic fluctuation density field. The duality relationship between the voter model and the coalescing random walk is repeatedly utilized in proofs of the main results. The proof strategies introduced in this paper are applicable in deducing CLTs for general additive functionals of three-dimensional and four dimensional voter models. We only deal with those with the quadratic forms to make our exposition easy to catch.
Square-root logarithmic bounds for the arithmetic complexity of factorial multiples

Assume that the Riemann zeta function has no zeros in $\Re(s)>1-δ$, $s\neq1$, for some fixed $0<δ\leq1/2$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, a positive multiple $m_k k!$ has arithmetic complexity $τ(m_k k!)\leq\exp(C\sqrt{\log k\log\log k})$, where $C$ depends only on $δ$. We first establish a smooth-number asymptotic at every sufficiently large center $x$ in intervals of length at least $x^{3/4}$. Combining this estimate with an established genus-two construction yields the arithmetic bound without Cheng's conjecture on smooth numbers in elliptic Hasse intervals. The bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.

A graph $G$ is degree-truncated DP-$k$-colourable (respectively, degree-truncated $k$-choosable) if it is DP-$f$-colourable (respectively, $f$-choosable), where $f(v)=\min\{k,d_G(v)\}$ for every vertex $v$. Hutchinson proved that every $2$-connected maximal outerplanar graph other than the triangle is degree-truncated $5$-choosable. Lo, Wang, Zhou and Zhu strengthened this result by proving that every $2$-connected $K_{2,4}$-minor-free graph other than cycles and complete graphs is degree-truncated DP-$5$-colourable. Outerplanar graphs are precisely the $\{K_4,K_{2,3}\}$-minor-free graphs. We study how the truncation threshold grows when $K_{2,3}$ is replaced by $K_{2,t}$, while $K_4$-minor remains excluded. A bound independent of $t$ is impossible, as shown by the family $\{K_{2,n}| n\ge 2\}$. Let $\mathcal S_t$ be the class of $2$-connected $\{K_4,K_{2,t}\}$-minor-free graphs other than cycles. Writing $χ^{\text{\sout{d}}}_{\mathrm{DP}}(\mathcal S_t)$ for the least truncation threshold valid throughout this class, we prove that, for every integer $t\ge3$, \[ \left\lfloor2\sqrt{2t}\right\rfloor \le χ^{\text{\sout{d}}}_{\mathrm{DP}}(\mathcal S_t) \le \left\lceil4\sqrt{2t}\right\rceil. \]
Wasserstein approximation of measures via orthogonal frames: statistical and computational complexities
Mateo Díaz; Nicolás García Trillos; Daniel López-Castaño; Congwei Yang

Dimension-reduction methods such as PCA identify a subspace capturing most of the variation in the data, but not a distinguished basis within it. Selecting a basis in which the samples are sparsely represented is a recurring task in unsupervised learning, addressed by methods in factor analysis, dictionary learning, and subspace clustering. We pose this task as Wasserstein approximation of the data distribution by measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame, which, in turn, reduces to a nonsmooth optimization problem over the orthogonal group $\mathrm{O}(d)$. We show that, under mild assumptions, both empirical risk minimizers and a locally initialized stochastic gradient method recover the population-optimal frame at the near-parametric rate $\widetilde{O}_d(n^{-1/2})$, where $n$ is the sample size. The main difficulty is that, although the population objective is smooth, the empirical objective is not-this mismatch precludes standard covering arguments. We overcome this issue by replacing Lipschitz continuity of the empirical gradient with a coarsely Lipschitz bound, a tool that may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments support our theoretical findings.
Energy equality and renormalization of Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations

We study weak solutions of the incompressible and the compressible Navier--Stokes--Vlasov systems on a bounded domain, where a viscous fluid is coupled to a dispersed particle phase through a drag force; the fluid obeys the no-slip boundary condition and the particles are subject to specular reflection. For solutions with Besov regularity, we show that the Vlasov equation is renormalizable in the sense of DiPerna--Lions, and we give regularity thresholds for the validity of the global energy equality. If the distribution function $f$ belongs to $B_p^{α,\infty}$ in space and velocity with time integrability $p$, and the fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to $B_q^{β,\infty}$ jointly in space and time with integrability $q$, then the energy equality holds provided $α+β>1$ and $β$ exceeds an explicit bound depending on $p$, $q$ and the dimension, under a natural integrability assumption on the pressure; an analogous criterion holds for the compressible system when the density is bounded from above and below. The condition $αp>1$ imposed on $f$ is not merely technical: it is exactly the range in which the macroscopic momentum flux possesses a boundary trace, so that the specular reflection condition passes to the macroscopic energy balance. When the particle phase is absent, our thresholds coincide with the criteria $β>\frac12+\frac1q$ and $β>\frac3q$ obtained by Yu for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations alone. The proofs combine a boundary cutoff argument with commutator estimates based on a scale-localized Besov modulus, together with a boundary-strip analysis.
Helly theorems for lattice of flats of a matroid

A basis of a matroid is adapted to a flat if it contains a basis of the flat. We prove that a family of flats in a rank r matroid has a common adapted basis whenever every subfamily of at most r+1 flats does. The ground set and the family may be infinite; only the rank must be finite. This result, in particular, contains Klyachko's vector space Helly theorem for subspaces. As an application, we obtain a splitting criterion for tropical toric vector bundles on projective spaces. As a secondary application, we derive quadratic bounds for the Helly number for distributive generation in the lattice of flats.
Equivalence between rationality and modular invariance under $C_2$-cofiniteness

We prove that for a simple and $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, the rationality is equivalent to the modular invariance of the space of complete ordinary one-point trace functions of its irreducible modules. This proves a conjecture given by Dong-Ren in \cite{DongRen}, which is also the inverse theorem of Zhu's modular invariance theorem \cite{Zhu}.
